behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype records and dense ordinary arrays; reject classes, accessors, symbols, extra keys, holes and coercion. All numbers finite binary64, integer fields safe. Validate every field and correspondence in schema order, then work preflight before arithmetic/output allocation. columns*rows must be safe <=4294967295 and each field array must have that length. No mutation, retained aliases or partial output; canonicalize output zero. Host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, renderer, assets or host state. Row-major periodic rectangular domain, cell spacing1, x right and y down. Scalar centers(x,y), u right face(x+.5,y), v lower face(x,y+.5). Velocity in cell units per caller time. Other targets deferred; no original artist recreation claim.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separate ordered primitives, every arithmetic intermediate checked finite (NUMERIC_OVERFLOW), no FMA/reassociation or epsilon. Exact analytical JSON fixtures; additional analytical comparisons abs1e-9+rel1e-12, topology/indices/errors exact. Modulo indices wrap positively. No convergence or mass conservation inferred from an image.
behavior.work: N cell events precharged; O(N) time/storage.
behavior.algorithm: For each row-major cell from immutable old values: centerWeight=1-4*rate; sum=centerWeight*center; then add rate*left, rate*right, rate*up, rate*down in order; result=retention*sum. Repeated neighbors on one-cell axes are counted repeatedly. rate=diffusivity*dt/cellWidth^2 in[0,.25] ensures nonnegative stencil weights; retention is a per-call factor, not a continuous-time rate. No implicit clamp, normalization or source. rate=.25 may preserve an alternating checkerboard, so stability does not mean strict smoothing. Under retention1 the stencil conserves total mass up to stated arithmetic; no material/pigment model claimed.

errors.WORK_LIMIT: Exact declared work reservation exceeds maxWork.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite checked arithmetic; no partial result.
errors.INVALID_GROWTH: Finite grown rest length is not positive.
errors.OUTPUT_LIMIT: Required live refinement exceeds supplied node/edge caps.
errors.ID_EXHAUSTED: A new ID/counter would exceed the safe integer domain.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Closest point or refinement rounding loses required nonzero geometry/material.
errors.STEP_BLOCKED: Every allowed candidate has forbidden contact/overlap.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype records, dense ordinary arrays with own data slots, no classes/accessors/symbols/extras/coercion; proxies outside interchange. Numeric values finite binary64; booleans never numbers. Validate complete input in input-schema field order, arrays in order, then correspondence/topology structure, then exact-integer work preflight before geometric predicates or result allocation. Normalize accepted/exposed zero to +0. Inputs unchanged and all outputs deeply detached. Host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, renderer or assets. Caller Cartesian coordinates; signed turns use algebraic counterclockwise orientation in x/y coordinates, visually clockwise when y points down. Explicit caller dt where present. p5-only initial delivery; no physical collision, source solver or other-target equivalence.
behavior.numerics: Binary64 separately rounded primitives, no FMA or reassociation. Check each computed floating arithmetic primitive finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. Exact dyadic/rational predicates use existing internal/exact-rational.js without converting before classification. Existing fdlibmHypot and fdlibmAtan2 profiles for stated norms/angles. Compare IDs, topology, ordering, counters and errors exactly; analytical floating fixtures may explicitly allow absolute1e-12 relative0. No global epsilon.
behavior.topology: Nodes/curves sorted unique stable IDs. Each node belongs to exactly one curve. Open curve has n>=2 unique nodeIds,n-1 edgeIds/restLengths,n-2 restTurns in traversal-center order. Closed curve has n>=3 unique nodes, n edgeIds/restLengths/restTurns, with implicit closing edge and turns centered on each traversal node. Edge IDs globally unique. next counters exceed all current node/edge IDs. maxNodes>=N,maxEdges>=E or INVALID_INPUT. Nonexistent/repeated ownership/connectivity/ID errors are INVALID_TOPOLOGY. restGrowth has one curve-ordered array per curve with one rate per edge; turnRates matches restTurns; externalAccelerations matches globally ID-sorted nodes. Complete all before budgets.
behavior.work: Let N=state.nodes.length,E=sum(curve.edgeIds.length),B=sum(curve.restTurns.length),S=min(maxNodes-N,maxEdges-E). Reserve exact W=8*N+8*E+4*B+(maxBacktracks+3)*E*E+maxEdges*maxEdges+8*S. Reject W>maxWork or any unrepresentable requested work as WORK_LIMIT before geometry. S is the maximum possible successful binary split count under output caps; no undefined actual output count enters preflight. Reservation includes old geometry, contact, every allowed candidate barrier and final refined geometry using maxEdges^2. No refund for early success. Exact rational bit costs/sorting are not events; O(N+E+S) retained storage with streaming contacts, quadratic predicate work per candidate.
behavior.embedding: After preflight validate original nonzero finite edges with exact dyadic predicates. Nonincident edges may not intersect/touch. Incident edges may share only their designated endpoint and may not overlap/backtrack collinearly. Reject INVALID_GEOMETRY. During candidate tests the same conditions determine pass/retry. Final returned states are embedded centerlines only; no continuous/swept collision, isotopy, hard-width clearance or fabrication guarantee. contactRange is a force radius, not a proved clearance.
behavior.targets: Process grown rest lengths in ascending stable edge ID: delta=dt*rate then Lnew=Lold+delta, each finite; nonpositive finite result is INVALID_GROWTH. Update preferred turns by ascending curve ID then traversal center: delta=dt*rate,value=oldTurn+delta, then r=value%TAU; if r<=-PI,r=r+TAU; if r>PI,r=r-TAU. PI=3.141592653589793,TAU=2*PI separately computed; all primitives finite. Output principal(-PI,PI]. These new targets are used in this call, but committed only after full success.
behavior.stretch: Initialize force arrays from externalAccelerations. Visit edges in stable ID order with orientation determined by curve traversal. dx=xb-xa,dy=yb-ya,L=fdlibmHypot(dx,dy),ux=dx/L,uy=dy/L,extension=L-grownRest,m=stretchStiffness*extension,fx=m*ux,fy=m*uy. Every primitive finite; L0 cannot reach this stage from valid geometry. Add Fa.x+=fx,Fa.y+=fy,Fb.x-=fx,Fb.y-=fy, separately checked.
behavior.bend: Visit curve IDs ascending, then interior/cyclic centers in traversal order. At a,b,c compute incoming dx,dy,La=norm,unit ux,uy, then outgoing dx,dy,Lc=norm,unit vx,vy. cross=ux*vy-uy*vx and dot=ux*vx+uy*vy, checking products before sum. theta=fdlibmAtan2(cross,dot). delta=principal(theta-grownTarget) using the targets reduction rule. q=bendStiffness*delta,qa=q/La,qc=q/Lc; Fa.x=qa*uy,Fa.y=-(qa*ux),Fc.x=qc*vy,Fc.y=-(qc*vx),Fb.x=-(Fa.x+Fc.x),Fb.y=-(Fa.y+Fc.y). Accumulate a.x,a.y,b.x,b.y,c.x,c.y. Check every primitive. Exact antiparallel turn chooses principal positivePI, including signed-zero cases. No degree normalization or random kick.
behavior.contact: Visit unordered nonincident edge pairs lexicographically by edge IDs; incident means sharing any node ID. First edge A->B,second C->D retain curve orientation. Exact closest-point candidates are intersections plus each endpoint projected/clamped to the other closed segment; evaluate exact squared distance, choose least distance then least exact first t then second s. Exact parallel ties obey the same rule. Compare exact distanceSquared with exact contactRange^2. If not strictly smaller or range0, contribute nothing. Valid original geometry excludes zero distance. Round exact separation vector firstClosest-secondClosest and t,s once to binary64. If positive exact distance produces zero rounded norm, fail REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE. D=fdlibmHypot(dx,dy), finite and positive; ratio=D/contactRange,rawFalloff=1-ratio,falloff=max(0,rawFalloff),strength=contactStrength*falloff,ux=dx/D,uy=dy/D,fx=strength*ux,fy=strength*uy. Check ratio and subtraction finite before max. Root freeze: if exact distance is inside but rounded D>=contactRange, contribute zero; the clamped nonnegative falloff never turns repulsion into attraction. wa=1-t,wb=t,wc=1-s,wd=s. Add weighted force to A.x,A.y,B.x,B.y; subtract weighted force from C.x,C.y,D.x,D.y, product then sum at each slot. Every primitive checked finite. Pins still contribute/react in force computation.
behavior.integrate: Visit node IDs ascending. For x then y: impulse=dt*force,kicked=oldVelocity+impulse,v=kicked*damping. Compute speed=fdlibmHypot(vx,vy); if speed>maxSpeed,scale=maxSpeed/speed then vx*=scale,vy*=scale. Check each primitive even when pinned or a coefficient0; then pinned proposed velocity is[0,0]. No position updates have yet been committed.
behavior.barrier: Try alpha1 and at most maxBacktracks halvings, alpha=alpha*.5 each retry. Candidate velocity=alpha*proposedVelocity x then y, travel=dt*velocity,point=oldPoint+travel, in node/axis order. Pins retain exact old point and zero velocity. If alpha becomes0, STEP_STALLED. If any proposed unpinned travel is nonzero but every candidate point equals the old point, STEP_STALLED before geometry (actual zero travel succeeds). If candidate embedding passes, retain its points and scaled velocities; otherwise retry from old points. After last invalid candidate STEP_BLOCKED. Grown targets are not scaled by alpha; acceptedMotionScale reports the movement reduction. No output on any failure.
behavior.refine: After accepted movement, visit pre-refinement edges ascending ID. Recursively bisect an edge while either its current geometric fdlibm length or grown rest length exceeds maxSegmentLength; visit left child subtree before right. Each split requires one live node and one net live edge; exceeding maxNodes/maxEdges yields OUTPUT_LIMIT atomically. Allocate one node ID then two edge IDs monotonically; prospective counters must stay safe or ID_EXHAUSTED. Parent edge retires. Position and velocity midpoint are exact rational averages rounded once; midpoint equal to either endpoint fails REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE. Child rest length is the exact parent half; require exactly representable positive binary64 half, else REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE (including odd subnormal parents). New node is unpinned. Insert zero preferred turn at new material vertex; keep old preferred turns at old vertex IDs. Update curve traversal node/edge lists, preserve closed seam, sort global node records byID. Emit preorder {parentEdgeId,nodeId,childEdgeIds,parentT:.5}. New nodes take part only next call. Revalidate final refined embedded geometry; invalidity due rounding is REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE. Return all state/lineage detached; no retained event history. Rest total and total preferred turn preserved under splitting; mass/energy/resolution-independent stiffness are not promised.

behavior.validation: Exactly the input and nested-union keys shown by the schema, ordinary dense arrays and passive own data properties. behavior.numerics: Separate binary64 primitive rounding, no reassociation/FMA. Every computed primitive must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, including division by an underflowed zero denominator. behavior.grid: For grid operations C=columns,R=rows,G=C*R, flattened row-major index y*C+x. Scalar/vector/binary state arrays have exactly G elements; vector pairs use caller X/Y axes. behavior.algorithm:
Elementary cellular rows

Proposed ID: `field.elementary-cellular-rows`; generator.

Artist output: a space-time grid from a one-dimensional three-cell rule. Studies:
space-time tapestries; radial rule bands where rows are drawn as successive rings.
Unlike candidate13, the rule distinguishes ordered left/center/right configurations.

Input:

```text
{initial:[0|1,...], rule:integer in 0..255, rows:integer>=1,
 boundary:"ZERO"|"WRAP", maxWork:integer}
```

Initial length C>=1; output length C*rows must fit the shared representation limit.
Output `{columns:C,rows:rows,cells:[0|1,...]}`. Row0 copies initial. For later rows,
read only the previous row and set `pattern=4*left+2*center+right`,
`next=(rule >>> pattern)&1`. ZERO supplies0 outside the row; WRAP uses nonnegative
modulo, including duplicated neighbors for C=1/2. No random initial row is generated.
Reserve `W=C+4*C*(rows-1)`; O(C*rows) work/output and O(C) extra state at most.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, rendering, assets, host state, mutation or retained aliases. Data uses caller coordinate/color conventions as specified.
behavior.numerics: Grid/feature indices and envelope squared distances use exact integer arithmetic. Only returned distances convert exact squared values to binary64 then use Math.sqrt. General distances compare with absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; indices/null/order exactly. Analytical fixture square roots are the specified correctly rounded binary64 profile. No Infinity or BigInt is returned.
behavior.algorithm: Input boolean mask has columns*rows entries. True cells are features. Return Euclidean pixel-center distances and nearest original row-major feature indices; equal squared distance chooses the smallest feature index. If no feature, both arrays contain null. Compute separably in O(G) envelope events, not all-pairs searches. First compute nearest feature column within each row by forward/backward scans; ties use lower column. Retain exact integer squared horizontal distances and feature indices; rows without features have null. Then each column solves the lower envelope of parabolas f[q]+(y-q)^2 for rows q with nonnull row results. Process q ascending. For a newer q and retained older v, the first integer y at which q is strictly better is floorDiv((f[q]+q*q)-(f[v]+v*v),2*(q-v))+1. Use exact signed integer floor division (toward negative infinity), exact integer squares and sums; JavaScript BigInt is the native profile. Maintain candidate rows and increasing integer start positions: the first starts at0; if a new switch is <= the last start, pop and recompute; if empty, new start0. A switch >=rows means the new candidate can be discarded for this finite grid. Otherwise append at its switch. Query y ascending, advancing when y>=next start. Earlier rows win equal squared distance, and their horizontal ties already choose lower columns, giving global smallest feature ID. Output distance is Math.sqrt(Number(exactSquaredDistance)), correctly rounding the integer to binary64 before square root. Internal exact integers are not exposed in JSON. This preserves nearest-feature identities even where coordinate squares exceed binary64 exact-integer range.
behavior.budget: Preflight 6*G <= maxWork safely before output allocation. This is an explicit grid-entry work allowance; the row scans and amortized envelope events are O(G), with O(G) retained arrays and O(max(columns,rows)) scratch. Exact integer arithmetic is on values bounded by the array/dimension representation limit; no arbitrary user-sized integers enter the API.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static carrier/domain/correspondence failure before work.

behavior.validation: Passive Object/null-prototype record with exactly points,samples,mode,bias,gain,maxWork. No accessors/classes/symbols/extras/coercion; proxies outside interchange. Dense ordinary arrays with own data slots and no extras. Validate outer record; points shape and all finite pairs in order (length0..2147483647); samples shape, equal length and all finite pairs; mode; bias finite pair; gain finite pair; maxWork nonnegative safe integer. Canonicalize all accepted zeros. Complete static validation even for empty/identity/budget failure.
behavior.work: After full static validation require N<=maxWork or WORK_LIMIT before arithmetic/output allocation. One event per point including all-zero gain. Empty input returns empty detached arrays. Validation O(N), output O(N), auxiliary algorithm state O(1). Host exhaustion is a host error; no partial result.
behavior.algorithm: Visit input index ascending. For channel0 then1 compute product=gain[c]*samples[i][c], then mapped=bias[c]+product, checking finiteness after each primitive. CARTESIAN sets dx=mapped0,dy=mapped1. POLAR computes cos=fdlibmCos(mapped0), sin=fdlibmSin(mapped0), then dx=cos*mapped1,dy=sin*mapped1, checking finiteness. Negative signed distance is allowed and reverses the offset. Canonicalize completed dx,dy zeros to positive zero before storing offsets and adding them. Compute outputX=points[i][0]+dx then outputY=points[i][1]+dy, each finite; canonicalize zero output components. Return points and offsets as separate mutable dense value arrays with fresh pairs even for repeated/duplicate/empty input. No clamping, normalization, angle wrapping, skipping or source-coordinate feedback.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separately rounded primitive order, no FMA/reassociation or binary32 narrowing. Polar trig uses the existing independently audited fdlibm profile in packages/javascript/src/fdlibm-trig.js; no host Math.sin/cos substitution. No epsilon in computation; fixture floating values have absolute tolerance1e-12, relative tolerance0, while lengths/errors/order compare exactly. Finite intermediate checks precede downstream cancellation; no overflow recovery.
behavior.native_surface: p5 exports fieldDisplace2D(input) and FieldDisplace2DError from field-displace-2d.js and index. Plain values only; other targets deferred.
behavior.environment: Already-sampled paired values are explicit input, not callbacks or host noise. Operation consumes no RNG, clock, field queries or renderer. Caller samples before the call and owns sampling failure/state.
behavior.adapter: Native p5 Canvas2D draws retained polyline vertices in returned order; endpoints and repeated points preserved. Polylines can be separate calls or flattened with caller-retained boundaries. This is coordinate geometry, never source-pixel remapping.

guide.title: Displace sampled points
guide.summary: Bend a grid or wobble a contour while keeping its points available for different drawing styles.
guide.useWhen: Use it when a retained 2D point set should bend through an already sampled field while preserving point order.

inputs.samples: One ordered finite [a,b] sample pair per point.
inputs.mode: CARTESIAN interprets pairs as x/y changes; POLAR as angle in radians and signed distance.
inputs.bias: Two base values: x/y changes or angle/distance, according to mode.
inputs.gain: Two sample multipliers; increase these to amplify coordinate changes or angle/distance variation.

guide.output: {points,offsets}
guide.tryThis: Switch to POLAR or change one gain while keeping the supplied points in order.
pitfalls: Samples are explicit input; the operation does not evaluate noise or own a field generator.
The returned points and offsets are detached and have one entry per input point.
Renderer drawing, path styling, and spatial sampling remain outside the operation.

operations.description: Compute separately weighted cohesion, alignment and separation steering over supplied neighbor pairs.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: carrier, finite/domain, correspondence or canonical pair failure
errors.WORK_LIMIT: N+P exceeds maxWork
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: nonfinite subtraction, norm, divide, accumulation, term or cap primitive

behavior.validation: Exact passive plain/null-prototype records, dense arrays with own data slots, finite point/velocity/coefficient values, nonnegative cohesion/alignment/separation/maxSteer and safe maxWork. Full validation precedes work. Each array length<=4294967295; columns*rows must be a safe integer<=4294967295 with exact value-array correspondence. Full numeric validation before work; no aliases/mutation/partial output. Exposed zeros canonical positive. Proxies outside interchange.
behavior.law: For each agent: cohesion*(mean neighbor position-own position) plus alignment*(mean neighbor velocity-own velocity) plus separation*mean over noncoincident normalized outward vectors. Position/velocity means use total degree; separation mean uses noncoincident degree only. Zero degree returns positive zero; coincident neighbors contribute alignment/cohesion but no invented separation direction. Cap raw steering by fdlibmHypot and maxSteer. Zero coefficients do not skip arithmetic. Any intermediate sum, difference or norm that overflows fails, even if a real-number mean, zero-weight result, or capped vector would be finite.
behavior.order: After N+P work approval, visit canonical pairs. For each [i,j], accumulate j position x,y then velocity x,y and degree into i; accumulate i values in the same x/y order into j; calculate dx then dy then fdlibm length; for nonzero length add normalized outward x,y/noncoincident degree to i then negated x,y/count to j. Visit agents ascending; calculate cohesion x,y, alignment x,y, separation x,y, raw x/y, then cap scale/x/y. Canonical order fixes observable binary64 accumulation.
behavior.work: Charge N+P after static validation and before output allocation. Time/storage O(N+P).
behavior.environment: No neighbor query, integration, speed cap, field, boundary, clock, RNG, renderer or species policy.
behavior.numerics: Ordered separate binary64 primitives; finite-check every computed primitive. fdlibm sin/cos/hypot existing audited implementations. Exact shared fixture outputs; independent trigonometric analytical oracles abs1e-12 relative0, indices/errors/counters exact. No epsilon in classification.
behavior.native_surface: flockSteer2D(input); p5-only initial target, named package export; errors carry stable code.

guide.title: Steer a supplied flock graph
guide.summary: Combine neighbor position, velocity and separation into editable steering vectors.
guide.useWhen: Choose the neighbor graph independently, then integrate returned steering in your motion model.

inputs.points: Supplied finite [x,y] positions in canvas or chosen world units.
inputs.pairs: Unique [i,j] indices with i<j, in strict lexicographic order; the caller chooses the graph.
inputs.cohesion: Weight of the vector toward mean neighbor position.
inputs.alignment: Weight of the difference from mean neighbor velocity.
inputs.separation: Weight of the mean unit vector away from noncoincident neighbors.
inputs.maxSteer: Nonnegative cap on each final steering-vector length.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit computation budget. See the operation contract for its event formula; this is not a millisecond limit.

guide.output: {steering}: one detached vector per original point; this does not integrate positions.
guide.code:
const result = flockSteer2D({"points":[[0,0],[2,0]],"velocities":[[0,0],[4,2]],"pairs":[[0,1]],"cohesion":0,"alignment":0.5,"separation":0,"maxSteer":100,"maxWork":3});
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Swap proximity pairs for a fixed chain, then change alignment while preserving the graph.
pitfalls: Coincident neighbors contribute no invented separation direction.
No neighbor search, walls or collision resolution is implicit.

operations.description: Draft proposal only.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed shape/domain/nonfinite input.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Budget exceeded or unsafe work arithmetic.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite computed intermediate.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. Complete static shape/value validation precedes work preflight. Geometric/topology tests run after preflight. Failure throws Error with stable code, no partial result. Outputs are detached. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0. Array lengths must fit 4294967295; unsafe requested growth/work arithmetic gives WORK_LIMIT before allocation. Host resource exhaustion is a host error, not an allocation guarantee. All grid/kernel/element dimensions are positive integers; each corresponding array length/product must fit 4294967295 and match exactly, otherwise INVALID_INPUT before work.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, rendering, assets, host state, mutation or retained aliases. Data uses caller coordinate/color conventions as specified.
behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. Check computed numeric intermediates for finiteness and throw NUMERIC_OVERFLOW on nonfinite results. No epsilon in classification or topology, no adaptive exact predicates or near-degeneracy guarantee. General scalar/coordinate comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; topology, indices, order, booleans and RNG states compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exact JSON output.
behavior.algorithm:
Artist task: convert continuous monochrome fields to directional print texture, removing scan-order error
diffusion; ordered screening has no propagated residue. Input {values,columns,rows,threshold,maxWork}:
values length=columns*rows, values/threshold in [0,1]. Output {bits}, one 0/1 per source. Copy values,
scan rows then columns, emit current>=threshold, error=current-emitted; diffuse in-bounds
right/down-left/down/down-right by 7/16,3/16,5/16,1/16. No clamp. Work=cells plus one per actual neighbor
write, charged before writes. Fixtures: 1x1 [.5] at .5 -> [1]; 2x2 all .4 -> [0,1,0,0].
Studies: etched radial moon; contour-fog ink.
behavior.budget: Charge cells, then one unit before every in-bounds diffusion write; no output allocation before known base work fits.

const result = floydSteinbergDither({ values:[.4,.6], columns:2, rows:1, threshold:.5, maxWork:3 });

operations.description: An immutable seeded single-octave 2D gradient field with pure binary64 samples in [0,1]. Independently specified; not Processing noise compatibility.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong constructor shape, unknown/missing key, bool/nonfinite/noninteger seed, or seed outside unsigned32.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Query not exactly two finite numbers, or either floor(q) or floor(q)+1 outside safe integer range.

behavior.construction: Validate exactly one seed key and mathematical integral value 0..4294967295. Integral floating values allowed, booleans rejected. Detach input; store immutable seed, normalize zero to +0. Serialize only {seed}; no derived table, cache or query history.
behavior.query_validation: Interchange query is exactly [x,y]. Validate shape then x then y. Both finite binary64 values must satisfy -9007199254740991 <= q < 9007199254740991, so floor(q) and floor(q)+1 are exact safe integers. Return no partial output on error. Native hot path sample(x,y) takes scalars and does not allocate a query tuple. The same native sample method may accept one coordinate tuple for interchange or two scalar arguments for the hot path. Invalid tuple shape is INVALID_QUERY. Unsupported native call arity is a host-language call error and is not an interchange-data result.
behavior.cells: I=floor(x), J=floor(y), retained as exact integers for corner arithmetic. u=x-floor(x), v=y-floor(y) each separately rounded binary64 subtraction. Tiny negative inputs may produce u or v equal to 1 by rounding; do not correct/reject. For hashing only, reduce each I+di,J+dj modulo 2^32. Do not cast a binary64 floor directly to signed int32; Java may convert to long then take low32 bits.
behavior.mix32: For unsigned32 v, in order: v=v XOR (v logical-right-shift 16); v=(v*0x7feb352d) modulo 2^32; v=v XOR (v logical-right-shift 15); v=(v*0x846ca68b) modulo 2^32; return v XOR (v logical-right-shift 16). Every integer multiply and XOR retains exactly 32 bits.
behavior.corner_hash: For integer corner (i,j): a=mix32(seed XOR u32(i) XOR 0x9e3779b9); h=mix32(a XOR u32(j) XOR 0x85ebca6b). Gradient index=h AND 7. u32 is mathematical modulo 2^32.
behavior.dot: gx*dx rounded to px; gy*dy rounded to py; px+py rounded to result. No gradient normalization. Corner order n00,n10,n01,n11 with offsets (u,v),(u-1,v),(u,v-1),(u-1,v-1); every offset subtraction separately rounded.
behavior.fade: F(t), consecutive binary64 steps: a=t*t; b=a*t; c=6*t; d=c-15; e=t*d; f=e+10; return b*f. No polynomial expansion, reassociation or FMA.
behavior.interpolation: L(a,b,t), consecutive binary64 steps: d=b-a; p=t*d; return a+p. Compute fx=F(u),fy=F(v); bottom=L(n00,n10,fx); top=L(n01,n11,fx); raw=L(bottom,top,fy); scaled=0.5*raw; result=0.5+scaled. Clamp only final result to [0,1], normalize zero to +0.
behavior.numerics: Every stated floating operation is IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even, separately rounded; no FMA or reassociation. Scalars compare exactly after canonical positive zero. No transcendental functions. Raw ideal bound [-1,1]; output closed interval [0,1], both endpoints possible; lattice samples exactly 0.5.
behavior.state: Pure immutable field. No RNG stream, table shuffle, host noise, time, assets, renderer, or externally mutable state. Queries may be repeated/reordered and distinct fields interleaved without changing results. Seed changes field identity; no statistical independence or cryptographic guarantee.
behavior.periodicity: Each lattice axis repeats at 2^32. Sample equality under a shifted coordinate requires that shift and fractional part be exactly representable and both queries in domain. Large coordinates lose subcell resolution; no epsilon correction. No configurable seamless tiling API.
behavior.cost: O(1) storage and query work: four corner hashes, at most eight mix32 evaluations (pure common-subexpression reuse is permitted), four dot products, fixed fades/lerps. Native sample(x,y) avoids query-array allocation. No eager full-grid sampling or hidden unbounded cache.
behavior.native_representations: Passive interchange data only, not active callbacks/accessors/proxies. Java accepts boxed Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double or native double scalars; unsupported Number subclasses are rejected before lossy coercion. Python accepts int/float but never bool; coordinates convert to binary64 before domain validation. JavaScript requires number scalars. Preserve seed integer semantics before conversion; constructor/serialization field names remain seed.

guide.title: Sample a seeded 2D field
guide.summary: Create a pure gradient-noise sampler with values from zero to one.
guide.useWhen: Use it to steer angles, lengths, or color phases.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295 that selects a repeatable 2D field. Construct once, then call sample(x, y) at many coordinates. Changing the seed changes the field; sampling does not advance random state.

guide.output: `sample(x, y)` returns a number from 0 to 1 at your field coordinates. It does not create points or draw marks. `serialize()` returns `{seed}` so you can recreate the same field.
guide.code:
const field = gradientNoise2D01({ seed: 42 });
console.log(field.sample(1.25, 3.5));
guide.tryThis: For a full-turn heading, use `field.sample(x * 0.01, y * 0.01) * Math.PI * 2`. The 0.01 is your chosen drawing-to-field scale, not a required default.

operations.description: Immutable seeded single-octave three-coordinate gradient field with pure binary64 samples in[0,1]; independent of Processing noise.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong constructor shape, unknown/missing key, bool/nonfinite/noninteger seed, or seed outside unsigned32.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Query not exactly three finite supported numbers, or a coordinate outside the safe-corner domain.

behavior.identity: Required uint32 seed, immutable detached serialization; pure x/y/z queries with no global state or sample consumption.
behavior.numerics: Exact binary64 safe-corner subtraction, three-stage lowbias32 corner hash, twelve integer gradients, quintic fades and x-then-y-then-z interpolation; clamp output0..1. See normative document for exact order.
behavior.native: GradientNoise3D01.create(Object) or create(long); serialize; sample(Object tuple), sample(Object,Object,Object), sample(double,double,double); only six standard boxed numeric carriers.
behavior.complexity: O(1) storage and eight-corner work per sample; scalar hot path allocation-free.

guide.title: Sample a seeded 3D field
guide.summary: Create a pure three-dimensional gradient-noise sampler.
guide.useWhen: Use it when a third coordinate represents depth, frame, or another explicit axis.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295 that selects a repeatable 3D field. Construct once, then call sample(x, y, z). You supply z explicitly, so it can represent depth or an animation coordinate.

guide.output: `sample(x, y, z)` returns a number from 0 to 1. Use it as a color phase, displacement or heading input. Repeated sampling at the same coordinates gives the same value; `serialize()` returns `{seed}`.
guide.code:
const field = gradientNoise3D01({ seed: 42 });
console.log(field.sample(1.25, 3.5, 0.5));
guide.tryThis: Advance z by an explicit amount per frame for an evolving field. Keep the seed and frame-to-z mapping to reproduce the animation later.

operations.description: Retain a finite two-dimensional trajectory by sampling an explicit gradient field at each evolving position and advancing a fixed distance. Reuse its positions and headings for different marks.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including layout-unsafe steps.
errors.TRACE_QUERY_INVALID: Dynamic field coordinate invalid; stepIndex and query_x/query_y stage.
errors.TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite heading/displacement/endpoint; stepIndex and stated stage.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index exceeds point or heading range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto storage/offset is not writable binary64 space for two values.

behavior.input: Interchange input is exactly the eight required keys. Passive JSON-compatible records only. Validate outer shape/keys, field shape/seed, start shape and x/y values, steps, stepDistance, fieldScale, fieldOffset shape and x/y values, angleBase, angleScale in that order. Every numeric value must be finite; booleans are never numbers. Integral floating counts/seeds are allowed. Steps must be0..1073741822 inclusive and stepDistance>=0. Copy configuration, canonicalizing every zero to positive zero.
behavior.construction: An explicit eager trace call authorizes O(steps) work and retained allocation. Configuration validation never samples or allocates output-sized storage. Complete all static validation before array allocation or field sampling. Reconstruct the existing GradientNoise2D01 from detached seed configuration. The first public form takes the complete interchange configuration; no arbitrary field callback or second field carrier is accepted.
behavior.layout: N=steps. Privately retain2*(N+1) binary64 position coordinates and N binary64 headings. Positions[0] is start; heading[i] drives the movement positions[i]→positions[i+1]. Count bound N<=1073741822 ensures2*(N+1)<=2147483647. This is a shared index representation bound, not a promise that maximal allocation succeeds. No extra maxSteps/maxBytes input. Incidental host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never INVALID_INPUT or partial successful output.
behavior.advance: For i=0..N-1: qx=round64(x*fieldScale), then qx=round64(qx+fieldOffset.x); validate qx in the field query domain before computing qy the same way. Sample field(qx,qy). mapped=round64(angleScale*sample); heading=round64(angleBase+mapped), then canonicalize a zero heading to positive zero. dx=round64(stepDistance*hostCos(heading)); dy=round64(stepDistance*hostSin(heading)). nextX=round64(x+dx); nextY=round64(y+dy). Canonicalize completed zero coordinates to positive zero, store point[i+1] and heading[i], and feed those stored coordinates into the next iteration. No FMA, reassociation, angle reduction, clamping, closure or binary32 conversion.
behavior.dynamic_validation: Per step, validate finite multiply and sum for query_x and its existing noise domain -9007199254740991<=qx<9007199254740991, then query_y similarly. Query failures use TRACE_QUERY_INVALID with zero-based stepIndex and stage query_x/query_y. After sampling check mapped and heading finite (stage heading), then cosine and dx finite (delta_x), sine and dy finite (delta_y), then nextX finite (position_x), nextY finite (position_y). These use TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with stepIndex/stage. Discard internal partial arrays and return no path. Final endpoint is not sampled to validate a hypothetical next step.
behavior.zero: N=0 validates every static input but performs no field query, arithmetic advance or trigonometry; result contains the canonical start and no heading. stepDistance=0 still performs every requested field query and heading calculation and retains repeated positions. angleScale=0 does not skip field validation or sampling. Prefix identity is conditional on both calls succeeding in the same target/runtime.
behavior.ownership: Path owns detached arrays and configuration. No writable field, renderer or external state is retained. pointAt returns a fresh pair; pointInto writes exactly two slots after all validation, never exposing internal arrays. headingAt returns a scalar. serialize returns detached canonical input for recomputation; toValues returns detached complete output_schema values and explicitly authorizes that extra materialization. Replay/getters/export do not sample the field or recompute movement. If serialize/toValues allocation fails, no new value is returned and the original path remains usable and unchanged. Failure does not invalidate or partially mutate the retained path.
behavior.access: Native steps() (Python steps property) is N. pointAt index domain0..N; headingAt0..N-1. Validate index as finite safe nonnegative integer <=9007199254740991 (booleans excluded), then access-specific bound. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. Optional pointInto checks index/domain then bounds then output and offset; offset must be finite nonnegative integral, with two writable binary64 slots. Invalid access leaves output unchanged. Float32 buffers are forbidden. In Java, the transport may use a typed int offset (unrepresentable/wrong-type calls are host call errors); dynamic-language offsets retain the stated runtime validation. This does not change valid pointInto behavior or index/bounds-before-storage error order.
behavior.native_forms: Java GradientPath2D.trace(Object config), pointAt(Object or long), headingAt(Object or long), pointInto(index,double[],offset), steps(), serialize(), toValues(). JavaScript gradientPath2D(config), pointAt, headingAt, pointInto, steps getter, serialize, toValues. Python gradient_path_2d(config), point_at, heading_at, point_into, steps property, serialize, to_values. No overload accepting arbitrary callbacks or host field objects in v0.1.0. Supplying an existing field serialize() value reuses its declared configuration.
behavior.native_types: Follow existing grid numeric conventions: Java Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double only; reject BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive object/Array input with number values; Python int/float but never bool, convert to finite binary64 after validating integer domains where applicable. Python huge integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT/INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception. Output pointInto accepts Java double[], JS Float64Array or writable ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list or array(d). Offset/count/index validation must precede narrowing. Active accessors/proxies and custom containers are not interchange data. Input containers: Java Map for records and exactly two-element List for pairs; arrays/PVector are not pair input carriers. Only passive container behavior belongs to interchange; active custom hooks are outside it. Python requires exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs, rejecting custom Mapping/list subclasses and tuples. JS records have Object.prototype or null prototype and pairs are ordinary Array; class instances/typed-array pairs are not interchange input.
behavior.units: Planar caller-defined x/y coordinates, with heading0 advancing positive x and heading pi/2 positive y. Angles radians; host rendering decides whether positive y points down. FieldScale applies uniformly to both coordinate axes; offsets are lattice units. Step distance is coordinate units. Progress, envelope, perpendicular orientation and before/after anchor are caller choices.
behavior.numerics: Basic arithmetic IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even in stated order. Java/Android Math.sin/cos, JavaScript Math.sin/cos, Python math.sin/cos with no implicit angle normalization. Same-target identical inputs/runtime give exact replay and prefix. Cross-target coordinates/headings are checked under explicit per-case fixture tolerances, never a universal bit-identity or arbitrary-descriptor error-bound promise. Existing field algorithm remains exact for identical queries. Every completed zero output is canonical positive zero.
behavior.complexity: O(N) eager work and O(N) retained numeric storage; O(1) point/heading access and O(N) explicit detached value export. No per-step point object or command list. Source-range2000/16000 path measurements and declared example workloads required separately for each claimed runtime.
behavior.native_errors: Every library exception has code. Dynamic trace exceptions additionally expose stepIndex (Python step_index) and stage; these become error_detail:{stepIndex,stage} in interchange conformance reports. Static/access errors have no dynamic detail. Java may use a dedicated IllegalArgumentException subclass for validation and a dedicated ArithmeticException subclass for dynamic failures; JS Error subclasses and Python ValueError subclasses are native transport, not different semantic codes. Host allocation failure is not wrapped as a success or validation error.

guide.title: Follow a field
guide.summary: Retain a path by sampling a seeded direction field at each step.
guide.useWhen: Use it when marks should inherit motion from a field.

inputs.field: A descriptor `{seed: 42}` for the package’s 2D noise field. This field seed selects the terrain being sampled; pass data rather than a p5 noise function.
inputs.start: The initial `[x, y]` point in drawing units. It is retained as point 0, before any movement.
inputs.steps: Nonnegative integer number of advances. The returned path has steps + 1 positions and steps headings.
inputs.stepDistance: Nonnegative drawing distance for each advance. Larger values separate consecutive points more; zero keeps every point at the start.
inputs.fieldScale: Multiply each drawing coordinate by this value before sampling the field. Larger magnitudes sample a wider span of the field across the same drawing; zero samples one fixed location. Negative values are allowed.
inputs.fieldOffset: A finite `[x, y]` translation applied after fieldScale, in field coordinates. Change it to sample a different part of the same seeded field without moving the path’s starting point.
inputs.angleBase: Heading offset in radians, applied at every step. The heading is angleBase + noiseValue × angleScale; this is not just the initial direction.
inputs.angleScale: Number of radians represented by the field’s 0–1 span. For example, 2π maps that span around a full turn; 0 produces a straight path at angleBase.

guide.output: pointAt(index) reads positions 0 through steps, while headingAt(index) reads headings 0 through steps-1; toValues() returns ordered positions and headings arrays.
guide.tryThis: Use pointAt(index) and headingAt(index) to draw a short perpendicular mark at every retained step.

operations.description: Advance supplied Gray–Scott concentration grids by one explicit simultaneous reaction/diffusion update.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed shape, supplied scalar/carrier/domain, impossible array representation, or operation-specific static constraint.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: The exact required or next charged work exceeds maxWork or safe work representation.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: A computed floating primitive is nonfinite; no partial state or geometry escapes.

behavior.validation: Exactly the input and nested-union keys shown by the schema, ordinary dense arrays and passive own data properties. Numeric carriers are finite binary64 and never booleans; integral fields are exact integers in schema domain. Reject accessors, host instances and coercion. Complete static validation of every field/element precedes work preflight, RNG draws or output allocation. Products defining array lengths must be exact and <=4294967295 or INVALID_INPUT, even if all individual dimensions are valid. Canonicalize input zeros to +0.
behavior.work: maxWork is a required nonnegative safe integer. Count arithmetic is exact; an unsafe work sum/product or insufficient allowance is WORK_LIMIT. A charge checks before its action; rejected actions do not execute. The operation-specific schedule is normative. Static input validation has unavoidable input-sized cost. Budgets are abstract work, not memory or latency guarantees; host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.numerics: Separate binary64 primitive rounding, no reassociation/FMA. Every computed primitive must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, including division by an underflowed zero denominator. No numerical repair, implicit epsilon or state clipping. Exposed zeros are +0. General finite output fields use absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; integer/topology/order/state/token values compare exactly. The bound fixture file contains only exact analytical outputs; approximate RK4 linear-field and nonzero-angle turtle geometry tests remain separate future property tests.
behavior.ownership: Read only caller inputs; output records and arrays are detached. No input record, array, RNG object, renderer, host state or callback is retained. All generated state remains private until success. No partial result on error; a successful RK4 boundary termination is its explicit retained-prefix result, not an error. Scalars and immutable strings are values.
behavior.grid: For grid operations C=columns,R=rows,G=C*R, flattened row-major index y*C+x. Scalar/vector/binary state arrays have exactly G elements; vector pairs use caller X/Y axes. Discrete CLAMP selects nearest valid index; WRAP uses nonnegative modulo. Named neighbor offsets are counted separately even when small dimensions map them to the same cell. Spacing is positive [hx,hy]; discrete periodic axes have periods C*hx,R*hy, not duplicated endpoint grids.
behavior.laplacian: Laplacian over old state: lapX=((left-center)+(right-center))/(hx*hx); lapY=((up-center)+(down-center))/(hy*hy); lap=lapX+lapY. Evaluate separately rounded primitives in written order, X before Y. CLAMP/WRAP select neighbors as described by grid behavior; all output cells read the complete old state.
behavior.algorithm:
Gray–Scott reaction/diffusion step

Proposed ID: `field.gray-scott-step-2d`; state transform.

Artist output: next chemical concentration grids for reaction islands and stripe-grown
masks. The reusable output is scalar data for marching squares, palettes or image masks.
It owns one update; initialization, seeding disturbances, frame loops and rendering stay
outside. Studies must show an explicit bounded number of replayed steps.

Input:

```text
{state:{u:[number,...],v:[number,...]}, columns:integer>=1, rows:integer>=1,
 spacing:[positive,positive], diffusionU:number>=0, diffusionV:number>=0,
 feed:number>=0, kill:number>=0, dt:number>=0,
 boundary:"CLAMP"|"WRAP", maxWork:integer}
```

Output: `{u:[number,...],v:[number,...]}`. U/V are finite signed scalars, deliberately
not constrained to [0,1], so an unstable but finite result remains valid input to the next
call. No concentration clipping or assertion of physical stability is implied.

Reserve W=9G before output allocation. Visit cells row-major. Compute lapU then lapV by
the shared stencil. Then `reaction=(u*v)*v`, `du=(diffusionU*lapU-reaction)+feed*(1-u)`,
`dv=(diffusionV*lapV+reaction)-(feed+kill)*v`,
`uNext=u+dt*du`, `vNext=v+dt*dv`, in written order. Evaluate the complete expressions
even when dt or coefficients are zero. Work/storage O(G); no RNG or hidden timestep.

behavior.algorithm:
Life-like cellular step

Proposed ID: `field.life-like-step-2d`; state transform.

Artist output: next binary grid under an explicit totalistic birth/survival rule.
Studies: colony carpets; cell-age relief, with age accumulation explicitly in the caller.
This is simultaneous local state evolution, not the existing occupancy-claim path walk.

Input:

```text
{cells:[0|1,...], columns:integer>=1, rows:integer>=1,

```

then dx=-1..1 order, omitting only offset[0,0]. DEAD makes out-of-grid samples zero;
WRAP counts all eight offsets even if they address duplicate cells or the center itself.
Alive cells survive iff the count is in survival; dead cells are born iff it is in birth.
No asynchronous traversal, history, age, RNG or automatic stopping. O(G) work/storage.

old+strength*(centroid-old); strength0 returns exact old coordinate after cell

substitution point: caller can use final sites in the existing Voronoi operation.

passBudget=floor((maxWork-N-iterations)/iterations). Each Voronoi call receives
floor(passBudget/2); the other half is a separate centroid allowance. Charge one
centroid unit per returned polygon vertex and one per site update, including
empty cells. Insufficient allowance throws WORK_LIMIT; unused allowances are
not transferred between phases or passes. Zero iterations only requires N and
returns copied sites; empty input may return immediately after budget validation.

actual spent work. Validate finite sites and ordered finite bounds independently
before the zero-pass early return. Bounds match the Voronoi array schema.
