errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong shape/carriers, dimensions/product, unequal dimensions, pixel count/value, mask count/nonfinite/outside [0,1], null typed buffers.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Pixel index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Pixel index is representable but outside the retained output raster.

errorOrder: Follow behavior.validation; all configuration failures INVALID_INPUT.

behavior.input: Exactly source,destination,mask. Both raster records have exactly width,height,pixels. Positive integral dimensions; identical source/destination dimensions; exact pixel and mask counts. All pixels unsigned32; masks finite binary64 in [0,1]. No defaults.
behavior.compositing: For each pixel in row order: if mask == 0 or source alpha byte == 0, copy destination bits exactly. Otherwise let a=(sourceAlpha/255.0)*mask; b=destinationAlpha/255.0; t=1.0-a; u=b*t; v=a+u. If v == 0 (possible through underflow), output transparent black without division. Otherwise for each stored R,G,B byte pair s,d compute p=s*a; q=d*u; c=(p+q)/v. Output alpha byte Q(v*255.0), colors Q(c), where Q(x)=floor(min(255,max(0,x))+0.5). If quantized alpha is zero, output transparent black. Each stated arithmetic step is separately rounded binary64, ties-to-even; no FMA/reassociation or gamma conversion. The transparent-source/zero-mask identity branches precede transparent-black normalization and preserve hidden destination RGB.
behavior.ownership: The completed result owns a detached packed raster. It retains neither source pixels, destination pixels nor mask, and has no in-place form. Later caller mutation cannot affect the result. A failed call exposes no partial output.
behavior.access: width() and height() return dimensions. pixelAt(index) validates index as a finite safe nonnegative integer, then checks index < width*height; INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pixels() returns a detached int[] in Java (unsigned32 bit patterns), and toValues() returns detached {width,height,pixels}. Safe means at most 9007199254740991; negative zero is accepted as zero. pixelAt returns the Java int ARGB bit pattern; portable toValues pixels are unsigned32 numbers. Object indices accept only the same six numeric carriers as input.
behavior.numeric: IEEE binary64 arithmetic in stated order, one final byte quantization. Premultiplied working encoded RGB; no linear-light claim. Negative-zero mask equals zero.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.raster.MaskedComposite2D.compose(Object) and compose(int width,int height,int[] source,int[] destination,double[] mask). Result width(),height(),pixelAt(Object or long),pixels(),toValues(). Java implementation pending.
behavior.environment: No RNG, time, noise, host image, renderer, callback or mutable global state.
behavior.limits: width*height <= 2147483647, checked without signed32 overflow before allocation. Representation limit only; allocation failure is not INVALID_INPUT. O(width*height) time and owned output storage; no per-pixel allocation in typed kernel.
behavior.carriers: Object records are exact-key Map, arrays List. Numeric values accept only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double; reject boolean, strings, BigInteger,BigDecimal, arbitrary Number subclasses. Dimensions and pixels integral within schema bounds, mask converts to finite double. Typed buffers non-null. Passive stable inputs required; concurrent input mutation outside contract.
behavior.validation: Object: top keys; source keys/dimensions/product/pixel count then values; destination keys/dimensions/product/matching dimensions/pixel count then values; mask count then values. Typed: dimensions/product; source count; destination count; mask count then values. Complete validation before output allocation. Failure exposes no partial result.

guide.title: Composite through a mask
guide.summary: Blend a source raster over a destination with per-pixel mask weights.
guide.useWhen: Use it when your mask is already computed and needs exact composition.

inputs.source: A plain `{width, height, pixels}` object. Width and height are positive pixel counts; `pixels` contains exactly width × height unsigned `0xAARRGGBB` integers in row order. Convert p5.Image RGBA channels to this packed format first.
inputs.destination: The background raster in the same `{width, height, pixels}` format and with exactly the same dimensions as source. It is left unchanged; the operation creates a new raster.
inputs.mask: One finite value from 0 to 1 per pixel, in row order. Zero keeps the destination; one uses the source’s full alpha; intermediate values reduce source opacity before source-over blending.

guide.output: pixelAt(index) and pixels() return packed unsigned ARGB8/AARRGGBB values; toValues().pixels provides detached data.
guide.tryThis: Create `const image = p.createImage(raster.width, raster.height)` and call `image.loadPixels()`. Convert each packed ARGB32 pixel to RGBA slots: for pixel i, write red `(pixel >>> 16) & 255`, green `(pixel >>> 8) & 255`, blue `pixel & 255`, alpha `pixel >>> 24` at `image.pixels[4*i…4*i+3]`, then call `image.updatePixels()` and draw it with `p.image(image, 0, 0)`.

operations.description: Draft proposal only.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed domain/input.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Budget or safe arithmetic.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite computed intermediate.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. Complete static shape/value validation precedes work preflight. Geometric/topology tests run after preflight. Failure throws Error with stable code, no partial result. Outputs are detached. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0. Array lengths must fit 4294967295; unsafe requested growth/work arithmetic gives WORK_LIMIT before allocation. Host resource exhaustion is a host error, not an allocation guarantee. All grid/kernel/element dimensions are positive integers; each corresponding array length/product must fit 4294967295 and match exactly, otherwise INVALID_INPUT before work.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, rendering, assets, host state, mutation or retained aliases. Data uses caller coordinate/color conventions as specified.
behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. Check computed numeric intermediates for finiteness and throw NUMERIC_OVERFLOW on nonfinite results. No epsilon in classification or topology, no adaptive exact predicates or near-degeneracy guarantee. General scalar/coordinate comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; topology, indices, order, booleans and RNG states compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exact JSON output.
behavior.algorithm:
Input {colors,count,maxWork}; colors is nonempty RGB triples in [0,1], count>=1. Output
{palette,indices}. Begin box 0 containing source indices. A splittable box has >=2 members and nonzero
range in any channel. Choose box with greatest maximum channel range, tie lower current box index; choose
lowest tied channel. Stable-sort members by chosen channel then source index; replace selected box in place
by its lower half and append upper half (both creation order fixed). Stop when no splittable box or
min(count,colorCount) boxes. Palette is sequential source-order mean of each box. Each source chooses
nearest squared-RGB palette, tie lower index. Conservative work=colorCount*colorCount*count+
colorCount*count+colorCount, precharged. Fixtures: black/white,count2 -> black,white/[0,1];
three identical colors,count3 -> one identical palette and [0,0,0]. Studies: extract/dither field;
photo-grid mosaic.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export medianCutQuantize(input) from packages/javascript/src/median-cut-quantize.js. Other targets deferred.
behavior.arithmetic_order: Within a box, sum each channel in ascending original source-index order, starting at0, then divide by box size. Nearest palette squared RGB distance is ((dr*dr)+(dg*dg))+(db*db); tie chooses lower palette index. Count can exceed source size but preflight uses supplied count as written.

guide.title: Reduce RGB colors
guide.summary: Split source colors into stable median-cut boxes.
guide.useWhen: Split source colors into stable median-cut boxes.
guide.output: {palette,indices}
guide.code:
const result = medianCutQuantize({ colors:[[0,0,0],[1,1,1]], count:2, maxWork:14 });
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Change an input, keep maxWork sufficient, and draw the detached result.
pitfalls: Inputs are strict plain data and outputs do not retain them.

operations.description: Find the first closed-segment contact for each supplied directed query against supplied obstacles, retaining obstacle identity and explicit misses.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static shape/carrier/domain failure.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Interior selected contact cannot retain its distinction from a query endpoint; queryIndex and stage parameter or point.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Negative Java result index.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Nonnegative Java result index at or above size.

behavior.input: Exactly queries,obstacles,maxWork in a passive record. Validate keys; queries list and finite quadruples in order; obstacles list and finite quadruples in order; maxWork. Binary64 carriers only, no bool/string conversion. Java Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double only. Canonicalize signed zero. Validate all static input even when queries or obstacles empty. No defaults. Coordinates share caller units/origin/axes.
behavior.work: Let Q=queries.length,O=obstacles.length. Exact integer W=Q*O. WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when W>maxWork after all static validation and before contact computation/output generation. W counts abstract pair tests, not arithmetic instructions, time or allocation. Counts are representational ceilings, not artistic ranges.
behavior.contact: Each query A+t(B-A) and obstacle C+u(D-C) is closed. Nonparallel intersection qualifies iff exact t,u in[0,1]. Parallel noncollinear pairs miss. Collinear pairs intersect in a closed query-parameter interval: choose its least t. A zero-length query has t=0 iff its point belongs to the obstacle; a point obstacle may be contacted. Empty intersection misses. No automatic self/same-origin filtering. All predicates and ordering use exact rational values of supplied binary64 inputs.
behavior.selection: Select smallest exact t per query, ties by smallest supplied obstacle ordinal. Obstacle orientation does not affect contact location. Query orientation does. Return one entry per query in original order: null for miss or record obstacleIndex,t,point. No mutation or feedback between queries; later obstacles are not shortened by earlier queries. Overlap extent is not returned.
behavior.rounding: After selecting contact round exact t and each exact A+t(B-A) coordinate once to binary64 nearest-even; normalize zero. Exact t=0/1 preserves corresponding normalized input endpoint. For exact0<t<1 throw REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE stage parameter if rounded t is0or1; otherwise stage point if rounded point equals either query endpoint. Include queryIndex and stage. Check queries in input order; parameter before point. No partial output. Exact endpoint contacts including point queries are valid. Rounded point may lie slightly off exact obstacle; no painted-footprint guarantee.
behavior.ownership: Inputs not retained or mutated. Result owns contacts; exports detached data. No RNG,time,renderer or host objects. Native allocation failure remains host failure.
behavior.complexity: O(Q*O) exact geometric pair tests plus exact arithmetic bit costs; O(Q+O) captured input and O(Q) result storage; no per-pair retained result.
behavior.access: Java reference exposes static find(Object configuration), size(), hitAt(long index) and toValues(). hitAt returns null for miss or immutable Contact with obstacleIndex,t,x,y primitive fields. Negative indices produce INVALID_INDEX; index>=size produces INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. toValues returns independently owned output-schema records/lists. No mutable array accessor is necessary for a single contact. Java ContactException extends IllegalArgumentException with public final code, queryIndex and stage; queryIndex=-1 and stage=null except representation collapse. Contact fields are immutable primitive values; constructors are private.

guide.title: Find first segment contact
guide.summary: Query nearest contacts between ordered segment sets.
guide.useWhen: Use it when a drawing needs a deterministic closest obstacle relationship.

inputs.queries: Directed `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` segments. The first endpoint is the search origin; reversing endpoints can change which contact is first. Each query gets one hit or an explicit miss.
inputs.obstacles: Obstacle segments in the same `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` format and coordinate units. Input order breaks ties when contacts lie at the same query position. Endpoint contacts and collinear overlaps count.
inputs.maxWork: Nonnegative integer pair-test budget. Set it to at least queries.length × obstacles.length. The operation tests the complete supplied sets and does not shorten later obstacles after a hit.

guide.output: hitAt(queryIndex) returns null or {obstacleIndex,t,x,y}; the index matches queries, so use x and y to end or highlight that query stroke. toValues().hits instead exports each point as [x,y].
guide.tryThis: Use returned contact coordinates to place a highlight or stop a stroke.

operations.description: Retain an attempt-bounded connected path whose accepted proposals remain within a strict scalar band around the starting noise value.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static carrier/key/value, nonfinite value or out-of-domain static field.
errors.TRACE_QUERY_INVALID: Dynamic field coordinate invalid; includes attemptIndex and query stage.
errors.TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite heading, displacement or endpoint; includes attemptIndex and stage.
errors.VERTEX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: An accepted append would exceed maxVertices; includes attemptIndex and append stage.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Index exceeds retained point or heading range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination or offset cannot hold two binary64 values.

behavior.input: Validate passive input outer shape and exact keys, then field exactly {seed:uint32}, start exactly two finite binary64 coordinates x then y, heading finite binary64 radians without normalization, seed integer0..4294967295, attempts integer0..2147483647, stepDistance finite binary64 >=0, fieldScale finite binary64 including negative and zero, fieldOffset exactly two finite binary64 field coordinates, tolerance finite binary64 >=0, and maxVertices integer1..1073741823, in that order. Reject booleans, null, strings and arbitrary Number classes. All static failures are INVALID_INPUT. There are no defaults, recommended ranges or host fields/callbacks. Canonicalize -0 to +0 before computation and detached configuration export.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map output to u=unsigned_u32/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). State is private/discarded and never shares Processing/source/background/palette state. The all-zero state is unreachable and an internal invariant.
behavior.transition: Use fdlibm5.3 binary64 sin/cos as provided by Java StrictMath; no caller angle reduction. All basic operators round separately to binary64, with no FMA or reassociation. HALF_PI=0x1.921fb54442d18p0; decimal .1 and .2 mean nearest binary64 values. C(v,stage) raises TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with attemptIndex and stage if v is nonfinite. Q(x,y,prefix) evaluates qx=x*fieldScale, checks that product finite, then qx=qx+offsetX, checks that final value is finite and -9007199254740991 <= qx < 9007199254740991; then does the same qy with the x/y prefix stages. An invalid product or final value raises TRACE_QUERY_INVALID. Query existing field.sample(qx,qy), whose finite [0,1] output is guaranteed. After static validation retain start and heading. If attempts=0 return immediately with no RNG draws, field sample, coordinate transform or trig. Otherwise attemptIndex=-1; level=Q(startX,startY,start_query); then create private RNG. For attemptIndex 0..attempts-1: u0=U(); low=(-HALF_PI)*u0; u1=U(); high=HALF_PI*u1; span=high-low; u2=U(); delta=span*u2; turn=low+delta; proposal=C(heading+turn,proposal_heading); dx=C(stepDistance*fdlibmCos(proposal),delta_x); nx=C(x+dx,position_x); dy=C(stepDistance*fdlibmSin(proposal),delta_y); ny=C(y+dy,position_y); value=Q(nx,ny,candidate_query); u3=U(); driftProduct=.2*u3; drift=-.1+driftProduct; rejectionHeading=C(heading+drift,rejection_heading); difference=value-level; bandError=abs(difference). If bandError < tolerance, fail VERTEX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with attemptIndex and append stage when size==maxVertices, then canonicalize nx,ny,proposal, append point and heading, update x,y,heading and accepted. Otherwise canonicalize rejectionHeading into heading and increment rejected. Every completed attempt consumes four draws; rejection drift is calculated and validated even on acceptance. No retry, early stop, boundary handling or partial result.
behavior.canonicalization: Every stored coordinate and heading is canonical positive zero when equal to zero. Canonicalize updated x, y and heading before they feed the next attempt; do not canonicalize every temporary. Subnormal values and arithmetic underflow are permitted, with no flush-to-zero profile. The difference of two field samples cannot overflow. Trig and field are evaluated for zero distance. Resource failure is tested only for an actually accepted append, after candidate query and rejection-heading checks.
behavior.storage: O(attempts) work and O(accepted) retained numeric payload, 24 bytes per accepted move plus 16-byte starting coordinates excluding headers/capacity. Grow bounded packed arrays lazily; never preallocate maxVertices, retain rejected coordinates or create per-attempt objects. Resource failure is checked only for an actually accepted append, after candidate query and rejection-heading checks. Host allocation failures remain host errors.
behavior.native_surface: Java reference class is org.procedurals.paths.NoiseBandPath2D with static trace(Object). size(), attempts(), accepted(), rejected() return int; pointAt(Object/long) returns new double[2]; pointInto(Object/long,double[],int) writes two coordinates; headingAt(Object/long) returns the proposal heading for accepted segment i; serialize() returns detached validated configuration; toValues() returns exactly {positions:[[x,y],...],headings:[...],attempts,accepted,rejected}. No mutable state, shared RNG, drawing, implicit seed layout or incremental execution API.
behavior.access: For point and heading access, reject nonfinite, negative, fractional or >9007199254740991 index as INVALID_INDEX; a valid index >=size (point) or >=accepted (heading) is INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pointInto validates index before output; null/insufficient double[] or negative/overflowing offset gives INVALID_OUTPUT with no writes. Failed queries leave the result usable.
behavior.native_representations: Java interchange: passive Map records and List pairs; only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double numeric carriers. Reject BigInteger,BigDecimal,custom Number and booleans before conversion. pointInto accepts double[] and int offset; no partial writes. No arbitrary field/callback inputs. JSON ordinary records/arrays define future portable interchange; no runtime support is implied.
behavior.complexity: Eager O(attempts) transition work and O(accepted) retained storage; O(1) point/heading access and O(size) detached export.
behavior.normative_transition: design/operations/noise-band-path-contract.md; transition and ordered arithmetic there are normative together with this catalog. No new host-dependent semantics may be inferred.
behavior.numeric_details: Canonicalize input and stored coordinate/heading zeros to +0 before subsequent use; intermediate signed zeros remain IEEE754. Subnormals and underflow are permitted; no flush-to-zero. Trig and field queries execute even at zero stepDistance. Four draws per completed attempt even when bounds coincide or tolerance is zero; dynamic errors stop before later draws. Query product is checked finite only; final product+offset must also meet lattice bounds. Error detail is exactly {attemptIndex,stage}, with -1 for initial query and zero-based attempts thereafter; static and access errors have no dynamic detail.
behavior.ownership: Copy input configuration; construct privately; serialize and toValues deeply detached. Caller modifications before/after export cannot alter retained path. Host allocation errors remain host errors and no partial result escapes.

guide.title: Trace within a noise band
guide.summary: Grow a bounded path while a noise condition accepts steps.
guide.useWhen: Use it for organic strands with an explicit work limit.

inputs.field: A descriptor `{seed: 42}` for the package’s 2D noise field. This field seed selects the terrain being sampled; pass data rather than a p5 noise function.
inputs.start: Starting `[x, y]` position, always retained. Its noise value establishes the reference level for every proposal in this path.
inputs.heading: Initial direction in radians. Zero points along positive X; positive angles turn toward positive Y. On a usual p5 canvas that appears clockwise.
inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295 for the path’s proposal turns. This is separate from field.seed: change it to try another route through the same noise field.
inputs.attempts: Nonnegative integer number of proposals. Rejected proposals do not add a point, but subsequent attempts continue. This is not a requested number of vertices.
inputs.stepDistance: Nonnegative distance between the current point and a proposed next point. Zero permits repeated positions when the band accepts them.
inputs.fieldScale: Multiply each drawing coordinate by this value before sampling the field. Larger magnitudes sample a wider span of the field across the same drawing; zero samples one fixed location. Negative values are allowed.
inputs.fieldOffset: A finite `[x, y]` translation applied after fieldScale, in field coordinates. Change it to sample a different part of the same seeded field without moving the path’s starting point.
inputs.tolerance: Nonnegative allowed difference from the starting noise value. A proposal is accepted only when its absolute difference is strictly less than tolerance. Zero accepts none; larger values relax the band.
inputs.maxVertices: Positive integer limit including the starting point. Set attempts + 1 to allow every proposal to succeed. An accepted proposal beyond this capacity throws rather than truncating the path.

guide.output: pointAt(index) reads the start plus each accepted [x,y] step and headingAt(index) reads accepted headings; size, accepted, and rejected show what the fixed attempt budget produced. toValues() is copied geometry.
guide.tryThis: Turn headings into cross marks or connected strokes.

operations.description: Generate ordered retained cardinal cell paths whose cells are claimed by one call-local occupancy set.

dimensions.description: [columns, rows] integer lattice dimensions; origin is north-west, x grows east and y grows south.

starts.description: Ordered start-cell pairs. Duplicates are valid sequential occupancy outcomes.

maxSteps.description: Maximum successful cardinal moves after each available start.

random.description: Exactly one private-stream carrier: uint32 seed or nonzero [s0,s1,s2,s3] uint32 state.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static carrier/key/value, out-of-domain coordinate/limit, seed/state carrier or forbidden all-zero supplied state.
errors.WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: All static fields are valid but starts.length*(maxSteps+1) exceeds maxCells.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Path or cell index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: A representable path or cell index exceeds its retained range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: cellInto destination or offset cannot hold two int values.

behavior.input: Input has exactly dimensions, starts, maxSteps, maxCells and random. Static validation order is: outer passive record/keys; dimensions pair then columns then rows; starts outer List/length, then each pair and its x then y in increasing start index; maxSteps; maxCells; random record/keys, then its sole seed or state carrier and state words in increasing index. Every numeric carrier is finite integral in its stated domain and never bool. Each start must be within its corresponding half-open dimension. State [0,0,0,0] is INVALID_INPUT. Complete all static validation before comparing capacity, initializing the stream, claiming occupancy, allocating output-sized storage or mutating caller data. Then calculate starts.length*(maxSteps+1) with exact checked wide integer arithmetic; if it exceeds maxCells, fail WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. No defaults.
behavior.generation: Use one call-local sparse occupancy set and process starts in input order. An occupied start appends [] and occupied-start and consumes no word. Otherwise append and claim the start. If maxSteps is zero, append step-limit before enumerating neighbours. For each remaining successful move, enumerate in-bounds unoccupied candidates in north, east, south, west order. No candidates appends blocked without a word. Otherwise consume one word, select one candidate, append it and claim it. Reaching maxSteps successful moves appends step-limit. There are no retries, proposals with replacement, random starts, truncation or partial output.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. A supplied state bypasses seed expansion. For available count c in1..4, choose floor(unsigned_u32*c/4294967296); this consumes exactly one word, including c=1. This discrete mapping is the contract and does not assert equal mathematical probability where c does not divide2^32. Blocked and occupied-start paths consume no word.
behavior.integer_layout: Coordinates are signed int32 values; valid dimensions ensure every emitted coordinate and cardinal neighbour calculation is representable. Retain two signed int32 coordinate scalars per emitted cell in growable owned packed storage. maxCells<=1073741823 keeps total two-coordinate scalar storage signed-int-indexable. Do not dense-allocate by dimensions, preallocate maxCells, or allocate per-cell output objects during generation. maxCells is a representation admission ceiling, not an actual output, latency, memory or artistic guarantee. Host allocation failures are host failures and never translated into operation errors.
behavior.ownership: Inputs are never mutated or retained. Occupancy, packed output and stream state are local to one eager call. The result owns detached storage. Each materialized JSON path/cell/state carrier and each native accessor carrier is fresh; changing it cannot affect the result. Exporting/read access never advances the stream. A rejected configuration exposes no result and no partial output.
behavior.native_surface: Java reference class is org.procedurals.paths.OccupiedLatticePaths2D with static generate(Object config). Public accessors are int pathCount(); int pathLengthAt(Object path) and pathLengthAt(long path); int[] cellAt(Object path,Object cell) and cellAt(long path,long cell); void cellInto(Object path,Object cell,int[] output,int offset) and cellInto(long path,long cell,int[] output,int offset); String completionReasonAt(Object path) and completionReasonAt(long path); long[] randomState(); and Map<String,Object> toValues(). No mixed path/cell overload exists. randomState returns a fresh long[4], each 0..4294967295; cellAt returns fresh int[2]. The only public operation exception is nested LatticeException extends IllegalArgumentException with final String code. Host resource exceptions remain host exceptions.
behavior.access: All path/cell indices are finite safe nonnegative integers no greater than9007199254740991, with booleans excluded; integral floating carriers are accepted where a host supports them. For cellAt/cellInto, validate in this exact field order: path numeric domain, path range, cell numeric domain, cell range, then destination. An out-of-range path therefore wins over an invalid cell carrier; an invalid cell carrier wins over destination validation only after the path is in range. Thus empty occupied-start paths have no valid cell index. cellInto requires an int[] with two writable slots starting at a finite nonnegative integral offset and writes both only after every validation succeeds; any failure leaves every destination slot unchanged.
behavior.complexity: For admitted inputs, O(starts.length + emitted cells) retained storage and O(starts.length + successfulMoves) transition work, with at most four candidate checks per successful-move iteration. Sparse occupancy is O(emitted cells). path/cell scalar reads are O(1); toValues is O(starts.length + emitted cells) detached materialization, including empty occupied-start entries.
environment: explicit private xoshiro128**1.1 seed or state
behavior.exclusions: No renderer, drawing commands, grid metric, palette, style stream, session, callback, graph, maze/route guarantee, global occupancy, retained continuation object, host RNG, clock or noise is consumed. Guagua's unrestricted revisiting walk is deferred and is not this operation.

guide.title: Grow occupied grid paths
guide.summary: Retain non-overwriting paths through a rectangular lattice.
guide.useWhen: Use it for tile routes and constrained line work.

inputs.dimensions: Positive integer `[columns, rows]` cell counts. Coordinates run from 0 through columns − 1 and rows − 1; this is a grid, not a canvas size in pixels.
inputs.starts: Ordered integer `[x, y]` starting cells within the grid. Paths grow in this order and share occupancy, so earlier paths can block later starts. A blocked start returns an empty path.
inputs.maxSteps: Nonnegative integer move limit per path. Each successful move visits a free north/east/south/west neighbor. A path may stop earlier when all neighbors are occupied or outside the grid.
inputs.maxCells: Integer cell-work capacity. It must cover starts.length × (maxSteps + 1), even if paths would actually become blocked earlier. The operation checks this before growing any paths.
inputs.random: Either `{seed: 42}` or `{state: [s0, s1, s2, s3]}`. Each number is an integer from 0 to 4294967295; the four state words cannot all be zero. State can continue random choices, but does not preserve previous calls’ occupancy.

guide.output: pathCount is the number of paths; pathLengthAt(path) and cellAt(path,cell) let you draw every retained integer [x,y] cell. completionReasonAt(path) explains where a route stopped; toValues() copies that collection.
guide.tryThis: Map each returned cell to your canvas grid.

operations.description: Evaluate an ordered geometric octave sum over the existing 2D or 3D gradient-noise profile at supplied points.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static carrier/domain/normalization failure before work.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Exact schedule+sampling events exceed budget/safe bound.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite schedule, query product, weighted sample, sum or normalized result.
errors.QUERY_OUT_OF_RANGE: Finite multiplied coordinate outside existing gradient profile half-open safe query domain.

behavior.validation: Passive Object/null-prototype record with exactly dimension,points,seed,octaves,frequency,lacunarity,amplitude,persistence,normalization,maxWork. Reject classes/accessors/symbols/extras/coercion; proxies outside interchange. Dense ordinary arrays with own data slots, no extras. Static validation order: outer carrier/keys; dimension numeric2 or3; points shape length0..2147483647 and every tuple with exactly dimension finite coordinates in array/axis order; uint32 seed; octaves integer1..2147483647; finite frequency>=0; finite lacunarity>0; finite amplitude>=0; finite persistence>=0; normalization NONE/WEIGHT_SUM and WEIGHT_SUM requires amplitude>0; nonnegative safe-integer maxWork. Canonicalize accepted zeros. Validate all inputs before work, including zero weights and empty points.
behavior.work: After full static validation compute exact integer W=(N+1)*octaves with overflow-safe arithmetic. If W exceeds maxWork or safe integer maximum, WORK_LIMIT before schedule, field creation or output allocation. One schedule event and N field-sample events per octave, including zero-weight octaves. Empty points still compute schedule and amplitudeSum with cost octaves. Output storage O(N), schedule O(octaves), total work O((N+1)*octaves). Host exhaustion is a host error; no partial output.
behavior.schedule: Before evaluating any point, build frequencies and weights in octave order starting frequency and amplitude. Set amplitudeSum=0; for each used octave store frequency/weight then amplitudeSum=amplitudeSum+weight, checking finite. Only if another octave remains: nextFrequency=frequency*lacunarity then nextWeight=weight*persistence, checking finite after each. Underflow to0 is valid. Never update past the last octave. Finite amplitudeSum is required even for NONE and empty points.
behavior.algorithm: Select existing field.gradient-noise-2d-01@0.1.0 or field.gradient-noise-3d-01@0.1.0 by dimension, with the SAME supplied seed for every octave. For each point in supplied order start sum=0. For each octave ascending: for axes x,y,(z) in that order compute q=point[axis]*frequency[octave], check finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW; require -9007199254740991<=q<9007199254740991 or QUERY_OUT_OF_RANGE. Sample the existing profile only after all query axes validate. Compute weighted=weight*sample then sum=sum+weighted, each finite. No skip when weight0. If WEIGHT_SUM compute value=sum/amplitudeSum once after the last octave and require finite; else value=sum. Canonicalize completed output zero. Return detached {values,amplitudeSum}; no output clamp, signed remap, compensated sum, normalization per octave or coordinate feedback.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separately rounded primitive operations in specified order; no FMA/reassociation or narrowing. Existing gradient profiles and hash define exact scalar samples; no host Processing/p5 noise substitution. State/shape/errors compare exactly; scalar fixture tolerance absolute1e-12 relative0. Finite arithmetic checks precede any later cancellation; underflow to zero valid. Inputs are finite, but multiplied query coordinates may violate the existing profile domain.
behavior.native_surface: p5 named exports octaveGradientNoise(input) and OctaveGradientNoiseError from octave-gradient-noise.js and package index; other targets deferred. Plain values only.
behavior.environment: No ambient noise, RNG, clock, field callbacks or host objects. Fixed seed reused each octave, no seed advance. Any coordinate offset is supplied by caller before frequency scaling; no per-octave offset or independent seed.
behavior.adapter: Native p5 Canvas2D study maps returned scalar values to mark size/color on retained positions. Renderer never evaluates noise or recomputes accumulation; save exports the rendered canvas.

guide.title: Evaluate octave gradient noise
guide.summary: Add smaller patches of variation to a broad pattern, then use the values for size, color or movement.
guide.useWhen: Sample the same retained positions at several scales. Weight normalization keeps the total field scale separate from its detail count.

inputs.points: Ordered finite coordinate tuples matching dimension.
inputs.seed: Explicit uint32 seed reused at every octave.
inputs.octaves: Positive band count; more bands can add smaller detail when lacunarity exceeds 1.
inputs.frequency: Initial nonnegative spatial frequency; higher values make the broad pattern smaller.
inputs.lacunarity: Positive frequency multiplier between bands; values above 1 move toward finer detail.
inputs.amplitude: Initial nonnegative weight; sets strength for NONE and cancels under WEIGHT_SUM.
inputs.persistence: Nonnegative weight multiplier; larger values give later bands more influence.
inputs.normalization: NONE keeps the raw sum; WEIGHT_SUM divides by the total weight.
inputs.maxWork: Schedule and sampling budget: at least (points.length+1)*octaves.

guide.output: {values,amplitudeSum}
guide.tryThis: Increase octaves or change normalization, then compare values in the original point order.
pitfalls: The same seed is reused for each octave; it is not an ambient or advancing RNG stream.
Coordinate products are checked against the existing profile domain before sampling.
The operation returns scalar values only; displacement, color mapping, and drawing are caller work.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. behavior.algorithm:
Input: points (at least two xy points), closed (boolean), distance (finite),
miterLimit (finite >=1), maxWork. Output: {points}. Adjacent coincidences are
INVALID_INPUT, including a repeated closing point. Closed input requires at
least three points. Unit left normal of edge dx,dy is [-dy/length,dx/length].
Distance is signed in this coordinate convention. Open endpoints use the single
adjacent normal. At an interior corner with incoming/outgoing unit directions,
cross==0 and dot<0 is INVALID_INPUT (exact reversal), including distance==0.
Same-direction parallel edges emit the vertex plus distance*incoming normal.
Otherwise intersect the two offset infinite lines; use that miter if its distance
from the original vertex <= abs(distance)*miterLimit. A longer miter emits two
bevel endpoints, incoming then outgoing. Zero distance returns the source vertex
once after validating direction/reversal constraints. No caps, thickness region,
self-intersection cleanup or polygon Boolean behavior is implied. Preflight
4*N <= maxWork. Closed output begins at the join of source vertex zero; it does
not append its initial point. Output order follows source traversal.

behavior.algorithm:
Input {stops,count,maxWork}, >=2 encoded sRGB triples in [0,1], count>=2. Output {colors}, encoded
sRGB triples. Decode each component c by c/12.92 if c<=.04045, otherwise ((c+.055)/1.055)^2.4. At
u=k/(count-1), select span min(floor(u*(N-1)),N-2), t=u*(N-1)-span, convert stops to Oklab, lerp L,a,b,
inverse convert, clamp each reconstructed linear RGB component independently to [0,1], then encode linear
c by 12.92c if c<=.0031308, otherwise 1.055*c^(1/2.4)-.055. Output k=0 and k=count-1 are copied exact
input endpoint triples. Forward LMS rows:
(.4122214708,.5363325363,.0514459929),(.2119034982,.6806995451,.1073969566),
(.0883024619,.2817188376,.6299787005), cube roots, then
(.2104542553,.7936177850,-.0040720468),(1.9779984951,-2.4285922050,.4505937099),
(.0259040371,.7827717662,-.8086757660). Inverse uses
l'=L+.3963377774a+.2158037573b, m'=L-.1055613458a-.0638541728b,
s'=L-.0894841775a-1.2914855480b; cube; then
(4.0767416621,-3.3077115913,.2309699292),(-1.2684380046,2.6097574011,-.3413193965),
(-.0041960863,-.7034186147,1.7076147010). Work=stops+count. Fixtures: exact black/white endpoint
copies; red-to-blue count3 has an approximate specified interior tolerance per channel 1e-9.
Studies: terrain ramp; ribbon palette. Primary: https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/

behavior.arithmetic_order: Matrix row sums are (a*x+b*y)+c*z with separate checked operations. Interpolation is start+t*(end-start) per L,a,b component. Cube by (x*x)*x, and use Math.cbrt for forward LMS. Encoded output k=0 and k=count-1 copies endpoints exactly; internal stop positions are evaluated through the declared matrices. Clamp reconstructed linear channels to [0,1] before the stated encoding formula; this is component clipping, not perceptual gamut mapping.

operations.description: Retain supplied circles in order when their radius-dependent exclusion test permits them alongside earlier accepted circles.

centres.description: Ordered candidate centre pairs; length must equal radii length.

radii.description: One positive radius per centre, in the same coordinate unit.

separationScale.description: Multiplier on summed radii;1 permits tangency, below1 permits overlap, above1 reserves size-relative clearance.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong shape, unsupported passive carrier, bool numeric, unequal centre/radius lengths, nonpositive radius or separationScale, or proposal cardinality above the representation bound.
errors.PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite pair arithmetic or specified pair underflow; candidateIndex and named pair stage, no output.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite nonnegative safe integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index is outside0..size-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination or offset lacks two writable binary64 slots.

behavior.layout: A placement result privately retains 2*N binary64 centre coordinates, N binary64 radii and N integer original proposal indices, where N is accepted count. Apply proposal-count ceiling1073741823 statically to seeded attempts or explicit input length, so even accepting every proposal fits2*N<=2147483647. This is a shared packed-array/index representation bound, not an allocation, latency or useful artistic range guarantee. Capacity growth must be capped at this representation ceiling without integer overflow. Host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never INVALID_INPUT or partial successful output.
behavior.acceptance: Visit proposals in original order i=0..attempts-1. For each, visit retained circles in their acceptance order. Compute dx=round64(x-oldX), dy=round64(y-oldY), xx=round64(dx*dx), yy=round64(dy*dy), squared=round64(xx+yy), sumR=round64(r+oldR), threshold=round64(sumR*separationScale), limitSquared=round64(threshold*threshold), in that exact order with validation immediately after each stage. Reject the proposal at the first pair where squared<limitSquared and skip its remaining pairs. Equality is accepted. If no pair rejects, append canonical centre, positive radius and original index. The first valid proposal is accepted without pair arithmetic. Seeded generation and explicit filtering feed exactly this same internal kernel; no duplicated predicate or implicit sorting.
behavior.pair_validation: For each computed pair stage require finite binary64. Stages in order: difference_x, difference_y, square_x, square_y, distance_squared, radius_sum, threshold, threshold_squared. Also fail square_x when dx!=0 and xx==0; fail square_y when dy!=0 and yy==0; fail threshold when threshold<=0 (positive operands must not underflow to zero); fail threshold_squared when limitSquared==0. These conservative guards reject nonzero square underflow and collapsed positive exclusion, without an arbitrary coordinate envelope. Failure code PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID includes candidateIndex=i and stage. Discard the entire internal accepted prefix and return no result. Do not report the compared retained index. A rejected proposal does not evaluate later pair stages or remaining retained pairs.
behavior.ownership: Result owns detached accepted arrays only. Inputs must not be mutated concurrently with either eager call; active getters/proxies/custom hooks are outside the passive interchange contract. Complete the full static validation pass before allocating result-sized retained storage or starting pair work. A full-input snapshot is not required. Do not retain caller-owned arrays or persistent rejected-proposal copies. Getter returns and toValues are detached. toValues returns exactly output_schema and explicitly authorizes additional O(N) materialization. Allocation failure in a fresh pointAt/point_at pair or toValues/to_values materialization returns no new value and leaves the original retained result usable and unchanged. The result has no serialize/toJSON/config replay API: callers retain their input configuration; accepted geometry is not a reconstruction of the rejected proposal sequence.
behavior.access: Native size() and attempts() (JavaScript/Python properties) return accepted N and original proposal count. Rejected count is attempts-size; do not add count aliases. pointAt/point_at returns a fresh two-number centre, radiusAt/radius_at returns one radius, sourceIndexAt/source_index_at returns original proposal index. All indices require finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991, never bool; integral floating indices are accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (index>=N). pointInto/point_into checks index validity and bound before destination/offset. Then require writable binary64 space for exactly two slots and a finite nonnegative integral offset; otherwise INVALID_OUTPUT. Never mutate any destination slot on failure. Float32 output buffers are forbidden. Java may use typed int offset; wrong-type/unrepresentable host calls are host-call errors, not different interchange semantics. Java pointInto has a required typed int offset and returns void. JavaScript pointInto(index,out,offset=0) returns the supplied out destination. Python point_into(index,out,offset=0) returns None. These are native transport conventions; all write the same two coordinates and preserve the same failure ordering.
behavior.native_types: Follow existing grid numeric conventions: Java Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double only; reject BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive object/Array input with number values; Python int/float but never bool, convert to finite binary64 after validating integer domains where applicable. Python huge integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT/INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception. Output pointInto accepts Java double[], JS Float64Array or writable ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list or array(d). Offset/count/index validation must precede narrowing. Active accessors/proxies and custom containers are not interchange data. Input containers: Java Map for records and exactly two-element List for pairs; arrays/PVector are not pair input carriers. Only passive container behavior belongs to interchange; active custom hooks are outside it. Python requires exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs, rejecting custom Mapping/list subclasses and tuples. JS records have Object.prototype or null prototype and pairs are ordinary Array; class instances/typed-array pairs are not interchange input.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even for every basic operation in the stated order. No FMA, reassociation, sqrt/hypot substitute, epsilon, binary32 conversion or host transcendental in the core. Normalize every zero input coordinate and completed zero output coordinate to positive zero. Radius and scale must be strictly positive. Compare core output coordinates/radii by exact binary64 bits and all counts/source indices/errors exactly across targets; do not tolerate topology differences. This is a checked floating predicate, not an exact real-number geometry guarantee. Supplied radial points are caller data: cross-host trigonometry used to construct them is outside this contract.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar centre coordinates and radii in the same length unit. A radius is half a circle diameter. No canvas, axis orientation or renderer is implicit; host drawing may use y downward. separationScale is dimensionless, multiplying summed radii:1 permits computed tangency, below1 permits geometric overlap, above1 adds size-relative clearance. It is not a fixed pixel gap. The filter has no containment domain.
behavior.complexity: O(P*A) pair work, at worst O(P^2), for P proposals and up to A accepted circles; O(A) retained primitive storage and O(1) accessor work. Explicit filtering also statically validates all P records before pair work. Seeded generation streams candidates and retains no all-proposal array. Eager invocation authorizes finite work; no universal real-time or saturation guarantee. Any future acceleration must preserve outputs AND defined failure behavior/order, not merely typical placements.
behavior.native_errors: Validation/access exceptions have code. PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID additionally exposes candidateIndex (Python candidate_index) and stage, emitted as error_detail:{candidateIndex,stage} by conformance runners. Static INVALID_INPUT and accessor errors have no dynamic detail. Java validation errors may subclass IllegalArgumentException and arithmetic errors ArithmeticException; JS Error and Python ValueError subclasses are transport. Host resource failures are not converted to validation errors or partial success.
behavior.input: Input has exactly centres, radii, separationScale. Validate outer passive record/keys; centres Array/List length0..1073741823; radii Array/List and equal length; separationScale finite positive; then for i=0..P-1 validate centre pair and finite x/y, then positive finite radius, in that order. Booleans are never numbers. Validate EVERY explicit proposal before allocating result-sized retained storage or starting pair work, including proposals that would later be rejected. Normalize coordinate zeros; explicit input must not mutate during this synchronous eager call. Do not retain rejected input after return. Empty input still validates scale and returns empty arrays with attempts0.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.sampling.CirclePlacements2D.filter(Object config) returns CirclePlacements2D, with size(),attempts(),pointAt(Object or long),pointInto(index,double[],int offset),radiusAt(Object or long),sourceIndexAt(Object or long),toValues(). JavaScript orderedCircleFilter2D(config) returns result with size/attempts getters, pointAt,pointInto,radiusAt,sourceIndexAt,toValues. Python ordered_circle_filter_2d(config) returns result with size/attempts properties, point_at,point_into,radius_at,source_index_at,to_values. No result serialize/toJSON or count aliases. Both operations return the same result type/semantics.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, renderer, asset, lifecycle or trigonometric input. Supplied circle values and order plus separationScale fully determine the result.
behavior.degenerate: Coincident or collinear centres are valid inputs; the ordered predicate decides acceptance. Radius0/negative, negative or zero separationScale, nonfinite values and mismatched lengths are INVALID_INPUT. A tiny positive radius can be retained as the first/only circle; a later pair may fail the specified arithmetic guards. Below1 scale permits overlap. No hidden clamping, containment, deduplication, sorting or geometric tolerance.

guide.title: Keep separated circles
guide.summary: Filter caller-provided circles in proposal order.

inputs.separationScale: A positive multiplier on the sum of two radii. At 1 circles may touch; below 1 they may overlap; above 1 they have size-relative clearance. It is not a fixed pixel gap.

operations.description: Synchronously advance equal-unit-mass 2D bodies under supplied reciprocal attraction and short-range repulsion pairs.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static carrier, shape, correspondence, canonical pair or domain failure.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: N+P exceeds maxWork after static validation.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite intermediate force, norm, velocity or position, no partial output.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype record; no classes, accessors, symbols, extras or coercion. Dense ordinary arrays with own data slots and no extras; proxies outside interchange. Point arrays contain finite binary64 pairs, length at most2147483647. Canonicalize accepted zero values. Validate all fields and correspondence in input-schema order before work checks, including empty/identity cases. No input mutation or aliasing; all output arrays and pairs detached. Velocities length equals points. Pairs are integer indices 0<=i<j<N in strict lex order, no duplicates. Coefficients finite nonnegative; damping in[0,1], dt strictly positive, maxSpeed nonnegative, maxWork nonnegative safe integer.
behavior.work: After complete static validation require N+P<=maxWork, before arithmetic/output allocation. O(N+P) time and storage. No partial state on error.
behavior.algorithm: Initialize N force pairs to positive zero. Visit supplied pairs lex order. Compute dx=xj-xi then dy=yj-yi, length=fdlibmHypot(dx,dy); check finite after each. Compute fx=attraction*dx then fy=attraction*dy. If 0<length<repulsionRadius compute ratio=length/repulsionRadius, falloff=1-ratio, strength=repulsion*falloff, ux=dx/length, uy=dy/length, rx=strength*ux, ry=strength*uy, then fx=fx-rx and fy=fy-ry; check every primitive finite. Coincident pairs have zero repulsion and attraction; no direction invented. Accumulate Fi.x+=fx, Fi.y+=fy, Fj.x-=fx, Fj.y-=fy, in that order, checking each sum. Then visit agents ascending: for x then y compute impulse=dt*force, kicked=oldVelocity+impulse, v=kicked*damping, each finite. speed=fdlibmHypot(vx,vy), finite. If speed>maxSpeed compute scale=maxSpeed/speed then multiply vx and vy, each finite. For x then y compute travel=dt*v then position=oldPosition+travel, each finite. Canonicalize all returned zeros. Return detached points,velocities,forces, never shared pair storage.
behavior.numerics: Binary64 ordered primitives, no FMA/reassociation; fdlibmHypot existing audited profile, correctly rounded native arithmetic otherwise. No epsilon in computation. Exact fixture integer/index/error comparison; specified floating fixtures permit absolute1e-12 relative0 only. Nonfinite intermediate raises NUMERIC_OVERFLOW even if later multiplication/damping would cancel it.
behavior.environment: No randomness, clock or renderer. dt in caller time units, no inferred frame rate. No boundary policy, speed floors, mass, force normalization by degree, pinning, alignment, sensors, contact memory or collision resolution. Damping is per call, after acceleration and before movement; zero damping prevents movement.

guide.title: Move a network with pair forces
guide.summary: Let connected points pull together and resist crowding, then draw their motion as trails or changing relationships.
guide.useWhen: Supply a proximity graph or a fixed graph; the same synchronous step works with either.

inputs.points: Finite [x,y] positions; one per equal-unit-mass body.
inputs.velocities: Finite [vx,vy] values in coordinate units per time unit, matching points.
inputs.pairs: Canonical unique [i,j] pairs with i<j in strict lexicographic order.
inputs.attraction: Nonnegative linear attraction coefficient, in inverse time squared.
inputs.repulsion: Nonnegative peak repulsive acceleration, tapered to zero at repulsionRadius.
inputs.repulsionRadius: Short-range repulsion distance; zero disables repulsion.
inputs.damping: Per-call velocity multiplier from zero to one, applied before movement.
inputs.dt: Strictly positive logical time step; the operation never reads a clock.
inputs.maxSpeed: Nonnegative speed cap in coordinate units per time unit.
inputs.maxWork: Budget of at least point count plus supplied pair count.

guide.output: {points,velocities,forces}: three detached arrays. Forces are the summed pre-damping, pre-speed-cap force vectors.
guide.code:
const next = pairForceStep2D({points:[[0,0],[2,0]],velocities:[[0,0],[0,0]],pairs:[[0,1]],attraction:0.5,repulsion:0,repulsionRadius:0,damping:1,dt:1,maxSpeed:10,maxWork:3});
console.log(next.points);
guide.tryThis: Replace proximity pairs with a fixed chain, or change repulsion while retaining the initial state. Requery next positions before drawing current proximity edges.
pitfalls: Coincident points have no invented separation direction.
Damping is per call, so changing dt alone does not preserve the trajectory.
There are no walls, collisions, flock alignment or retained contact ages.

operations.description: Rewrite explicit token productions in simultaneous generations with bounded token and work counts.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed shape, supplied scalar/carrier/domain, impossible array representation, or operation-specific static constraint.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: The exact required or next charged work exceeds maxWork or safe work representation.
errors.OUTPUT_LIMIT: Initial or proposed generation length exceeds maxTokens; no partial generation is returned.

behavior.validation: Exactly the input and nested-union keys shown by the schema, ordinary dense arrays and passive own data properties. Numeric carriers are finite binary64 and never booleans; integral fields are exact integers in schema domain. Reject accessors, host instances and coercion. Complete static validation of every field/element precedes work preflight, RNG draws or output allocation. Products defining array lengths must be exact and <=4294967295 or INVALID_INPUT, even if all individual dimensions are valid. Canonicalize input zeros to +0.
behavior.work: maxWork is a required nonnegative safe integer. Count arithmetic is exact; an unsafe work sum/product or insufficient allowance is WORK_LIMIT. A charge checks before its action; rejected actions do not execute. The operation-specific schedule is normative. Static input validation has unavoidable input-sized cost. Budgets are abstract work, not memory or latency guarantees; host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.numerics: Separate binary64 primitive rounding, no reassociation/FMA. Every computed primitive must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, including division by an underflowed zero denominator. No numerical repair, implicit epsilon or state clipping. Exposed zeros are +0. General finite output fields use absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; integer/topology/order/state/token values compare exactly. The bound fixture file contains only exact analytical outputs; approximate RK4 linear-field and nonzero-angle turtle geometry tests remain separate future property tests.
behavior.ownership: Read only caller inputs; output records and arrays are detached. No input record, array, RNG object, renderer, host state or callback is retained. All generated state remains private until success. No partial result on error; a successful RK4 boundary termination is its explicit retained-prefix result, not an error. Scalars and immutable strings are values.
behavior.tokens: A token is a nonempty string treated as one atomic symbol. Compare exact UTF-16 code-unit sequences with no Unicode normalization or character splitting. Rule/command token keys are unique; unknown tokens follow the operation-specific passthrough or unknown-token policy.
behavior.algorithm:
Parallel token grammar rewriting

Proposed ID: `grammar.parallel-token-rewrite`; transform.

Artist output: a rewritten token sequence reusable for substitution tile bands or
generation-stratified botanical text. Turtle interpretation is separate. No character
splitting, production probabilities, context sensitivity or symbol drawing is hidden.

Input:

```text
{axiom:[token,...], rules:[{symbol:token,replacement:[token,...]},...],
 iterations:integer in [0,4294967295], maxTokens:integer in [0,4294967295],
 maxWork:integer}
```

A token is a nonempty string compared by exact UTF-16 code-unit sequence, without Unicode
normalization. Rule symbols must be unique. Empty axiom, empty rules and empty replacement
are legal. Output `{tokens:[token,...]}`. An unmatched token passes through once. Each
generation reads only the previous generation, in order; replacements are not rewritten
again until the next generation. Zero iterations returns a detached axiom.

After static validation, atomically charge `W0=axiom.length+rules.length+sum(replacement.length)`
for setup, then fail OUTPUT_LIMIT if axiom exceeds maxTokens. Before each generation charge1,
including an empty generation. For each old token charge1 for its lookup; determine its
replacement/passthrough, check proposed new length<=maxTokens, then atomically charge its
output length before appending. OUTPUT_LIMIT precedes the emission charge for that token.
Work/storage follows total visited/emitted tokens, with at most two generations live.
String comparison/hashing additionally depends on token text lengths; maxWork is token-work,
not a character-processing or byte bound. It does not authorize retaining every generation.

behavior.algorithm:
Input {points,widths,initialNormal,maxWork}; >=2 3D points, widths length equal, finite nonnegative full
widths, finite normal. Output {positions,indices}. Reject zero adjacent segment, exact reversal (unit
tangent dot exactly -1), and initial normal parallel to first tangent. Endpoint tangent is adjacent unit
segment; interior tangent normalizes adjacent unit sum. Orthogonalize initial normal. Transport with minimal
Rodrigues rotation, axis=normalized cross, sin=|cross|, cos=dot; same-direction copies. After every
transport, reorthogonalize normal against current tangent and normalize; failure is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW.
Positions are point +/- (width/2)*normal; faces [L,R,Rnext],[L,Rnext,Lnext]. Closed seam is excluded.
Work=24N+6(N-1). Fixtures: x-axis, width2 -> y +/-1; right angle is finite/orthogonal.
Studies: flight ribbons; folded contour paper.

behavior.frame_rules: A supplied zero adjacent segment, adjacent unit directions with dot exactly -1, or zero projected initialNormal is INVALID_INPUT. Compute interior point tangents as normalized sums of adjacent unit directions. For each new tangent, cross(previousTangent,currentTangent) supplies axis and sine; cosine is their dot. Zero cross with positive dot copies normal; a zero-cross reversal is INVALID_INPUT. Rodrigues vector rotation is n*cos + (axis cross n)*sin + axis*(axis dot n)*(1-cos), evaluated left-to-right per component. Reproject n-currentTangent*(n dot currentTangent), normalize by Math.hypot; zero or nonfinite generated frame is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. Full widths produce plus first, minus second positions at each point; L=2*i,R=2*i+1. An input ending at its initial coordinate is still an open strip with independent endpoint frames; no seam closing/correction. Preflight output2*N positions and2*(N-1) faces.

behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. behavior.algorithm:
Input: bounds [minX,minY,maxX,maxY] with strict positive finite width/height,
radius (>0), attemptsPerActive (positive integer), maxPoints (nonnegative integer),
rngState (uint32), maxWork. Output: {points,rngState,exhausted}. Own local LCG32:
state=(1664525*state+1013904223) mod 2^32, each unit draw advances then divides
by 2^32. MaxPoints0 returns empty points, unchanged state, exhausted=false.
Otherwise first point consumes x then y draws and lies in the closed bounds (endpoint rounding is retained).
Maintain insertion-ordered points and active indices. Each active iteration
consumes one draw to select floor(u*active.length). Try candidates in order:
radius draw first, angle draw second; rho=radius*sqrt(1+3*u), angle=2*pi*v.
Candidate=activePoint+rho*[cos(angle),sin(angle)]. Reject outside closed
bounds or distance < radius from any point. Accept the first passing candidate,
append it to points and active list, then restart active selection. After all k
fail, remove selected active entry by swapping with last then popping. Stop at
maxPoints or empty active list. exhausted is true exactly when active is empty.

Use sparse uniform grid cells of radius/sqrt(2), searching dx/dy offsets -2..2
in y-major order. This is an acceleration only; candidate acceptance is identical
to a complete existing-point distance test. Reject cell-size underflow, or unsafe
integer cell coordinates with NUMERIC_OVERFLOW; no dense domain-sized allocation.
Charge one work unit per RNG draw, one per candidate, and one per actual existing
point distance comparison, before each event; maxWork exhaustion throws atomically.
Input validation/storage setup is O(N) in accepted points. Representation/finite
checks precede appending. Budget is explicit algorithm events, not time guarantee.

behavior.candidate_order: Charge the candidate event before its radius and angle draws. First-point coordinates are minX+u*width, minY+v*height, retaining closed-boundary endpoint rounding. Validate ordered bounds before maxPoints zero; compute checked width/height and positive represented cell size only when maxPoints>0. Point distance uses Math.hypot(dx,dy). Cell buckets retain point insertion order. Check neighboring cells in dy=-2..2 then dx=-2..2 order; charge each actual point comparison, stopping at first distance < radius. Selection uses floor(u*active.length). Output rngState is the final private LCG state. maxPoints zero has exhausted=false.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed passive carrier, finite/domain scalar or array correspondence.

errors.WORK_LIMIT: BigInt V+27F exceeds maxWork.

behavior.validation: Input is exactly required own string keys on an ordinary or null-prototype passive record, with dense ordinary arrays and own data slots only; no symbols, extra keys, accessors, coercion, defaults or retained aliases. Proxies are outside interchange. Validate positions, triangles and their in-range distinct integer corners, mode, groups, all UV triples/pairs, maxVertices and maxWork in schema order, fully before budget or geometry. V,F,nested lengths<=2147483647; groups are nonnegative safe integers; all coordinates finite; UV components in [0,1]. -0 canonicalizes to +0. Malformed carriers/scalars INVALID_INPUT; out-of-range, noninteger or repeated face corners INVALID_TOPOLOGY. Face indices must first be finite numeric scalars, otherwise INVALID_INPUT. Finite noninteger/out-of-range or repeated indices are INVALID_TOPOLOGY.
behavior.environment: Right-handed caller-local xyz. Triangle [i,j,k] has outward face normal (p_j-p_i)x(p_k-p_i). Supplied normalized corner UV convention u increases right, v increases down in an upright image; no host texture flip, implicit chart, winding repair, coordinate weld, material, light, renderer, asset, RNG, clock or mutable state in core.
behavior.native_surface: prepareSurfaceAttributes3D(input), PrepareSurfaceAttributes3DError with stable code. First target p5.js pure core and a private pinned-p5 Geometry study; no additional public renderer adapter is admitted.
behavior.order: After complete static validation, O=3F BigInt must be <=maxVertices (conservative flat/worst-smooth cap), else OUTPUT_LIMIT. W=V+27F BigInt must be <=maxWork, else WORK_LIMIT. Both before exact geometry or output allocation. Compute all face normals in face order. For each face, use exact dyadic source-coordinate differences/cross to test exact zero, DEGENERATE_FACE before rounded arithmetic. Then binary64 difference components ax,ay,az,bx,by,bz, each finite-checked; cross cx=ay*bz-az*by, cy=az*bx-ax*bz, cz=ax*by-ay*bx, checking each multiply/subtract. Nonfinite primitive NUMERIC_OVERFLOW; represented all-zero cross with exact nonzero cross REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE. Unitize using fdlibmHypot(fdlibmHypot(cx,cy),cz), then x/y/z division once, finite-checked and -0 canonicalized. In smooth mode, sum each incident unit face normal once by (source index,group), traversing faces ascending and corners 0,1,2, adding x/y/z in order with finite checks. Normalize group sums in first key-encounter order; all represented components zero AMBIGUOUS_NORMAL. Complete face/group normals before output expansion. Flat emits three new vertices per face. Smooth traverses corners in input order, reusing first encounter of (source index, group, exact canonical binary64 UV pair), with a single untextured sentinel when cornerUVs=null. Distinct UV pairs create seam twins with identical group normal; different source indices are never welded. Output triangles retain face/corner order, uvs null iff input null, and unreferenced input positions are omitted.
behavior.work: Deterministic full reservation V+27F with BigInt arithmetic; no runtime event charging or hidden quadratic weld scan. maxWork is nonnegative safe integer. Worst output vertices 3F must fit maxVertices<=2147483647 even when smooth reuse could reduce actual count. Time O(V+F) aside from exact arithmetic bit cost; storage O(V+F). Host allocation exhaustion remains host error.
behavior.numerics: Exact dyadic zero-cross topology test precedes binary64 cross; binary64 operations follow the stated primitive order with finite checks. fdlibmHypot is the pinned internal fdlibm algorithm for both nested magnitudes. General normal components compare with per-component absolute tolerance 1e-12, relative tolerance 0; topology, copied represented coordinates, UVs, axis normals, indices and errors compare exactly. A rounded all-zero smooth sum is AMBIGUOUS_NORMAL; no epsilon or arbitrary fallback.

operations.description: Project a periodic staggered velocity grid through a bounded weighted-Jacobi pressure solve.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed carrier, dimension, shape or parameter domain; validation before work.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Safe event budget exceeded before computation.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite arithmetic intermediate, no partial output.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype records and dense ordinary arrays; reject classes, accessors, symbols, extra keys, holes and coercion. All numbers finite binary64, integer fields safe. Validate every field and correspondence in schema order, then work preflight before arithmetic/output allocation. columns*rows must be safe <=4294967295 and each field array must have that length. No mutation, retained aliases or partial output; canonicalize output zero. Host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, renderer, assets or host state. Row-major periodic rectangular domain, cell spacing1, x right and y down. Scalar centers(x,y), u right face(x+.5,y), v lower face(x,y+.5). Velocity in cell units per caller time. Other targets deferred; no original artist recreation claim.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separate ordered primitives, every arithmetic intermediate checked finite (NUMERIC_OVERFLOW), no FMA/reassociation or epsilon. Exact analytical JSON fixtures; additional analytical comparisons abs1e-9+rel1e-12, topology/indices/errors exact. Modulo indices wrap positively. No convergence or mass conservation inferred from an image.
behavior.work: N*(iterations+3) cell events safely precharged; O(N*(iterations+1)) time,O(N) storage.
behavior.algorithm: D_i=(u_i-u_left)+(v_i-v_up). Initialize pressure to zero. For each iteration synchronously, row-major: sum=((p_left+p_right)+p_up)+p_down; target=(sum-D_i)/4; next=p_i+(2/3)*(target-p_i). After iterations u_i=old_u_i-(p_right-p_i), v_i=old_v_i-(p_down-p_i). Recompute divergence with same order. Pressure is velocity correction potential, not physical pressure. Return all detached arrays. Zero iterations preserves velocity; finite iteration count does not promise zero divergence.
