operations.description: Generate an owned indexed-triangle radial surface from a caller-supplied ordered local axial radius profile, angular subdivision, independent endpoint closures, and explicit face bound. It computes retained local geometry, topology metadata, and flat unit normals only.

profile.description: Ordered local [z,radius] pairs. z strictly increases; endpoint radii are nonnegative and interior radii are strictly positive. Only the two-point profile whose two endpoint radii are both zero is invalid; a P>=3 profile may have poles at both endpoints.

slices.description: Angular cell count. This upper value is a representational ceiling, not an encouraged resolution or allocation guarantee.

capStart.description: Request a fan cap at the first positive-radius profile ring. A zero-radius start pole already closes itself.

capEnd.description: Request a fan cap at the last positive-radius profile ring. A zero-radius end pole already closes itself.

maxFaces.description: Required caller face-work limit. Its maximum is a signed-int packed-representation ceiling, not a practical-work or artistic recommendation.

positions.description: Owned local [x,y,z] vertex positions in canonical profile-ring/pole then cap-centre order.

normals.description: Owned local flat unit [x,y,z] normals aligned one-to-one with triangles.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, profile length below2, non-increasing axial coordinate, endpoint negative radius, nonpositive interior radius, the two-point profile with both endpoint radii zero, slices outside3..715827881, nonboolean cap, or maxFaces outside1..715827881.
errors.FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Complete static input is valid but exact preallocation face count F exceeds required maxFaces. No geometry/RNG/output allocation or partial result occurs.
errors.MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Generated face has nonfinite edge component, zero edge scale, or zero rounded scaled cross. error_detail has faceIndex and edge,edge_scale,or cross_scale stage; no output is returned.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside the requested retained array range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: An Into destination/offset does not provide three writable slots of the required native element type.

errorOrder: INVALID_INPUT during complete static input validation
FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED after static validation and exact count calculation, before geometry allocation
MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID during canonical face-normal traversal after topology/positions are generated
INVALID_INDEX, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, INVALID_OUTPUT during retained-result access in that order

behavior.input: Input has exactly profile,slices,capStart,capEnd,maxFaces. Static validation order is outer passive record/exact keys; profile outer List and length; each profile pair in increasing list order, pair shape then z then radius, including z monotonicity and endpoint/interior radius constraints; the special two-point/both-poles rejection; slices; capStart; capEnd; maxFaces. Every accepted number is finite binary64 and never bool. Integral slices/maxFaces carriers validate their stated domains before narrowing. Normalize accepted zeros to +0. No sort, resampling, implicit profile, callback, default, or later-field short circuit. Complete static validation, including unused later profile rows, precedes count capacity, allocation and geometry.
behavior.counts_and_layout: Let P=profile length, S=slices, K=number of positive-radius profile points, Z=number of endpoint poles, and C=number of requested caps whose endpoint ring is positive. V=K*S+Z+C. Each positive-to-positive side band emits2*S triangles; each pole-adjacent side band emitsS; each requested positive-ring cap emitsS. Compute F with exact wide integer arithmetic after static validation and before geometry allocation. FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if F>maxFaces. The accepted count proof in design/operations/cp7-count-bounds.md establishes V<=F+1 for the admitted domain, including P>=3 double-pole profiles; P<=2147483647 and S,maxFaces<=715827881 keep count expressions within signed64 arithmetic and retained triples addressable by signed-int packed storage. These values do not guarantee allocation success, latency, or a useful artistic range. Host resource allocation failure returns no result and is never INVALID_INPUT or partial success. Core retained work/storage is O(P*S), indexed reads O(1), detached export O(F+V).
behavior.topology: Local axis is Z. Angles increase from +X toward +Y. Set TAU=6.283185307179586 and evaluate theta=(TAU*cell)/slices in that order; position=(radius*cos(theta),radius*sin(theta),z) using named-target binary64 trigonometry. Positive rings append S vertices in input-profile then increasing-cell order. A zero-radius endpoint appends exactly one (0,0,z) pole; no 2pi seam vertex is evaluated or stored. Append requested cap centres after all profile positions, start before end. Visit side bands in input order then cells increasing with next=(cell+1) moduloS. Ordinary positive-ring cell appends (a,b,c),(a,c,d), where a=lower/current,b=lower/next,c=upper/next,d=upper/current. Start-pole cell appends (pole,upper/next,upper/current); end-pole cell appends (lower/current,lower/next,pole). After sides, start fans append (centre,ring/next,ring/current), then end fans (centre,ring/current,ring/next). Side winding is outward; start/end cap winding faces -Z/+Z. Face kinds use side,start-cap,end-cap; side bands identify the lower profile index and caps use band=-1.
behavior.normals: For each ordered triangle(a,b,c) after positions/topology are generated, calculate u=b-a and v=c-a componentwise in x/y/z order. Reject a nonfinite edge component with MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID stage edge. Let su=max(abs(ux),abs(uy),abs(uz)) and sv likewise; reject zero su or sv at stage edge_scale. Divide every u component directly by su and every v component directly by sv. Compute qRaw=cross(uScaled,vScaled) through separate binary64 multiply/subtract operations in x/y/z order, no FMA or reassociation. Let sn=max(abs(qRaw.x),abs(qRaw.y),abs(qRaw.z)); reject zero sn at stage cross_scale. Divide qRaw directly by sn, then length=sqrt((qx*qx+qy*qy)+qz*qz); normal=q/length componentwise. Canonicalize completed zeros. No epsilon, analytic profile normal, binary32 narrowing, smooth interpolation, or silent dropped face is permitted. Dynamic failure returns no result and carries faceIndex/stage. The selected algorithm avoids demonstrated direct cross/norm overflow but does not claim all-finite robustness.
behavior.ownership: Result stores packed owned primitive data and never retains caller record/profile containers. Inputs are passive immutable interchange during eager generation. Result is immutable. vertexAt,triangleAt,normalAt return fresh triples; faceKindAt,bandAt,cellAt and counts are direct retained reads; toValues deep-copies exactly output_schema. vertexInto,triangleInto,normalInto validate all access and destination conditions before three writes; failure leaves destination unchanged and successful writes leave slots outside the target triple unchanged. Materialization allocation failure does not corrupt retained data. No config serialization/replay, aliases, callbacks, iterator inputs, or draw side effect.
behavior.access: vertexCount() and faceCount() return retained counts. vertexAt, triangleAt and normalAt return fresh three-element carriers; faceKindAt, bandAt and cellAt return aligned scalar data. Index must be finite safe nonnegative integer<=9007199254740991 and never bool; integral floating indices are accepted by dynamic-language targets. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT for vertexInto, triangleInto and normalInto. Each Into offset is finite safe nonnegative integral and the destination provides three writable slots of its required native element type: binary64 for vertex/normal, integer for triangle. Rejected reads leave every destination slot unchanged; success leaves slots outside the target triple unchanged. Java uses typed required int offsets and returns void; wrong/unrepresentable typed Java calls are host-call errors. JavaScript returns its destination and Python returns None. Deferred target bindings follow native_forms and native_types; no support is claimed before implementation and native validation.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.mesh.RadialProfile3D.generate(Object config) returns RadialProfile3D with vertexCount(), faceCount(), vertexAt(Object or long), triangleAt(Object or long), normalAt(Object or long), faceKindAt(Object or long), bandAt(Object or long), cellAt(Object or long), vertexInto(Object or long,double[],int), triangleInto(Object or long,int[],int), normalInto(Object or long,double[],int), and toValues(). No aliases, presets, callbacks, iterator forms or configuration serializer are proposed. Deferred JavaScript bindings use the same camelCase member names; Python uses vertex_count, face_count, vertex_at, triangle_at, normal_at, face_kind_at, band_at, cell_at, vertex_into, triangle_into, normal_into and to_values. Factory export/module locations are deferred target packaging decisions, not extra operation semantics. All targets remain unimplemented and unvalidated.
behavior.native_types: Follow the existing retained-operation passive-carrier convention: Java accepts Map outer records and passive List profile/pair containers with the stated exact lengths; accepted Java numeric carriers are only Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float and Double, rejecting BigInteger, BigDecimal and custom Number before conversion. Java At/Into numeric index overloads accept Object or long as listed; Java vertexInto/normalInto require double[] and triangleInto requires int[]. Deferred JavaScript accepts passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Arrays; Python accepts exact builtin dict/list with int/float but never bool. JavaScript vertex/normal destinations are Float64Array or writable ordinary Array; triangle destinations are Int32Array or writable ordinary Array. Python vertex/normal destinations are exact builtin list or array(d); triangle destinations are exact builtin list. Destination validation must precede writes, including writable-slot checks for ordinary JavaScript Arrays. Host geometry/renderer carriers, native typed-array input pairs, class instances, active getters/proxies and custom dynamic-language mapping/list containers are outside portable interchange. Java input List/Map implementations must be passive; no callback or concurrent mutation semantics are promised.
behavior.units: Caller-defined local Cartesian distance units. Positions use [x,y,z] with +Z along supplied axial order and angular coordinates around Z from +X toward +Y. No canvas mapping, camera, object transform, clipping, style, palette, lighting setup, renderer, shader, texture, callback, preset, or drawing command is part of generation.
behavior.numerics: Specified basic arithmetic is IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even with separate operation rounding. TAU is the stated binary64 literal. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion, RNG, host global state, implicit epsilon, smoothing or coordinate clamp. Input and completed output zeros canonicalize to +0. Topology, counts, face metadata, indices and same-runtime binary64 output bits compare exactly. Cross-runtime fixture positions and normals compare with a separately generated nonnegative absolute allowance per component and case. Zero allowances require exact reference bits; exported zero is always positive zero. Bounds derive from reference sin/cos widened by two adjacent binary64 values each way (clipped to [-1,1], theta zero exact) and interval propagation through specified arithmetic. Inconclusive bounds block fixture acceptance; no global epsilon, relative fallback or automatic expansion. This selected-case engineering envelope is not a universal host-trigonometry guarantee. Near-collapse arbitrary inputs can differ in success/error across runtimes; registered error witnesses must match exact code, faceIndex and stage. Same-target/runtime repeated generation matches retained bits, without requiring Python reference bits for nonzero-allowance values.

Java/Android Math.sin, Math.cos and Math.sqrt; JavaScript Math.sin, Math.cos and Math.sqrt; Python math.sin, math.cos and math.sqrt. No implicit angle reduction.
behavior.complexity: O(P*S) eager retained geometry and face-normal generation, O(1) indexed reads, and O(V+F) detached export. Avoid per-face object/vector allocation in generation or ordinary drawing loops. The representational ceiling is not a memory or throughput promise.
behavior.native_errors: Static/access errors expose stable code. MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID also exposes faceIndex and stage, serialized as error_detail:{faceIndex,stage}. FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED has no partial result. Host allocation/resource failure remains a host resource exception and is not converted to validation error. No renderer/adapter result is produced by core generation.

guide.title: Revolve a profile into a surface
guide.summary: Create a retained mesh from a radial profile and angular slices.
guide.useWhen: Use it when a silhouette should become editable 3D geometry.

inputs.profile: At least two `[z, radius]` pairs describing a silhouette around the Z axis. Z must strictly increase. Interior radii must be positive; either endpoint can have radius 0 to form a pole. Two zero-radius endpoints alone cannot form a surface.
inputs.slices: Integer number of sections around the axis, at least 3. Increasing it refines the circular direction; add profile points to refine the silhouette along Z.
inputs.capStart: Boolean requesting a flat cap when the first profile radius is positive. A zero-radius start pole already closes the surface.
inputs.capEnd: Boolean requesting a flat cap when the last profile radius is positive. A zero-radius end pole already closes the surface.
inputs.maxFaces: Positive integer triangle budget covering the side bands and requested caps. If the mesh would exceed it, generation fails without publishing partial geometry.

guide.output: vertexAt(index) returns local [x,y,z], triangleAt(face) returns vertex indices, and normalAt(face) returns a face normal. Loop faceCount(), call p.beginShape(p.TRIANGLES), emit its indexed vertices, then p.endShape(); toValues() is detached geometry, not a rendered view.
guide.tryThis: In p5 WEBGL, call `p.normal(...mesh.normalAt(face))` before emitting the indexed vertices of each triangle. Add your own camera, lights and material; this operation only supplies geometry.

operations.description: Immutable ordered radial influences that sum inward power-profile displacements at the original point; may fold and self-intersect geometry.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed constructor, unsupported carrier/nonfinite value or nonpositive radius/power.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Malformed/nonfinite query or wrong target array.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite contribution, accumulated displacement or final point; no partial target writes.

behavior.identity: Immutable detached ordered influence descriptor; empty identity, exact-center zero, duplicate contributions retained.
behavior.numerics: Separately rounded binary64; named fdlibm5.3 hypot/pow; original-query contributions summed in order then added once. Infinite separation is outside finite radius; nonfinite sum/output fails atomically.
behavior.native: RadialPull2D.create(Object/double[][]), serialize, influenceCount, transform(Object), transform(double,double), transform(double,double,double[]); see normative contract.
behavior.complexity: O(N) setup/storage and query work; reusable target hot path allocation-free.

guide.title: Pull points radially
guide.summary: Build an influence model that displaces points around radial controls.
guide.useWhen: Use it to warp your own geometry without touching its topology.

inputs.influences: Ordered `[centerX, centerY, radius, power]` tuples. Radius and power must be positive. Points inside each radius receive an inward displacement whose falloff uses (distance/radius)^power. Larger power increases that pull at a fixed interior distance. Contributions use the original point and add together; overlapping pulls may fold geometry.

guide.output: transform([x,y]) returns a local [x,y] pair; transform(x,y) returns {x,y}. Apply it once per vertex before your drawing call; serialize() copies influence data.
guide.code:
const pull = radialPull2D({ influences: [[0, 0, 10, 2]] });
console.log(pull.transform(5, 0));
guide.tryThis: Apply the model to each point before drawing a shape.

operations.description: Enumerate all unordered point-index pairs within an inclusive Euclidean radius using a deterministic x sweep.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Carrier, shape or finite-domain failure before work.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Next event exceeds maxWork, no partial output.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype record; no classes, accessors, symbols, extras or coercion. Dense ordinary arrays with own data slots and no extras; proxies outside interchange. Point arrays contain finite binary64 pairs, length at most2147483647. Canonicalize accepted zero values. Validate all fields and correspondence in input-schema order before work checks, including empty/identity cases. No input mutation or aliasing; all output arrays and pairs detached.
behavior.work: After static validation charge N events before sorting/output; then one event per unordered pair whose rounded absolute x difference<=radius, including y/distance rejections. Charge candidate before y/hypot arithmetic. If next event exceeds maxWork, WORK_LIMIT, no partial result. Sorting/static validation are not budget events. O(N log N+C+K log K), O(N+K) storage; C may be N(N-1)/2 for vertical or dense points. Budget behavior depends on orientation.
behavior.algorithm: Sort indices by ascending point x with original index tie break (compare values, do not use subtraction as comparator). For each sorted index a visit subsequent sorted indices b ascending. Compute dx=x[b]-x[a]; if dx>radius break (positive infinity is an outside screen). Otherwise charge candidate; compute dy=abs(y[b]-y[a]); if dy>radius skip, including infinity. If radius==0 accept only exact x and y equality. Otherwise accept iff existing fdlibmHypot(dx,dy)<=radius; an infinite hypot is outside. Store [min(originalA,originalB),max(...)]. Sort output pairs lexicographically by integer indices.
behavior.numerics: Binary64 primitive rounding, no FMA, no epsilon. fdlibmHypot is the existing audited profile in packages/javascript/src/internal/fdlibm-hypot.js (including its subnormal correction). Topology compares exactly under that profile, not abstract exact-real geometry. Input numbers finite; subtraction/hypot infinity is allowed only as an outside screen.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, renderer, wrapping, domain, persistent index or hidden identity. Coordinate units arbitrary consistent Cartesian units; query independent of axis handedness.
behavior.native_surface: radiusPairs2D(input), RadiusPairs2DError from radius-pairs-2d.js and package index.

guide.title: Find nearby point pairs
guide.summary: Connect nearby marks while keeping their positions and drawing treatment separate.
guide.useWhen: Use the returned pairs to draw a proximity network or drive the pair-force step.

inputs.points: Finite [x,y] positions. Array indices identify the points for this call.
inputs.radius: Inclusive distance threshold in the same units as the positions; zero finds exact coincidences.
inputs.maxWork: Budget for one event per point plus every pair in the x-distance window. Dense or vertical sets can still need quadratic work.

guide.output: {pairs}: detached [i,j] indices, i<j, in strict lexicographic order. There is no self-pair or duplicate.
guide.code:
const result = radiusPairs2D({points:[[0,0],[3,4],[20,0]],radius:5,maxWork:6});
console.log(result.pairs);
guide.tryThis: Change the radius without changing the positions, then draw the same pair list with a different mark or opacity.
pitfalls: Indices do not retain identity after insertion or reordering.
There is no wrapping, collision resolution or persistent contact state.
A deterministic x sweep can still be quadratic for vertical point sets.

operations.description: Crossfade two same-sized straight ARGB8 rasters using explicit per-pixel weights and premultiplied working channels.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong shapes/carriers, dimensions/products, unequal raster dimensions, pixel counts/values, weights count/nonfinite/outside [0,1], null typed buffers.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Pixel index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Pixel index is representable but outside the retained output raster.

errorOrder: Follow behavior.validation; all configuration failures INVALID_INPUT.

behavior.input: Exactly first,second,weights. Both rasters have exactly width,height,pixels; positive integral dimensions with equal sizes, unsigned32 pixels, exact counts. Weights finite binary64 [0,1]. No defaults.
behavior.compositing: For each pixel, w==0 copies first packed bits, w==1 copies second packed bits. Otherwise compute t=1.0-w; af=firstAlpha/255.0; as=secondAlpha/255.0; u=af*t; v=as*w; a=u+v. If a==0 output transparent black without division. Let Q(x)=floor(min(255,max(0,x))+0.5). Compute output alpha Q(a*255.0); if it is zero return transparent black. For each encoded RGB byte pair f,s: p=f*u; q=s*v; c=(p+q)/a; output channel Q(c). Each arithmetic step separately rounded IEEE binary64 ties-to-even; no FMA, reassociation or gamma conversion. Endpoint identity precedes normalization of transparent black, preserving hidden RGB.
behavior.ownership: Completed result owns detached packed pixels, retaining neither input nor weights. No in-place form. Failed call exposes no partial output; later caller mutation cannot affect the result.
behavior.access: width() and height() return dimensions. pixelAt(index) validates index as a finite safe nonnegative integer, then checks index < width*height; INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pixels() returns a detached int[] in Java (unsigned32 bit patterns), and toValues() returns detached {width,height,pixels}. Safe means at most 9007199254740991; negative zero is accepted as zero. pixelAt returns the Java int ARGB bit pattern; portable toValues pixels are unsigned32 numbers. Object indices accept only the same six numeric carriers as input.
behavior.numeric: Ordered binary64 arithmetic with final byte quantization as stated. Premultiplied working encoded RGB; no linear-light claim. Negative-zero weight equals zero.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.raster.RasterCrossfade2D.mix(Object) and mix(int width,int height,int[] first,int[] second,double[] weights); result width(),height(),pixelAt(Object or long),pixels(),toValues(). Implementation pending.
behavior.environment: No RNG, time, noise, host image, renderer, callback or mutable global state.
behavior.limits: width*height <= 2147483647, checked without signed32 overflow before allocation. Representation limit only; allocation failure is not INVALID_INPUT. O(width*height) time and owned output storage; no per-pixel allocation in typed kernel.
behavior.carriers: Object records are exact-key Map, arrays List. Numeric values accept only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double; reject boolean, strings, BigInteger,BigDecimal, arbitrary Number subclasses. Dimensions and pixels integral within schema bounds, weight converts to finite double. Typed buffers non-null. Passive stable inputs required; concurrent input mutation outside contract.
behavior.validation: Object: exact top keys; first raster keys/dimensions/product/pixel count then values; second keys/dimensions/product/matching dimensions/pixel count then values; weights count then values. Typed: dimensions/product; first count; second count; weights count then values. All validation before output allocation. All input failures INVALID_INPUT.

guide.title: Crossfade two rasters
guide.summary: Blend matching rasters with explicit per-pixel weights.
guide.useWhen: Use it for a calculated transition rather than a renderer blend mode.

inputs.first: A plain `{width, height, pixels}` object. Width and height are positive pixel counts; `pixels` contains exactly width × height unsigned `0xAARRGGBB` integers in row order. Convert p5.Image RGBA channels to this packed format first.
inputs.second: The second raster, with the same dimensions and packed pixel format as first. Neither input raster is modified.
inputs.weights: One finite 0–1 value per pixel in row order. Zero selects first, one selects second, and intermediate values blend their alpha and premultiplied color. Use a constant array for a uniform fade or varying weights for a spatial transition.

guide.output: pixelAt(index) and pixels() return packed unsigned ARGB8/AARRGGBB values; toValues().pixels is detached data rather than p5 RGBA channels.
guide.tryThis: Create `const image = p.createImage(raster.width, raster.height)` and call `image.loadPixels()`. Convert each packed ARGB32 pixel to RGBA slots: for pixel i, write red `(pixel >>> 16) & 255`, green `(pixel >>> 8) & 255`, blue `pixel & 255`, alpha `pixel >>> 24` at `image.pixels[4*i…4*i+3]`, then call `image.updatePixels()` and draw it with `p.image(image, 0, 0)`.

operations.description: Evaluate a bounded typed implicit scene along explicit CPU rays and return primary hit or miss records.

finite.x-binary64: finite; negative zero normalized to positive zero

sceneNode.x-constraint: root depth 1; at most 64 nodes on any root-to-leaf path; no cycles or shared object identities in scene records or arrays

finite.x-binary64: finite; negative zero normalized to positive zero

overshot.x-constraint: true only for a later negative field sample classified hit_epsilon

samples.x-constraint: primary field evaluations, including t=0 and boundary; at most maxSteps

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Unsupported or malformed passive carrier, scene tag/shape/identity, scalar domain, ray direction, extra/missing field, accessor, or array correspondence. Proxy behavior is outside portable interchange.
errors.LIMIT_DEPTH: Scene root-to-leaf depth exceeds64 during static preorder traversal.
errors.LIMIT_RAYS: After full static validation, rays.length exceeds maxRays.
errors.LIMIT_SCENE_NODES: After full static validation and ray cap, scene node count exceeds maxSceneNodes.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: After caps, exact BigInt R*(S+6)*N exceeds maxWork.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: After work reservation, a checked computed binary64 ray, field, advance, offset, gradient or normalization primitive is nonfinite, or a nonzero input direction has zero/nonfinite represented norm.

errorOrder: INVALID_INPUT or LIMIT_DEPTH at first static fault

behavior.validation: Top-level exact fields in schema order, then scene preorder left-before-right and rays in input order. Ordinary/null-prototype passive records and dense ordinary arrays with exact own data slots only; no accessors, symbols, extra fields, coercion, defaults, or retained aliases. Valid plain data invoke no user callback. Proxies are outside interchange because JavaScript reflection may invoke their traps; no universal Proxy rejection/code/no-side-effect claim. Complete supported static validation before caps or work. Scene identity graph must be a tree with no shared scene record or coordinate array and no cycle; root depth1, depth<=64. Static first fault is INVALID_INPUT or LIMIT_DEPTH. All input numbers finite binary64; zero canonicalized; direction not all zero; all positive fields strictly positive. Then LIMIT_RAYS, LIMIT_SCENE_NODES, WORK_LIMIT. Every later nonfinite computed result is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW; no partial output.
behavior.environment: Right-handed world xyz; distances, radii, extents, k, epsilon and normalStep share world units. Explicit rays; no camera, material, light, raster, host callback, RNG, time, GPU, asset, global state, or default scene.
behavior.native_surface: Pure raymarchImplicitRays3D(input) with RaymarchImplicitRays3DError.code. CPU primary hit records only; a future pinned-p5 example may rasterize those records without adding shader or mesh extraction to this operation.
behavior.field: H3(x,y,z)=fdlibmHypot(fdlibmHypot(x,y),z). Sphere q=p-center; d=H3(q)-radius. AxisBox q_i=abs(p_i-center_i)-halfExtents_i; outside=H3(max(q_i,0)); inside=min(max(q_x,max(q_y,q_z)),0); d=outside+inside. Union=min(a,b), intersection=max(a,b), difference=max(a,-b), left on exact ties. SmoothUnion: delta=a-b checked; absDelta=abs(delta); if absDelta>=k return hard min left-tied. Else h=1-absDelta/k, m=min(a,b) left-tied, d=m-(((k*h)*h)/4), with each primitive checked. TranslateUniform p_i=(p_i-translation_i)/scale, then scale*dChild. Both children of a binary node evaluate left then right even where a winner is known.
behavior.trace: Normalize every nonzero ray direction in input order with H3 and component division after work reservation. Trace rays in input order. Initial point is captured origin; later p_i=origin_i+(t*unit_i) with product and sum checked separately. At each primary sample increment samples. Initial negative d=>inside_start; otherwise d<=hitEpsilon=>hit_epsilon, with overshot true iff a later sample is negative. Positive outside-epsilon sample: if t===maxDistance miss_range; else if samples===maxSteps miss_steps; else remaining=maxDistance-t; if d>remaining miss_range; else next=maxDistance when d===remaining, otherwise checked t+d; next===t miss_stalled; next>maxDistance miss_range; otherwise sample next. Exact boundary is sampled once. No unsampled boundary or root interpolation.
behavior.normal: Base field carries conservative nonsmooth flag: sphere center; axisBox with all q_i<=0 and tied maximum or selected center axis; hard CSG equal-operand tie or selected child; smoothUnion propagates both children inside absDelta<k, selected child otherwise; transform passes child. On a hit with nonsmooth flag return null/undefined_nonsmooth and normalSamples0. Otherwise evaluate p+normalStep and p-normalStep for x,y,z in that order, exactly six field samples. g_i=((fPlus-fMinus)/normalStep)/2, checked after each primitive. H3(g)==0 returns null/undefined_zero; otherwise normalize each component with H3(g) and status estimated. Nonfinite arithmetic is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, not undefined. Miss normal null/not_applicable/0.
behavior.order: All field operations are binary64 nearest-even in the stated order with no FMA or reassociation, finite checked after each primitive, computed -0 canonicalized. At a hit, distance=traveled=t, position and fieldValue are the last sampled values. At a miss, distance=null, with traveled, position and fieldValue still from the last actual primary sample. The same ten result keys appear for every ray; results preserve ray order and own detached storage.
behavior.work: Let R=rays.length, S=maxSteps, N=scene node count. Preflight BigInt W=BigInt(R)*(BigInt(S)+6n)*BigInt(N), requiring W<=BigInt(maxWork) before ray normalization or field evaluation. Each primary sample and each normal offset evaluates all N nodes, no short circuit; at most S+6 samples per ray. maxRays and maxSceneNodes are safe integers, depth hard64. Output size O(R), evaluation O(R*S*N) aside from fdlibm and host allocation. Host allocation exhaustion is not recoded as a semantic partial result.
behavior.numerics: Sphere/axisBox are exact real 1-Lipschitz signed distances; hard CSG and polynomial smooth union are sign-correct 1-Lipschitz fields for their resulting zero sets, not generally exact Euclidean distances. In smooth transition when a<=b, partial weights are 1-h/2 and h/2, nonnegative and summing to1; symmetric case swaps them. Positive exact field is a conservative zero-set distance lower bound. Binary64 rounding, finite hitEpsilon, finite sample count, and potential underflow/overshoot remove any exact root or thin-feature guarantee. Structural/status/count/overshot and all exact-fixture numerics compare exactly; only two named numeric fixture cases have per-field tolerances.

guide.title: Query blended and cut volumes
guide.summary: Return bounded CPU hit records for rays through a typed sphere, box and CSG scene.
guide.useWhen: You want to inspect an implicit form's silhouette, cut, surface depth or estimated normal with explicit rays.

inputs.scene: A passive tree of sphere/axisBox leaves, union/intersection/difference/smoothUnion nodes and positive-uniform transforms.
inputs.rays: Ordered world-space origin/direction pairs. Directions are normalized by the operation.
inputs.maxDistance: Positive world-space travel limit; an exact reached endpoint is sampled once.
inputs.hitEpsilon: Positive approximate-hit threshold in world units.
inputs.normalStep: Positive central-difference offset for six extra field samples on a smooth hit.
inputs.maxSteps: Maximum primary field samples per ray, including the initial sample.
inputs.maxSceneNodes: Typed scene-node count cap; tree depth is separately limited to 64.
inputs.maxWork: Exact reservation R × (maxSteps + 6) × scene nodes before tracing.

guide.output: {results}: one detached hit/miss record per ray with sampled travel and position, field value, optional normal, overshoot flag and sample counts.
guide.tryThis: Widen the subtracting box or replace it with a sphere, then shade the returned normals with a separate light and camera choice.
pitfalls: Finite steps and epsilon do not certify an exact surface intersection or every thin feature.
A sharp corner or CSG tie can return an undefined normal; the operation does not produce a mesh or GPU image.

operations.description: Classify two strict regions and return their closest boundary witness and display distance.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed carrier, domain or static correspondence.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Exact declared event reservation exceeds maxWork.
errors.INVALID_REGION: Input rings or hole relationships invalid.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite required arithmetic/display output.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Required distinct exact geometry cannot be represented distinctly.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype records, dense ordinary arrays with own data slots, no extras/accessors/symbols/coercion; finite binary64 inputs. Validate full carrier/domain before budget. Proxies outside interchange. Every ring has >=3 distinct vertices, implicit closure, nonzero signed area, no duplicate seam/vertex, adjacent backtracking, self-contact, or self-crossing. Holes are strictly inside outer and pairwise disjoint/non-touching. Either winding input; owned output outer CCW/hole CW. Filled membership is outer minus holes. Static validation checks shape/domain, including strip duplicate/reversal rules; exact region topology follows work preflight. Hatch projection/count arithmetic is needed before its budget as explicitly specified. Errors atomic, no mutation/aliases; output zeros positive. Work sums/products use exact integers and compare before allocation; runtime/allocation guarantees do not follow from budgets.
behavior.algorithm: Validate both Regions after preflight. In exact dyadic arithmetic, scan a rings/edges then b rings/edges for first contact/crossing; if none, test filled-set containment in a then b order, considering holes. Boundary contact and overlap are INTERSECTS with null minimumDistance. For DISJOINT, enumerate all boundary edge pairs in supplied input ring/edge order; compute exact rational squared endpoint-to-segment distances, clamping exact projection to [0,1]. Select least exact squared distance; ties by aRing,aEdge,bRing,bEdge, then endpoint/projection test order. Round the selected exact closest-point pair coordinates independently to nearest-even binary64, subtract components in binary64, and return Math.hypot(dx,dy), canonicalizing zero. This display value is not guaranteed to be correctly rounded from the exact distance and never decides selection. Nonfinite display is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. All query witnesses index the supplied rings/edges without reordering or winding normalization; disjoint closest-vector rounding to zero is permitted as a display value only, never relation or selection authority.
behavior.work: Let E(R)=total ring edges and Q(R)=1+holes.length. VR(R)=E(R)^2+8*E(R)*Q(R)+4*Q(R)^2. W=VR(a)+VR(b)+12*E(a)*E(b)+E(a)+E(b), exact nonnegative integer; WORK_LIMIT iff W>maxWork before topology.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, host renderer, file IO or implicit assets. Consistent caller coordinate units; SVG input explicitly millimetres. Other targets deferred.
behavior.numerics: Topology and clearance thresholds use exact rational arithmetic on supplied binary64 dyadics. Constructed offsets and stated display arithmetic use ordered binary64 with finite checks; no epsilon, snap or repair. Exact shared JSON vectors; additional analytic shape tests compare declared floating arithmetic abs1e-9+rel1e-12 while topology/IDs/order remain exact. Optional outer miter failure falls back exactly as specified.
behavior.native_surface: regionClearance2D(input), named p5-package export with stable-code errors.

guide.title: Measure room between filled regions
guide.summary: Check whether shaped marks overlap, touch or leave a visible gap.
guide.useWhen: Compare complete outer rings and holes rather than only their centerlines.

inputs.a: First strict Region2D: outer ring and disjoint, strictly contained holes.
inputs.b: Second strict Region2D in the same coordinates.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit computation budget. See the operation contract for its event formula; this is not a millisecond limit.

guide.output: {relation,minimumDistance,witness}: classification and deterministic geometry indices; minimumDistance is null for intersecting filled regions, otherwise the boundary distance.
guide.code:
const result = regionClearance2D({"a":{"outer":[[0,0],[2,0],[2,2],[0,2]],"holes":[]},"b":{"outer":[[5,0],[7,0],[7,2],[5,2]],"holes":[]},"maxWork":10000});
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Move a mark near a hole and compare the filled-region result with a centerline-only intuition.
pitfalls: Rings must be simple; touching or nested holes are unsupported.
The result does not repair geometry or choose a new placement.

operations.description: An immutable row-major rectangular sequence of planar positions with explicit point counts and spacing.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong shape, unknown/missing keys, invalid numeric type/domain, nonfinite component, count outside representable domain.
errors.COORDINATE_OVERFLOW: Nonempty last-coordinate multiply or add is nonfinite.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index not a finite safe nonnegative integer (booleans excluded).
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index representation but index >= size.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: Optional native pointInto storage/offset is not writable binary64-capable space for two coordinates.

behavior.construction: Validate shape/type/domain in field order origin, spacing, columns, rows (vector x before y), then exact count product, then nonempty last coordinate x before y. Copy values, canonicalize all zero origins/counts to +0. Return immutable sequence; size computed, never serialized. No output-sized allocation.
behavior.sequence: size=columns*rows. i in [0,size): column=i modulo columns; row=(i-column)/columns, exact integer arithmetic. x changes fastest.
behavior.point: For each axis separately, product=roundBinary64(axisIndex*spacing); coordinate=roundBinary64(origin+product). No FMA or repeated addition. Normalize coordinate zero to +0.
behavior.empty: Either count zero gives size zero and no valid index. Validate input spacing regardless. Do not evaluate endpoint arithmetic for empty results.
behavior.coordinate_validation: For nonempty grids evaluate the last x and last y with the specified separate operations. A nonfinite product or sum rejects construction before output. Finite rounding may collapse adjacent positions at large magnitudes.
behavior.ownership: Immutable sequence detached from input arrays. Semantic pointAt(index) returns a fresh two-number binary64 value. Optional native pointInto(index,out,offset) writes exactly two coordinates after all validation. Invalid access leaves storage unchanged. Internal fields never alias writable output storage.
behavior.native_storage: Native-only optional optimization: pointInto accepts writable binary64-capable storage, with integral nonnegative offset and room for two values. Index type/domain then bounds then storage/offset validation. float32/PVector buffers are forbidden for this exact route. This is transport, not a second operation or serialized shape.

behavior.algorithm:
RK4 traces through an explicit vector grid

Proposed ID: `path.rk4-vector-grid-trace-2d`; transform/generator.

Artist output: a retained path following a supplied velocity field. This adds vector-grid
sampling and fourth-order integration to the existing fixed-step gradient-heading trace.
Studies: vortex streamlines; ribbons steered through a separately authored obstacle field.
The obstacle solver is not supplied by this operation and must not be hidden in its study.

Input:

```text
{vectors:[[number,number],...], columns:integer>=2, rows:integer>=2,
 origin:[number,number], spacing:[positive,positive], start:[number,number],
 dt:number>=0, steps:integer in [0,4294967294],
 boundary:"CLAMP"|"STOP", maxWork:integer}
```

Output: `{points:[[x,y],...], completedSteps:integer, termination:"STEPS"|"BOUNDARY"}`.
The first point is always the supplied start; point count is completedSteps+1. Velocity
components use caller distance per time unit; dt uses the matching time unit. No tangent,
normalization, adaptive integration, obstacles or closed-path detection is included.

Reserve `W=G+17*steps+1` before coordinate construction or trace storage. The allowance
accounts for four four-corner field samples plus one append per requested step, even if
STOP ends early. O(G+steps) work and retained storage; the output contains only accepted
steps. Construct `maxX=origin.x+(C-1)*hx`, `maxY=origin.y+(R-1)*hy` with checked arithmetic,
including for zero steps. The domain is that closed rectangle.
If either represented maximum is <= its origin, raise GRID_COLLAPSE: positive supplied
spacing did not produce a representable positive overall extent. This is distinct from
nonfinite arithmetic and is included in this proposal after root boundary review.

Sampler S(p): STOP returns the boundary signal when p is outside; CLAMP clamps only the
query coordinate, never the retained path point. Thus CLAMP traces may leave the rectangle.
Compute fractional grid coordinates after the boundary policy as (query-origin)/spacing,
then clamp these fractions to [0,C-1]/[0,R-1] to bound division-rounding excursions.
Use floor indices, except the final grid line uses the preceding cell with local
coordinate 1; exact query==represented maximum also selects that endpoint rule.
The uniform-grid arithmetic is specified this way rather than inferring distinct rounded
physical coordinates for every interior grid line. For each component, let a,b be top-left/top-right and c,d bottom-left/bottom-right. A row interpolation returns its left endpoint directly if tx==0, its right endpoint directly if tx==1, otherwise evaluates left+tx*(right-left) with checked primitives. If ty==0, evaluate only the top row; the bottom row interpolation must not execute. If ty==1, evaluate only the bottom row; the top row interpolation must not execute. Otherwise evaluate top, then bottom, then top+ty*(bottom-top). All supplied grid numbers are still statically validated before work preflight or sampling, including unused rows/endpoints. This endpoint evaluation order is an explicit root resolution.

For each step, in order, `k1=S(p)`, `k2=S(p+(dt/2)*k1)`,
`k3=S(p+(dt/2)*k2)`, `k4=S(p+dt*k3)`. For each component compute
`sum=((k1+2*k2)+2*k3)+k4`, `next=p+(dt/6)*sum`. Check every primitive. STOP rejects the
whole current step if any stage query or final next point leaves the domain; retain the
previous prefix and report BOUNDARY. Stage overflow is an error, not a boundary signal.
Otherwise append next and continue. No stationary shortcut: dt=0 repeats positions and
still evaluates stages. Zero steps returns STEPS without querying start, even if outside.

behavior.algorithm:
Curl from a scalar grid

Proposed ID: `field.scalar-grid-curl-2d`; transform.

Artist output: planar vectors tangent to scalar level sets. Studies: circulation arrows
over terrain; particle paths driven by the same retained vectors through candidate11.
Finite differencing and its boundary semantics are the computation; no noise is hidden.

Input:

```text
{values:[number,...], columns:integer>=2, rows:integer>=2,
 spacing:[positive,positive], boundary:"ONE_SIDED"|"WRAP", maxWork:integer}
```

Output `{vectors:[[number,number],...]}`. Define curl as `[dScalar/dy,-dScalar/dx]`
in the caller's coordinates; no renderer-axis reversal. Interior derivativeX is
`(right-left)/(2*hx)`, and derivativeY analogously. ONE_SIDED uses forward difference
at x=0 and backward difference at x=C-1, each divided by hx; Y similarly. A two-column
grid therefore uses the same one-sided X derivative in both columns. WRAP uses central
differences everywhere, sampling modulo; with two columns its X derivative is zero.
Evaluate derivativeX before derivativeY, then construct the rotated pair. No vector
normalization or promise of exact discrete incompressibility under other samplers.
Reserve W=5G; O(G) work/storage.

separationScale.description: Multiplier on summed radii;1 permits tangency, below1 permits overlap, above1 reserves size-relative clearance.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong shape, unsupported passive carrier, bool numeric, seed/count outside their integer domains, nonpositive extent/radius/separationScale, or reversed radiusRange.
errors.PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite proposal coordinate addition or pair arithmetic, or specified pair underflow; candidateIndex and named stage, no output.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite nonnegative safe integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index is outside0..size-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination or offset lacks two writable binary64 slots.

behavior.layout: A placement result privately retains 2*N binary64 centre coordinates, N binary64 radii and N integer original proposal indices, where N is accepted count. Apply proposal-count ceiling1073741823 statically to seeded attempts or explicit input length, so even accepting every proposal fits2*N<=2147483647. This is a shared packed-array/index representation bound, not an allocation, latency or useful artistic range guarantee. Capacity growth must be capped at this representation ceiling without integer overflow. Host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never INVALID_INPUT or partial successful output.
behavior.native_types: Follow existing grid numeric conventions: Java Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double only; reject BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive object/Array input with number values; Python int/float but never bool, convert to finite binary64 after validating integer domains where applicable. Python huge integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT/INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception. Output pointInto accepts Java double[], JS Float64Array or writable ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list or array(d). Offset/count/index validation must precede narrowing. Active accessors/proxies and custom containers are not interchange data. Input containers: Java Map for records and exactly two-element List for pairs; arrays/PVector are not pair input carriers. Only passive container behavior belongs to interchange; active custom hooks are outside it. Python requires exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs, rejecting custom Mapping/list subclasses and tuples. JS records have Object.prototype or null prototype and pairs are ordinary Array; class instances/typed-array pairs are not interchange input.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even for every basic operation in the stated order. No FMA, reassociation, sqrt/hypot substitute, epsilon, binary32 conversion or host transcendental in the core. Normalize every zero input coordinate and completed zero output coordinate to positive zero. Radius and scale must be strictly positive. Compare core output coordinates/radii by exact binary64 bits and all counts/source indices/errors exactly across targets; do not tolerate topology differences. This is a checked floating predicate, not an exact real-number geometry guarantee. Supplied radial points are caller data: cross-host trigonometry used to construct them is outside this contract.
behavior.native_errors: Validation/access exceptions have code. PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID additionally exposes candidateIndex (Python candidate_index) and stage, emitted as error_detail:{candidateIndex,stage} by conformance runners. Static INVALID_INPUT and accessor errors have no dynamic detail. Java validation errors may subclass IllegalArgumentException and arithmetic errors ArithmeticException; JS Error and Python ValueError subclasses are transport. Host resource failures are not converted to validation errors or partial success.
behavior.shared_semantics: The acceptance, pair_validation, ownership, access, units and complexity sections of sampling.ordered-circle-filter-2d@0.1.0 are normative for this operation. Its result/accessor contract is shared unchanged. This entry adds seeded proposal generation and its own static validation; no RNG is added to the filter.
behavior.input: Input has exactly six required keys. Validate outer passive record/keys; seed; attempts; origin pair/x/y; extent pair/width/height; radiusRange pair/min/max then min<=max; separationScale, in that order. All numbers finite and never bool. Seed and attempts are finite integral numbers within schema bounds before narrowing. Origin may be any finite coordinate; extents, radii and scale strictly positive. Normalize origin zero signs. Complete static validation before RNG initialization or output-sized storage. No defaults.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1, private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0 and q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). All-zero state is unreachable for this expansion, an internal invariant rather than a valid-seed input error. next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32. Then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Unsigned output/4294967296 is exact binary64 in[0,1). State is private, discarded on return/failure; no returned RNG or shared session.
behavior.proposal: For i=0..attempts-1 consume exactly four units ux,uy,u,v before geometric arithmetic, unconditionally even if a proposal is later rejected or min==max. Compute px=round64(extent.x*ux), x=round64(px+origin.x), py=round64(extent.y*uy), y=round64(py+origin.y), span=round64(maxRadius-minRadius), first=round64(span*u), second=round64(first*v), r=round64(minRadius+second), in that order. Check x and y finite immediately after their additions; nonfinite results raise PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with candidateIndex=i and stage proposal_x or proposal_y, respectively, and no output, including at the first proposal. The products, radius span and radius mapping are finite for valid input and the specified 32-bit unit mapping; defensive finite checks on them are internal assertions, not public error stages. Canonicalize final x/y zeros before acceptance. Finite underflow/absorption in proposal mapping is its defined rounding, unlike the checked exclusion predicate. Geometric endpoints can round to the nominal maximum; no general exclusive endpoint claim. Centres are mapped from the rectangle only: circle edges may extend outside it. No sorting, retries, host random draws, style randomness or count-dependent initialization.
behavior.zero_and_prefix: Zero attempts validates all static input but produces empty arrays and attempts0 with no proposal arithmetic or pair comparisons. Equal radius endpoints produce that radius but still consume all four units per proposal. Extending only attempts reproduces the exact accepted prefix when both calls succeed; later placements may be absent. Increasing separation need not monotonically reduce output count for arbitrary inputs. Replaying an unchanged config deterministically reconstructs the same result. Returning a result does not retain that config.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.sampling.CirclePlacements2D.seeded(Object config); JavaScript seededCirclePlacement2D(config); Python seeded_circle_placement_2d(config). All return the shared immutable CirclePlacements2D result specified by ordered-circle-filter-2d. No alternate input form, seed-only defaults or public raw RNG helper.

guide.title: Place circles from a seed
guide.summary: Propose and retain separated circles under an explicit attempt budget.
guide.useWhen: Use it for reproducible scattered forms.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295. Reuse it with the same inputs to reproduce the result; change it to explore another arrangement.
inputs.attempts: Nonnegative integer count of circle proposals. Only proposals that pass separation are kept; more attempts do not guarantee a particular circle count or a filled canvas.
inputs.origin: The `[x, y]` origin of the rectangle in which centers are proposed. This limits centers, not the full circles.
inputs.extent: Positive `[width, height]` of the center-proposal rectangle. Circle edges may extend outside it; add your own containment rule if needed.
inputs.radiusRange: Positive `[minimumRadius, maximumRadius]`, with minimum no larger than maximum. Equal values make fixed-size circles. The proposal distribution favors smaller radii rather than sampling them uniformly.
inputs.separationScale: A positive multiplier on the sum of two radii. At 1 circles may touch; below 1 they may overlap; above 1 they have size-relative clearance. It is not a fixed pixel gap.

guide.output: pointAt(index) and radiusAt(index) provide each accepted circle in proposal order; sourceIndexAt(index) points back to the accepted proposal. toValues() copies placements.
guide.tryThis: Draw circles or replace them with your own symbols.

operations.description: Generate discovery-ordered spanning-tree topology from a connected supplied graph using an explicit randomized DFS schedule.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed shape, supplied scalar/carrier/domain, impossible array representation, or operation-specific static constraint.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: The exact required or next charged work exceeds maxWork or safe work representation.
errors.DISCONNECTED: The root traversal ended before discovering every supplied vertex; no partial forest is returned.

behavior.validation: Exactly the input and nested-union keys shown by the schema, ordinary dense arrays and passive own data properties. Numeric carriers are finite binary64 and never booleans; integral fields are exact integers in schema domain. Reject accessors, host instances and coercion. Complete static validation of every field/element precedes work preflight, RNG draws or output allocation. Products defining array lengths must be exact and <=4294967295 or INVALID_INPUT, even if all individual dimensions are valid. Canonicalize input zeros to +0.
behavior.work: maxWork is a required nonnegative safe integer. Count arithmetic is exact; an unsafe work sum/product or insufficient allowance is WORK_LIMIT. A charge checks before its action; rejected actions do not execute. The operation-specific schedule is normative. Static input validation has unavoidable input-sized cost. Budgets are abstract work, not memory or latency guarantees; host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.numerics: Separate binary64 primitive rounding, no reassociation/FMA. Every computed primitive must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, including division by an underflowed zero denominator. No numerical repair, implicit epsilon or state clipping. Exposed zeros are +0. General finite output fields use absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; integer/topology/order/state/token values compare exactly. The bound fixture file contains only exact analytical outputs; approximate RK4 linear-field and nonzero-angle turtle geometry tests remain separate future property tests.
behavior.ownership: Read only caller inputs; output records and arrays are detached. No input record, array, RNG object, renderer, host state or callback is retained. All generated state remains private until success. No partial result on error; a successful RK4 boundary termination is its explicit retained-prefix result, not an error. Scalars and immutable strings are values.
behavior.rng:
rngState is an integer in `[0,4294967295]`, including zero. A draw first sets
`state=(1664525*state+1013904223) mod 4294967296`, then returns `u=state/4294967296`.
The multiplication and addition are exact integer arithmetic before reduction. JavaScript
may use unsigned `Math.imul` arithmetic if it produces those exact uint32 states. For
uniform selection among K ordered candidates use `floor(u*K)`. Both operations return
`rngState` containing the final state; they do not use a seed expander or fork a stream.
The multiplication by K uses binary64, with K within the array-length domain; clamp an
otherwise rounded index K to K-1. This is bounded mapping, not unbiased rejection sampling.
behavior.algorithm:
Seeded depth-first spanning tree

Proposed ID: `topology.seeded-depth-first-spanning-tree`; generator.

Artist output: parent/child topology reusable for corridor labyrinths and radial vein
trees. Input graph edges may come from a grid or existing Delaunay output. This is a
randomized DFS distribution, **not a uniformly sampled spanning tree**. It does not invent
an embedding, connect disconnected components or generate branch lengths.

Input:

```text
{vertexCount:integer in [1,4294967295],edges:[[integer,integer],...],
 root:integer in [0,vertexCount-1],rngState:uint32,maxWork:integer}
```

Each edge has 0<=a<b<vertexCount. Edges must be strictly lexicographically increasing;
duplicates and self-edges are invalid. Isolated vertices are represented through
vertexCount. Output `{edges:[[parent,child],...],parents:[integer,...],depths:[integer,...],
rngState:uint32}`. Output edges are directed discovery-order edges, not sorted undirected
pairs. Root parent=-1 and depth0; all other parents/depths correspond to first discovery.

Reserve setup W0=V+2E before owned graph/traversal storage. Build ascending neighbor lists;
strictly sorted input edges permit ordered appends without a separate random/sort phase.
Mark root visited, push it. Repeatedly take stack top v, scan **all** its neighbors in
ascending order, charging1 before every neighbor visit, and collect the currently unvisited
candidates. If none, pop v without a draw. Otherwise charge1 for the choice, draw exactly
once even for a singleton candidate list, select floor(u*K) with the shared mapping, mark
that vertex visited, append [v,child], set parent/depth and push child. The next loop starts
at the new top; when returning to v, rescan its full neighbor list with fresh charges.
On empty stack, if discovered count<V raise DISCONNECTED; otherwise return the tree/state.
No result escapes on disconnection, and the caller's RNG value remains an immutable input.

Time can include repeated neighbor scans and is bounded by charged visits, not assumed
linear DFS with a different cursor-based random policy. Storage O(V+E), with candidate
scratch reused per scan and a stack bounded by V. V=1/E=0 succeeds with W=1 and zero draws.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export seededDepthFirstSpanningTree(input) from packages/javascript/src/seeded-depth-first-spanning-tree.js; plain output matching output_schema. Other targets deferred.

operations.description: Retain a bounded breadth-first endpoint branch tree from an explicit root, portable seed, and ordered generation rules. It computes segment geometry and ancestry only.

maxSegments.description: Includes the root. This is a six-binary64-plus-three-int32 packed-storage representation ceiling, not a work or artistic recommendation.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, invalid seed/maxSegments, negative root length/scale or probability outside closed[0,1].
errors.BRANCH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: A root or successful child finite arithmetic check fails; error_detail has parentIndex,slotIndex and stage length|heading|delta_x|delta_y|position_x|position_y.
errors.SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: A successful slot would exceed maxSegments; error_detail has parentIndex and slotIndex, before its angle draw or child arithmetic.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside0..size()-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: segmentInto destination/offset lacks four writable binary64 slots.

errorOrder: Static phase: INVALID_INPUT is the only operation error; it completes before root arithmetic, output-sized allocation or RNG initialization.
Root phase after static validation: root arithmetic may raise BRANCH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with parentIndex=-1 and slotIndex=-1 before traversal begins.

Breadth-first expansion phase: an inactive parent consumes no draw; an active parent samples scale then each slot gate. A failed gate cannot raise capacity or child arithmetic. For a successful gate, SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED is checked before angle draw and all child arithmetic; after the angle draw, child arithmetic may raise BRANCH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID.
Result access phase: INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT for segmentInto.

behavior.input: Input has exactly seed,root,rules,maxSegments. Validate outer passive record/keys; seed; root record/keys; root origin pair then x/y; heading; length; rules outer List; then each rule in increasing list order: record/keys, lengthScale pair then lower/upper endpoint, slots outer List, then every slot in increasing order: record/keys, probability, turn pair then lower/upper endpoint; finally maxSegments. Every accepted number is finite binary64 and never bool. Seed/maxSegments accept integral finite carriers in their stated domains before narrowing. Scale endpoints are nonnegative and probability is closed[0,1]; origin, heading and turn endpoints may be any finite binary64; root length is nonnegative. Each lengthScale and turn interval must also satisfy its first endpoint<=its second endpoint; this cross-field requirement is INVALID_INPUT and cannot be expressed by the Draft 2020-12 pair schema alone. Normalize accepted zero signs to +0. All static data, including unused later rules, validates before root arithmetic, output-sized allocation or RNG initialization. No defaults.
behavior.construction: After complete static validation, compute the root segment with parentIndex=-1 and generation=0. Visit parents in increasing retained index order, including children appended earlier by preceding parents. A parent whose generation is outside rules consumes no units. Otherwise consume exactly one unit for that rule shared per-parent scale, including when its slots list is empty. For each slot in declared order consume exactly one gate unit even when probability is0 or1; it succeeds iff gate<probability. A failure consumes no angle. On success, check maxSegments before another draw or child arithmetic, consume exactly one angle unit, compute/validate and append the child immediately, then increment the parent child count. Children are visited only later through the growing retained list; no recursive descent, retry, invisible/style draw or terminal shrink draw occurs.
behavior.rule_prefix: For identical seed/root and identical existing rules, appending later rules preserves geometry, headings, nominal lengths, parent indices and generations for every previous node when both calls succeed. maxSegments need not be equal when neither call fails capacity; either successful call may reach capacity exactly. Former leaves may acquire children, so childCounts, terminal membership, full output and output-array prefix equality are not promised. Changing only a later rule preserves earlier-level geometry under the same condition. A rule expression normalized by total depth is a changed existing rule and forfeits this guarantee. Altering early slots/gates may shift subsequent stream consumption and has no broader locality promise.
behavior.intervals: For each consumed unit t, sample scale or turn by L(a,b,t). t=0 returns canonical a and t=1 returns canonical b. Otherwise, when a and b have strictly opposite signs, raw=round64(round64(a*round64(1-t))+round64(b*t)); otherwise raw=round64(a+round64(round64(b-a)*t)). Clamp raw to the closed finite endpoint interval [min(a,b),max(a,b)], then canonicalize zero. Apply no FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion, interval shortcut or skipped unit for constant endpoints.
behavior.segment_numerics: For a successful child after its angle draw, compute length=round64(parent.length*scale), then heading=round64(parent.heading+turn). Its start is the exact retained parent endpoint. For root and child segments separately compute dx=round64(hostCos(heading)*length), dy=round64(hostSin(heading)*length), endX=round64(startX+dx), endY=round64(startY+dy). Check finite results in order length, heading, dx, dy, endX, endY. A root dynamic failure carries parentIndex=-1 and slotIndex=-1. A child failure carries its retained parent index and successful slot index. Do not normalize heading; coordinates use x right/y down, so positive turn is clockwise in a conventional screen drawing. Coincident endpoints and zero lengths remain valid when all stated computations are finite. Canonicalize each completed scalar zero to +0 before storing or using it as a retained attribute. For a conforming finite bounded sine/cosine, delta_x/delta_y overflow is unreachable after finite length/heading; those defensive stages need a proof of unreachability rather than fabricated finite-input witnesses.
behavior.limits: maxSegments includes root and bounds retained nodes, not all validated input rules/slots or total slot visits. It is a representation ceiling, not an allocation, latency, runtime, or artistic guarantee. If a successful slot would append above capacity, raise SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with parentIndex/slotIndex before its angle draw or child arithmetic. Root-only output at capacity succeeds; failed gates at capacity do not fail. No truncation or partial result is returned. Host allocation failure remains a host resource exception.
behavior.layout: Privately retain six binary64 scalar slots and three int32 slots per segment: start x/y, end x/y, heading, nominal length, parent index, generation and direct child count. maxSegments<=357913941 keeps each packed array signed-int-indexable. Use growable packed storage; do not preallocate maxSegments or allocate per-node objects in the expansion loop. Retained primitive payload is 60 bytes per node excluding headers, spare capacity, input and detached materialization.
behavior.ownership: Result owns detached packed arrays only and retains no caller record/List, RNG state, renderer or style. Accepted passive inputs are not concurrently mutated during the eager call. segmentAt and toValues materialize fresh detached ordinary data; segmentInto writes four slots only after all access/output validation succeeds. Getter/export allocation failure returns no new value and leaves the result usable. There is no serialize/toJSON/config echo, ID alias, implicit terminal marker or reconstructed-tree export.
behavior.access: size() returns retained segment count. segmentAt returns a fresh four-number [x0,y0,x1,y1] carrier. headingAt,lengthAt,parentAt,generationAt,childCountAt return aligned scalar data. Index must be finite safe nonnegative integer<=9007199254740991 and never bool; integral floating indices are accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT for segmentInto. segmentInto requires finite nonnegative integral offset and four writable binary64 slots, rejects Float32, and preserves every destination slot on failure. Java has typed required int offset and returns void; wrong/unrepresentable Java calls are host-call errors. JavaScript returns out; Python returns None.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.topology.BranchTree2D.generate(Object config) returns BranchTree2D with size(), segmentAt(Object or long), segmentInto(index,double[],int), headingAt(Object or long), lengthAt(Object or long), parentAt(Object or long), generationAt(Object or long), childCountAt(Object or long), toValues(). JavaScript and Python forms are prospective only: a shared result exposes size, segmentAt/segment_at, segmentInto/segment_into, aligned scalar accessors and toValues/to_values. No aliases, callbacks, iterator, host RNG or serializer are proposed.
behavior.native_types: Follow CP5 passive-carrier rules: Java Map records and passive List containers with the specified exact pair/interval lengths, accepting only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double and rejecting BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Arrays; Python exact builtin dict/list with int/float but never bool. Arrays/PVector, typed-array input pairs, class instances, active getters/proxies and custom mapping/list containers are outside interchange. Java segmentInto accepts double[]; a future JavaScript target may accept Float64Array or writable ordinary Array and Python exact builtin list or array(d).
behavior.numerics: Basic operations use stated IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even order. Java/Android Math.sin/cos, JavaScript Math.sin/cos and Python math.sin/cos have no implicit heading reduction. Same target/runtime replay is exact. Cross-target coordinates use explicit per-case tolerances only where nontrivial host trigonometry occurs; topology, RNG words, indices, generations, child counts, headings, nominal lengths, axis/zero-trig fixtures and stated arithmetic errors remain exact. No universal cross-runtime trig tolerance or arbitrary-descriptor error bound is claimed.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map output to u=unsigned_u32/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). State is private/discarded and never shares Processing/source/background/palette state. The all-zero state is unreachable and an internal invariant.
environment: private xoshiro128**1.1 with uint32 seed/Two-SplitMix64 expansion
behavior.complexity: O(rule/slot validation + visited slots + emitted nodes) work and O(emitted nodes) retained numeric storage. maxSegments bounds retained nodes but not arbitrary supplied rule/slot validation or all failed gate visits. Indexed access is O(1); detached export is O(size). Benchmarks must cover realistic branching and a long one-slot chain without host recursion.
behavior.native_errors: Library failures expose code. BRANCH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID and SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED additionally expose parentIndex (Python parent_index) and slotIndex (Python slot_index), serialized in conformance as error_detail:{parentIndex,slotIndex,stage?}. Static/access errors have no dynamic detail. Java may use dedicated IllegalArgumentException/ArithmeticException subclasses; JS Error and Python ValueError subclasses carry equivalent data. Host allocation failure is never INVALID_INPUT or partial success.

guide.title: Grow retained branches
guide.summary: Generate endpoint branches from explicit rules and a seed.
guide.useWhen: Use it when a tree needs repeatable topology before styling.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295. Reuse it with the same inputs to reproduce the result; change it to explore another arrangement.
inputs.root: The first branch as `{origin: [x, y], heading, length}`. Heading is in radians and length is nonnegative. Zero heading points along positive X; length is in your drawing units.
inputs.rules: One rule per generation, in order. Each is `{lengthScale: [min, max], slots: [{probability, turn: [min, max]}, ...]}`. Length scales are ordered nonnegative multipliers on parent length; turns are ordered radian offsets from parent heading; probability is 0–1. Each slot can create a child at a parent endpoint.
inputs.maxSegments: Positive integer limit on all retained segments including the root. More generations or child slots can grow the tree quickly; exceeding the limit fails the complete call.

guide.output: segmentAt(index) returns local [x1,y1,x2,y2] and generationAt(index) identifies its branch generation, so loop size and style each p.line(). toValues() copies it.
guide.tryThis: Use generationAt() to vary stroke color or width.

operations.description: Generate a retained ordered pool of branching segments by repeatedly cutting selected existing segments.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static carrier/key/domain validation before generation.
errors.ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite checked intermediate, details attempt and stage; child coordinate stages additionally childOrdinal. First failure in transition order wins.
errors.SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Actual append count would exceed maxSegments, after selection/policy draws and before parent/child endpoint arithmetic; details attempt and selectedIndex.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Not a finite safe nonnegative integer; booleans rejected.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Index>=size.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: segmentInto lacks four writable binary64 slots or valid offset.

errorOrder: Static INVALID_INPUT before generation including zero work.
Per-attempt length arithmetic precedes skip; policy arithmetic precedes actual append cap; cap precedes cut/child arithmetic.
Access INVALID_INDEX then INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE then INVALID_OUTPUT.

behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map output to u=unsigned_u32/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). State is private/discarded and never shares Processing/source/background/palette state. The all-zero state is unreachable and an internal invariant.
behavior.numeric_profile: fdlibm5.3 sin/cos/atan2 under Java binary64 rules; correctly rounded sqrt; all basic arithmetic separately rounded binary64, no FMA/reassociation. Exact outputs, no topology/coordinate tolerance. Java StrictMath supplies the elementary profile; other target implementations deferred.
behavior.transition_specification:
Normative transition0.1.0, root reviewed.
Each arithmetic operator below rounds separately to binary64. C(value,stage) fails
ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW {attempt,stage} on nonfinite, otherwise returns value. Function
arguments evaluate left-to-right. Constants are nearest binary64 decimal values.
U() is one unsigned xoshiro output divided by4294967296. PI=0x1.921fb54442d18p1.
R(lo,hi) returns lo without U when lo>=hi; otherwise lo+((hi-lo)*U()). All R bounds
below are finite in[0,3] or[-.1,.1], so their arithmetic cannot overflow. Upper-bound
rounding is accepted, not retried. First-cut selection is min(2,floor(3*U())).

Validate passive input shape/keys; then fields seed,segment coordinates x0/y0/x1/y1,
attempts,firstCutAngleScale,minCutLength,maxSegments. All finite; boolean not numeric.
Store initial segment and divided=false. Zero attempts exports immediately. Export
canonicalizes signed coordinate zeros to+0 without changing internal arithmetic.

For attempt=0..attempts-1:
 index=min(size-1,floor((U()*size)*R(.8,1)))
 sx,sy,ex,ey = selected current endpoints
 dx=C(ex-sx,"difference_x"); dy=C(ey-sy,"difference_y")
 xx=C(dx*dx,"square_x"); yy=C(dy*dy,"square_y")
 squared=C(xx+yy,"squared_length"); length=correctlyRoundedSqrt(squared)
 heading=fdlibmAtan2(dy,dx)
 if length<minCutLength: skips++; continue
 fraction=R(R(.6,.7),R(0,.8))
 if divided[index]: fraction=fraction*.4
 remainder=length*(1-fraction)  # finite: fraction in[0,.8],length finite
 if not divided[index]:
   a=R(0,1.2)*R(.2,1); a=C(a*firstCutAngleScale,"spread_positive")
   b=R(0,1.2)*R(.2,1); b=C(b*firstCutAngleScale,"spread_negative")
   unused=U() # source range interpolation result unused; no arithmetic needed
   l0=C(remainder*R(.9,1.2),"length_positive")
   l1=C(remainder*R(.9,1.2),"length_negative")
   l2=C(remainder*R(.9,1.2),"length_straight")
   h0=C(heading+a,"heading_positive")
   h1=C(heading-b,"heading_negative")
   h2=C(heading+R(-.1,.1),"heading_straight")
   choice=min(2,floor(3*U()))
   children = [] if choice==0 else [(h0,l0,false),(h1,l1,false)] if choice==1
              else [(h2,l2,false)]
 else:
   deviation=R(.1,.4); sign=-1 if U()<.5 else+1; deviation=(deviation*sign)*2
   distance=C(remainder*R(.9,1.1),"length_repeat")
   turn=C(heading+deviation,"heading_repeat")
   children = [continuation(ex,ey,true),(turn,distance,false)]
 if size+len(children)>maxSegments:
   fail SEGMENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED {attempt,selectedIndex:index}
 nx=C(sx+C(dx*fraction,"cut_delta_x"),"cut_x")
 ny=C(sy+C(dy*fraction,"cut_delta_y"),"cut_y")
 For each child in append order, ordinal=0,1:
   continuation keeps old(ex,ey) exactly, no trig
   ordinary endpoint:
     cx=C(nx+C(fdlibmCos(turn)*distance,"child_delta_x"),"child_x")
     cy=C(ny+C(fdlibmSin(turn)*distance,"child_delta_y"),"child_y")
   child stage errors also include childOrdinal; other stages do not.
 Only after all appended endpoints validated: selected end=(nx,ny),divided=true;
 append children starting(nx,ny) with their specified flags; successfulCuts++.

No partial output on any failure. Child coordinates are prepared before any mutation.
No arithmetic or trig for unselected child endpoints. Source policy scalar computations
and draws DO occur for unselected first-cut children, preserving specified errors/order.
No caller callbacks, shared RNG state, rendering or ancestry. Exact output comparisons.
behavior.ownership: Copy passive input; retain packed coordinates/flags; never expose mutable arrays. No partial result on failure. Host allocation errors remain host errors.
behavior.storage: Grow four binary64 slots and one divided flag per segment; do not preallocate maxSegments. Primitive payload33bytes/segment excluding array headers/spare capacity.
