behavior.access: Index finite safe nonnegative integer<=9007199254740991, boolean rejected. INVALID_INDEX then INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE then INVALID_OUTPUT. segmentInto requires nonnull double[] and int offset>=0 with four slots; validate all before writing; failed write preserves array. segmentAt/toValues detached; getter allocation failure leaves result usable. No config serialization.
behavior.zero_work: Return copied root with divided=false and all counters0; do not calculate length/trig or consume RNG.
behavior.extreme_coordinates: Zero attempts does not evaluate distance, so any finite endpoint tuple is returned. For attempted work the explicitly squared length may overflow at square_x/square_y/squared_length or underflow to zero; underflow is not an error and then minCutLength>0 causes a skip. No robust hypot substitution or coordinate normalization is permitted in this version. This follows the declared arithmetic, not a measured artistic range.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.topology.LinePool2D.generate(Object config) returns LinePool2D. size(), attempts(), successfulCuts(), skips() return int. segmentAt(Object or long index) returns fresh double[4]; segmentInto(Object or long index,double[] out,int offset) returns void; dividedAt(Object or long index) returns boolean; toValues() returns detached Map with exact output-schema fields. No mutable buffers exposed.
behavior.native_types: Follow CP5 passive-carrier rules: Java Map records and passive List containers with the specified exact pair/interval lengths, accepting only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double and rejecting BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Arrays; Python exact builtin dict/list with int/float but never bool. Arrays/PVector, typed-array input pairs, class instances, active getters/proxies and custom mapping/list containers are outside interchange. Java segmentInto accepts double[]; a future JavaScript target may accept Float64Array or writable ordinary Array and Python exact builtin list or array(d).

guide.title: Repeatedly cut a line
guide.summary: Build a bounded retained pool of line segments.
guide.useWhen: Use it for branching cut structures with stable segment access.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295. Reuse it with the same inputs to reproduce the result; change it to explore another arrangement.
inputs.segment: Initial `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` line in your drawing units. It is retained even with zero attempts. Later cuts shorten selected segments and may append branches.
inputs.attempts: Nonnegative integer number of attempts to cut a selected segment. Segments shorter than minCutLength are skipped; successful cuts do not all create the same number of branches.
inputs.firstCutAngleScale: Nonnegative multiplier on the generated first-cut angular spread, measured in radians. Larger values spread first-cut branches farther from their parent direction. Repeat cuts use their own fixed turn rule.
inputs.minCutLength: Positive drawing length threshold for selecting a segment to cut. Shorter segments are skipped. This does not promise that all output branches exceed the threshold.
inputs.maxSegments: Positive integer capacity including the original line and appended children. If a cut would exceed it, the call throws with no partial pool.

guide.output: segmentAt(index) returns each local [x1,y1,x2,y2] in retained order, so loop size and draw p.line() directly. toValues() copies segment data.
guide.tryThis: Draw each retained segment in its stored order.

operations.description: Apply seeded shared-channel brightness addition or alpha multiplication to a straight ARGB8 raster, returning detached pixels and the next random state.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static schema/carrier/domain failure, before work and arithmetic.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: N exceeds maxWork after static validation; no draws or output.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite span or effect primitive; no partial raster or returned state.

behavior.validation: Exactly source,mode,range,exponent,rngState,maxWork in a passive Object/null-prototype record. Reject accessors, class instances, symbols, extra keys, coercion and booleans as numbers; proxies are outside passive interchange. Dense ordinary arrays with own data slots and no extra properties. Static validation order: outer record/keys; source record/keys; width; height; exact product <=2147483647; pixels shape then all pixel values in row-major order; mode; range shape then low then high then low<=high and for ALPHA_MULTIPLY low>=0; exponent finite>0; rngState; maxWork. Dimensions1..2147483647 and uint32/safe integer domains as schema. Canonicalize accepted zeros. Validate every pixel even for identity effect and insufficient budget. INVALID_INPUT is raised before work/algorithm arithmetic. No defaults.
behavior.work: After complete static validation require N=width*height<=maxWork or WORK_LIMIT, before range subtraction, random draws or output allocation. One abstract event per pixel includes one draw, one power and channel arithmetic; no skips for transparent pixels or identity intervals. Validation itself is O(N). Output storage O(N), auxiliary effect state O(1). Host resource exhaustion is a host error; no partial result escapes.
behavior.rng: LCG32 own state: state=(1664525*state+1013904223) modulo4294967296. A draw advances first, then u=state/4294967296. Zero is valid. Traverse y ascending then x ascending; exactly one draw per pixel even when source alpha0, low==high, source black, output clips, or effect is identity. Return final state. Calls can thread that state; seed replay is external state restoration. No ambient RNG, hash, time or renderer.
behavior.algorithm: Compute span=high-low after work preflight; nonfinite span is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. For each pixel draw u, set q=fdlibm5.3Pow(u,exponent) (exponent1 may use exact u). Compute scaled=span*q then sample=low+scaled, checking each primitive for finiteness. RGB_ADD unpacks straight R,G,B and computes R+sample then G+sample then B+sample; preserve source alpha byte. ALPHA_MULTIPLY computes sourceAlpha*sample and preserves original straight RGB bytes. Quantize each changed channel by floor(min(255,max(0,value))+.5); nonfinite arithmetic fails before clamp. Repack unsigned32 ARGB. Preserve hidden RGB even when alpha quantizes to0; no premultiplication/unpremultiplication, color-space conversion, spatial interpolation or automatic compositing. A point sample at the high endpoint can occur from binary64 rounding even though uniform u<1. Source output arrays are separate and mutable value carriers; modifying returned pixels never changes input or later calls.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separately rounded primitive operations, no FMA/reassociation or binary32 narrowing. Power is the existing independently audited fdlibm5.3 e_pow numerical profile, including its positive-base/positive-exponent zero and underflow behavior; p5 implementation reuses packages/javascript/src/internal/fdlibm-pow.js with its Sun Microsystems notice. Do not substitute host Math.pow. Inputs u in[0,1) and exponent>0 imply q finite in[0,1]; underflow to0 is valid. Every primitive specified above must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. No global epsilon; packed pixels, dimensions and RNG state compare exactly. uint32 transition may use unsigned Math.imul arithmetic. Preserve zero byte values.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export seededPixelGrain(input) and SeededPixelGrainError from packages/javascript/src/seeded-pixel-grain.js and the public package index. Returns {raster:{width,height,pixels},rngState}; no native host objects. Other targets deferred.
behavior.adapter: Core requires no renderer. Editable native example requires p5 Canvas2D RGBA8 pixel read/write with pixelDensity(1), upper-left row-major order and explicit byte packing/unpacking. Call loadPixels after drawing and updatePixels after copying output. Process isolated transparent layers before compositing for alpha grain; never substitute flattened scene grain for per-fragment shader scheduling. Browser premultiplication may discard hidden transparent RGB on upload/readback; exact core hidden-RGB tests remain core evidence, while visible native output is checked separately. Save exports the already rendered canvas without reseeding or redraw. Pack straight p5 RGBA bytes as unsigned (A<<24)|(R<<16)|(G<<8)|B and unpack back without premultiplication. Native visual validation cannot attest hidden transparent RGB. The editable adapter rejects density other than1 or mismatched byte length before invoking core; unreadable/tainted canvas errors propagate visibly as host errors. These example checks are not another public core API.
behavior.environment: Only explicit input and the named deterministic power profile. No global RNG/noise/time, callbacks, image assets, shaders, fonts or persistent mutation.

guide.title: Add seeded raster grain
guide.summary: Give flat colors a fine brightness texture, or make an existing layer speckled and translucent.
guide.useWhen: Use it on a captured pixel raster, then draw or composite the returned raster. Keep the seed to repeat the texture.

inputs.source: {width,height,pixels}: straight ARGB8 pixels in upper-left row-major order.
inputs.mode: RGB_ADD changes brightness; ALPHA_MULTIPLY changes opacity.
inputs.range: [low,high]: brightness change in bytes, or an opacity multiplier interval.
inputs.exponent: Positive power: values above 1 favor the low end of the interval; values below 1 favor the high end.

guide.output: {raster:{width,height,pixels},rngState}
guide.tryThis: Change mode or range, then inspect the detached raster and returned state.
pitfalls: The operation has no defaults and does not read a renderer or ambient RNG.
ALPHA_MULTIPLY preserves straight RGB bytes and changes only alpha.

operations.description: Generate an immutable, mutation-ordered sequence of equal-quadrant rectangular leaves from explicit seed, rectangle, replacement count and eligible-list fraction.

seed.description: Explicit uint32 seed for the private portable stream.

replacements.description: Number of requested live-leaf replacements. The maximum is a signed-int packed-coordinate representation ceiling, not a practical-work or artistic recommendation.

origin.description: Root rectangle left/top [x,y] in caller coordinate units.

extent.description: Root rectangle positive [width,height] in caller coordinate units.

selectionFraction.description: Fractional eligible prefix of the current ordered live list; the last eligible index has fractional weight when live-count*fraction is not integral.

items.description: [left,top,right,bottom] axis-aligned leaf bounds in live-list order.

ids.description: Within-run creation identities aligned with bounds.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong carrier/shape/keys, bool numeric, invalid uint32 seed, replacement count outside its representation domain, nonpositive extent, or selectionFraction outside(0,1].
errors.INVALID_RECTANGLE: After valid static input, root endpoint add/subtract cannot produce finite strictly increasing and positive represented horizontal and vertical bounds. This error has no dynamic detail.
errors.PARTITION_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: A requested selected-parent midpoint is not strictly inside its parent after specified binary64 calculation. error_detail has replacementIndex and midpoint_x or midpoint_y stage; no output is returned.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside0..size()-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: boundsInto destination/offset lacks four writable binary64 slots.

behavior.input: Input has exactly five required keys. Validate outer passive record/keys; seed; replacements; origin pair/x/y; extent pair/width/height; selectionFraction, in that order. Every numeric value is finite and never bool. Seed and replacements accept finite integral values in their stated bounds before narrowing. Origin can be any finite coordinate; extent components and selectionFraction must be strictly positive, and selectionFraction must not exceed1. Normalize accepted input zero signs to positive zero. No defaults.
behavior.root_rectangle: After static input validation and before RNG initialization or output-sized allocation, calculate right=round64(left+width), then bottom=round64(top+height). Each endpoint must be finite and strictly greater than its origin coordinate. Calculate representedWidth=round64(right-left), then representedHeight=round64(bottom-top); each must be finite and strictly positive. A failure in any of these checks is INVALID_RECTANGLE. A representable positive root is valid when replacements=0 even if a subsequent half split would not be representable. Leaves cover this represented endpoint rectangle; no real-number exact-extent guarantee is implied by rounded origin+extent. Do not calculate or require finite area: finite spans can have an overflowing area product without invalidating the partition.
behavior.layout: N=replacements. Privately retain four binary64 endpoints and one integer creation id for each of 1+3*N live leaves. N<=178956970 ensures 4*(1+3*N)<=2147483647, allowing signed-int-indexed packed endpoint storage; this is a representation ceiling, not an allocation, latency or useful artistic-range promise. Host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never a validation error or partial successful output. Internal leaves retain shared endpoints left/top/right/bottom, never independently recomputed child border coordinates.
behavior.selection: For replacement index i=0..N-1, let L be the current ordered live-leaf count. Consume exactly one private portable unit u in [0,1). Compute limit=round64(L*selectionFraction); compute product=round64(u*limit); selected=floor(product). The arithmetic is separate binary64 operations: no FMA, reassociation, pre-rounded eligible count, clamping, retry or extra draw. Under the validated domains and unit mapping selected is a current index in0..L-1. SelectionFraction=1 exposes the whole list; a fractional L*selectionFraction gives the last eligible index its fractional sampling interval rather than truncating that index away.
behavior.replacement: Read the selected parent bounds [left,top,right,bottom]. Compute spanX=round64(right-left), halfX=round64(spanX*0.5), midpointX=round64(left+halfX) and require left<midpointX<right. Then compute spanY=round64(bottom-top), halfY=round64(spanY*0.5), midpointY=round64(top+halfY) and require top<midpointY<bottom. Test x before y. If either midpoint cannot be represented strictly inside its selected parent, discard all internal work and raise PARTITION_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with error_detail:{replacementIndex:i,stage:midpoint_x|midpoint_y}; never silently skip, clamp, partially return or consume a substitute draw. On success append four children using the parent's stored endpoints in exactly TL=[left,top,midpointX,midpointY], TR=[midpointX,top,right,midpointY], BR=[midpointX,midpointY,right,bottom], BL=[left,midpointY,midpointX,bottom] order, assigning the next four consecutive creation ids, then remove the parent at selected. The children are nested inside an already validated parent; finite positive child spans follow as an invariant rather than separate dynamic stages.
behavior.zero_and_replay: N=0 validates every static input and the representable root rectangle, returns exactly root bounds and id0, and initializes or consumes no RNG state. Every requested replacement consumes one unit before its midpoint check. Replaying unchanged valid input reconstructs exactly the same topology, ids and binary64 bounds. Returning a result retains neither input carrier nor stream state. A successful longer run follows the same first N replacement steps as the shorter run, then replaces additional leaves: its final leaf array is generally not a prefix or a superset of the shorter final leaf array. A later dynamic failure returns no result.
behavior.ownership: Result owns detached arrays only. Caller input containers must not be mutated concurrently with the eager call; active getters/proxies/custom hooks are outside passive interchange. Complete static validation before output-sized allocation or RNG initialization. Result is immutable. boundsAt returns a fresh four-number binary64 array; toValues returns deep-copied bounds/ids/replacements exactly matching output_schema. boundsInto validates before writing four slots. No caller input or RNG state is retained. No serialize/toJSON/config replay API or count aliases: callers retain their original configuration. Getter/export allocation failure returns no new value and leaves the retained result usable. Invalid access changes no destination slots.
behavior.access: Java size() and replacements() (JavaScript/Python getters/properties) return retained leaf count and requested replacement count. boundsAt/bounds_at returns a fresh four-number bounds array, idAt/id_at the within-run creation identity. Index must be finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991, never bool; integral floating indices accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (index>=size), then INVALID_OUTPUT for boundsInto/bounds_into. Require a finite nonnegative integral offset and four writable binary64 slots; reject Float32 buffers and leave all destination slots unchanged on failure. Java boundsInto has required typed int offset and returns void; wrong-type/unrepresentable typed host calls are host-call errors. JavaScript boundsInto(index,out,offset=0) returns out; Python bounds_into(index,out,offset=0) returns None. Validate offset/index before narrowing.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.layout.QuadrantPartition2D.generate(Object config) returns QuadrantPartition2D with size(), replacements(), boundsAt(Object or long), boundsInto(index,double[],int offset), idAt(Object or long), toValues(). JavaScript seededQuadrantPartition2D(config) returns result with size/replacements getters, boundsAt,boundsInto,idAt,toValues. Python seeded_quadrant_partition_2d(config) returns result with size/replacements properties, bounds_at,bounds_into,id_at,to_values. No alternate carrier, defaults, serialize/toJSON or count aliases.
behavior.native_types: Follow established portable carrier rules: Java accepts Map records and exactly two-element List pairs; only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double numeric values are accepted, rejecting BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript accepts passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Array pairs; Python accepts exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs with int/float but never bool. PVector, typed-array pair input, class instances, active accessors/proxies and custom mapping/list containers are not interchange inputs. Java boundsInto uses double[]; future JavaScript accepts Float64Array or writable ordinary Array and Python exact builtin list or array(d). Python huge-integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT or INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception; validate integral domains before conversion where applicable.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar coordinate units. Bounds use [left,top,right,bottom]; positive x goes from left to right and positive y from top to bottom. The operation performs no canvas mapping, axis flip, clipping, drawing, content placement or style selection.
behavior.numerics: Every stated add, subtract and multiply is IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, with separate operation rounding. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion, host random API, clamp or epsilon. Normalize accepted zero input coordinates and every completed zero bound to positive zero. Compare topology, output length, ids, replacements, RNG state/vector bits and bounds by exact binary64 bits. The representability checks are a finite binary64 predicate, not a real-number geometric guarantee.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each nonzero-replacement call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0 and q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32. Then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map an unsigned output to unit u=output/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). The all-zero state is unreachable under this expansion and is an internal invariant. State is private, discarded on return/failure and never shared with content/style work. There is no Processing or source palette/background prelude.
environment: private xoshiro128**1.1 with specified uint32-seed/Two-SplitMix64 expansion
behavior.complexity: Flat ordered packed storage permits O(replacements^2) worst-case element moves and O(1+3*replacements) retained primitive storage; selection/split arithmetic itself is O(replacements). Rank-indexed implementations may improve the bound only while preserving every ordered result and error. Indexed retained access is O(1); detached export is O(size). Avoid per-leaf object allocation in the replacement loop. Benchmark practical ranges and distinguish retained payload from transient growth; the representation limit promises neither allocation success nor latency.
behavior.native_errors: Validation/access exceptions expose code. PARTITION_ARITHMETIC_INVALID additionally exposes replacementIndex (Python replacement_index) and stage, serialized by runners as error_detail:{replacementIndex,stage}. INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_RECTANGLE and accessor errors have no dynamic detail. Java validation errors may subclass IllegalArgumentException and dynamic errors ArithmeticException; JavaScript Error and Python ValueError subclasses carry equivalent data. Host resource failure is not converted to validation or partial success.

guide.title: Subdivide seeded regions
guide.summary: Replace eligible rectangles with quadrant cells.
guide.useWhen: Use it for a repeatable mosaic skeleton.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295. Reuse it with the same inputs to reproduce the result; change it to explore another arrangement.
inputs.replacements: Nonnegative integer number of leaf replacements. Each selected rectangle becomes four quadrants, so the result has 1 + 3 × replacements cells.
inputs.origin: The `[x, y]` lower-coordinate corner of the starting rectangle. With p5’s downward Y axis this is its top-left corner.
inputs.extent: Positive `[width, height]` of the starting rectangle in drawing units. Child rectangles occupy quadrants of this area.
inputs.selectionFraction: A value greater than 0 and no greater than 1. It limits selection to a prefix of the current ordered cell list: 1 considers all cells; smaller values favor earlier cells. It controls which cells split, not how many split.

guide.output: boundsAt(index) returns [left,top,right,bottom] and idAt(index) returns the stable live ID, so loop size and draw each cell with width right-left and height bottom-top. toValues() copies the layout.
guide.tryThis: Draw a different mark inside every returned bounds.

operations.description: retained batch of seeded uniform planar points in one explicitly supplied triangle. It computes point geometry only.

seed.description: Explicit uint32 seed for the specified private portable stream.

count.description: Requested points. The maximum only ensures two signed-int-indexed scalar slots per point; it is not a practical workload or artistic range.

triangle.description: Three ordered [x,y] planar vertices. Vertex order is preserved; no winding normalization.

items.description: Retained planar [x,y] positions in generation order.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, invalid seed/count, or invalid unit-independent triangle coordinate.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside 0..size()-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination/offset lacks two writable binary64 slots.

behavior.input: Static validation order: outer passive record and exact keys; seed; count; triangle container; vertex0 x/y; vertex1 x/y; vertex2 x/y. All accepted numbers must be finite binary64 values and never bool. Seed/count must be integral in their stated domains before narrowing. Normalize accepted zero signs to +0. Every static field, including triangle, validates for count0. Perform all static validation before stream initialization or output-sized allocation. No defaults.
behavior.generation: After full static validation, count=0 returns empty points and initializes/consumes no RNG. Otherwise initialize the specified private stream. For each index i ascending from0 to count-1, consume u then v, map through the shared specified triangle map and store point i. Exactly two units per point, including collapsed triangles; no retries, omitted invisible samples or style draws. An identical input replay is exact; increasing count preserves the shorter point prefix. Mapping the same ordered unit pairs through triangle-coordinate-map produces exactly the same point bits.
behavior.mapping: for each [u,v], calculate s=correctlyRoundedBinary64Sqrt(u), then independently for x and y calculate L(A,L(B,C,v),s). For L(a,b,t), t=0 returns canonical +0-normalized a and t=1 returns canonical +0-normalized b. Otherwise, when a and b have strictly opposite signs (one <0 and one >0), evaluate raw=round64(round64(a*round64(1-t))+round64(b*t)); otherwise evaluate raw=round64(a+round64(round64(b-a)*t)). Clamp raw to the closed finite [min(a,b),max(a,b)] endpoint interval and canonicalize zero to +0. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion or implicit clamp omission.
behavior.degeneracy: Accept every finite ordered vertex triple, including repeated or collinear triples, as the same collapsed mapping. Compute no area/determinant and use no epsilon or minimum-size gate. Ideal uniform-area interpretation applies only to nondegenerate geometry; a collapsed segment is not promised uniform arclength density. A positive seeded count consumes exactly two units per point even for repeated vertices. Empty outputs still validate every required field.
behavior.layout: N=count. The result privately retains exactly 2*N binary64 scalar slots. N<=1073741823 is a signed-int packed-storage representation ceiling only, not an allocation, latency or useful range guarantee. Host resource exhaustion is not INVALID_INPUT and never produces partial successful output.
behavior.ownership: Follow CP4 passive-carrier convention: synchronous callers do not concurrently mutate accepted containers; active getters/proxies/custom hooks are outside passive interchange. Complete static validation before output-sized allocation. A successful result owns detached packed points only; it retains no input container, coordinate list or stream state. pointAt and toValues materialize fresh detached data; allocation failure leaves an existing result unchanged. No serialize/toJSON/config replay or ID/count aliases.
behavior.access: size() in Java and size property/getter in JavaScript/Python returns retained point count. pointAt/point_at returns a fresh two-component binary64 point: Java double[], JavaScript ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list. Index must be finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991, never bool; integral floating indices accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (index>=size), then INVALID_OUTPUT for pointInto/point_into. Require a finite nonnegative integral offset and two writable binary64 slots; reject Float32 buffers and leave all destination slots unchanged on failure. Java pointInto has required typed int offset and returns void; wrong-type/unrepresentable typed host calls are host-call errors. JavaScript pointInto(index,out,offset=0) returns out; Python point_into(index,out,offset=0) returns None. Validate offset/index before narrowing.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.sampling.TrianglePoints2D.seeded(Object config) returns TrianglePoints2D with size(), pointAt(Object or long), pointInto(index,double[],int), toValues(). JavaScript seededTrianglePoints2D(config) returns a result with size property, pointAt, pointInto(offset default0), toValues. Python seeded_triangle_points_2d(config) returns a result with size property, point_at, point_into(offset default0), to_values. No additional overloads or aliases.
behavior.native_types: Follow established portable carrier rules: Java accepts Map records and List vertex/pair containers of the specified lengths; only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double numeric values are accepted, rejecting BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript accepts passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Array pairs; Python accepts exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs with int/float but never bool. PVector, typed-array pair input, class instances, active accessors/proxies and custom mapping/list containers are not interchange inputs. Java pointInto uses double[]; future JavaScript accepts Float64Array or writable ordinary Array and Python exact builtin list or array(d). Python huge-integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT or INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception; validate integral domains before conversion where applicable.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar [x,y] coordinates in an unchanged coordinate system; dimensionless unit coordinates. No axis flip, winding normalization, canvas conversion, topology, area/count allocation, palette/style, clipping or drawing.
behavior.numerics: Every stated primitive uses IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even. sqrt(u) is the correctly rounded binary64 square root; a target whose host sqrt cannot meet this must implement the required result. Normalize accepted input zeros and completed coordinate zeros to +0. Preserve nested interpolation, exact endpoint branches, strictly opposite-sign selection and final endpoint-interval clamp. No FMA, reassociation or binary32 narrowing. Compare all output coordinates, counts and seeded vector state by exact binary64 bits; no output tolerance. Output quantization and finite PRNG units are not an exact continuous probability law. Private/source Java Random and direct-weighted-sum images are not bit-reproduction targets.
environment: IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic and correctly rounded sqrt
Private xoshiro128**1.1 with specified uint32-seed/Two-SplitMix64 expansion
behavior.complexity: O(N) eager work and 2*N retained binary64 slots; O(1) indexed access and O(N) detached toValues materialization. Avoid per-point object allocation in generation. The representation ceiling does not promise allocation success or latency.
behavior.native_errors: Validation and access failures expose code with no dynamic detail. Java exceptions may subclass IllegalArgumentException, JavaScript Error, Python ValueError, with equivalent code fields. There is no dynamic triangle arithmetic error: validated finite input uses the endpoint-aware clamped map. Host allocation failure remains a host resource exception; it is never converted into INVALID_INPUT or partial success. Wrong-type/unrepresentable Java typed host calls are host-call errors.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each positive-count call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0 and q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32. Then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map an unsigned output to unit u=output/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). The all-zero state is unreachable under this expansion and is an internal invariant. State is private, discarded on return/failure and never shared with content/style work. There is no Processing or source palette/background prelude.

guide.title: Sample points in a triangle
guide.summary: Generate uniform retained triangle samples from a seed.
guide.useWhen: Use it for dots, grain, or point-driven marks inside a triangle.

inputs.seed: An integer from 0 to 4294967295. Reuse it with the same inputs to reproduce the result; change it to explore another arrangement.
inputs.count: Nonnegative integer number of points to produce. This is an exact output count; zero returns an empty set.
inputs.triangle: Three finite `[x, y]` vertices in drawing units, forming a triangle with nonzero area. Points are sampled uniformly over its area; either winding is accepted.

guide.output: pointAt(index) returns each sampled local [x,y] coordinate; loop size to place dots or mark origins. toValues() copies them.
guide.tryThis: Draw each point as a dot or use it as a mark origin.

operations.description: Greedily select supplied tapered strips against actual regions using exact clearance comparisons.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed carrier, domain or static correspondence.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Exact declared event reservation exceeds maxWork.
errors.INVALID_REGION: An exclusion region has invalid topology after preflight.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite required arithmetic/display output.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Required distinct exact geometry cannot be represented distinctly.

behavior.validation: Exact passive Object/null-prototype records, dense ordinary arrays with own data slots, no extras/accessors/symbols/coercion; finite binary64 inputs. Validate full carrier/domain before budget. Proxies outside interchange. Every ring has >=3 distinct vertices, implicit closure, nonzero signed area, no duplicate seam/vertex, adjacent backtracking, self-contact, or self-crossing. Holes are strictly inside outer and pairwise disjoint/non-touching. Either winding input; owned output outer CCW/hole CW. Filled membership is outer minus holes. Static validation checks shape/domain, including strip duplicate/reversal rules; exact region topology follows work preflight. Hatch projection/count arithmetic is needed before its budget as explicitly specified. Errors atomic, no mutation/aliases; output zeros positive. Work sums/products use exact integers and compare before allocation; runtime/allocation guarantees do not follow from budgets.
behavior.algorithm: Static-validate all candidate records using strip static rules, IDs (nonempty, unique), clearance, and all exclusion carrier shapes before preflight. Validate exclusion topology after preflight. Visit candidates in input order. If accepted count already equals maxAccepted, append LIMIT with witness kind LIMIT/againstKind NONE/againstIndex -1 and all geometry fields -1 without building candidate. Otherwise construct strip; a rejected strip produces INVALID_STRIP_TOPOLOGY and its witness. Compare actual visible Region2D to exclusions in input order, then accepted actual regions in acceptance order. First INTERSECTS or exact squared distance < exact clearance^2 rejects, with witness copied from comparison, againstKind and zero-based againstIndex. Equality accepts. Accepted witness is NONE with all indices -1. No retries, split, trim, shuffle or guard inflation.
behavior.work: Let C candidates, X exclusions. For candidate i let Ni=point count, Ei=4Ni+4, Qi=2, Vi=Ei^2+8EiQi+4Qi^2. For exclusion j let Fj=total ring edges, Rj=ring count, Uj=Fj^2+8FjRj+4Rj^2. Pair(A,B)=VA+VB+12EAEB+EA+EB. W=sum_i(32Ni+Vi)+sum_j Uj+sum_i sum_j Pair(candidate_i,exclusion_j)+sum_{0<=k<i<C} Pair(candidate_i,candidate_k). Compute W with exact integers after static validation, charging every possible candidate build and comparison regardless of maxAccepted. WORK_LIMIT iff W>maxWork before exclusion topology or candidate construction. This charges repeated region validation within every pair query and varies with exclusion topology.
behavior.environment: No RNG, clock, host renderer, file IO or implicit assets. Consistent caller coordinate units; SVG input explicitly millimetres. Other targets deferred.
behavior.numerics: Topology and clearance thresholds use exact rational arithmetic on supplied binary64 dyadics. Constructed offsets and stated display arithmetic use ordered binary64 with finite checks; no epsilon, snap or repair. Exact shared JSON vectors; additional analytic shape tests compare declared floating arithmetic abs1e-9+rel1e-12 while topology/IDs/order remain exact. Optional outer miter failure falls back exactly as specified.
behavior.native_surface: selectTaperedStrokeStrips2D(input), named p5-package export with stable-code errors.

guide.title: Keep ribbons with room around them
guide.summary: Select ordered variable-width paths that leave the requested negative space.
guide.useWhen: Supply candidate IDs, paths and widths; reuse retained regions for different drawing treatments.

inputs.candidates: Ordered records with id, points, widths, closed, cap, join and miterLimit. Earlier accepted strips take priority.
inputs.clearance: Minimum filled-region separation in position units; equality is accepted.
inputs.exclusions: Strict filled regions that every candidate must avoid.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit computation budget. See the operation contract for its event formula; this is not a millisecond limit.
inputs.maxAccepted: Maximum retained candidates; later records receive static validation and LIMIT reporting, without strip construction or topology checks.

guide.output: {accepted,rejected}: retained strips and explicit rejection reasons/witnesses in deterministic order.
guide.code:
const result = selectTaperedStrokeStrips2D({"candidates":[{"id":"a","points":[[0,0],[4,0]],"widths":[2,2],"closed":false,"cap":"BUTT","join":"BEVEL","miterLimit":1},{"id":"b","points":[[0,3],[4,3]],"widths":[2,2],"closed":false,"cap":"BUTT","join":"BEVEL","miterLimit":1}],"clearance":1,"exclusions":[],"maxAccepted":2,"maxWork":100000});
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Increase clearance while keeping candidate paths fixed, or reorder paths to change which competing marks survive.
pitfalls: This is ordered selection, not a global packing optimum.
Every candidate receives static validation; candidates skipped after the accepted-count cap are not constructed or topology-tested.

operations.description: Synchronously sense a scalar grid with two lateral probes and turn moving agents.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: carrier, grid shape/domain, finite input or control failure
errors.WORK_LIMIT: 3N exceeds maxWork
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: nonfinite interpolation, motion or trig intermediate

behavior.validation: Exact passive plain/null-prototype records and dense ordinary arrays with own data slots only. Validate all agents, the complete scalar grid, controls, and maxWork before work. Input heading and all scalar values must be finite; speed and sensorDistance are nonnegative, sensorAngleTurns in [0,0.5], dt strictly positive. Each array length<=4294967295; columns*rows must be a safe integer<=4294967295 with exact value-array correspondence. Full numeric validation before work; no aliases/mutation/partial output. Exposed zeros canonical positive. Proxies outside interchange.
behavior.sampling: Compute and finite-check gx=(x-originX)/spacingX and gy analog first, even for zero boundary. Zero returns +0 outside inclusive [0,columns-1]×[0,rows-1]; clamp clamps coordinates before interpolation; wrap uses binary64 remainder r=u%extent, if r<0 add extent, and if rounded r>=extent set +0, matching the existing periodic-grid profile; wrap upper indices. Finite-check all primitives. Use row-major bilinear primitives bottom=a+(b-a)*tx, top=c+(d-c)*tx, sample=bottom+(top-bottom)*ty; singleton dimensions reuse their one endpoint. Huge finite wrapped coordinates may lose spatial phase under binary64 arithmetic; do not otherwise repair or reject them if intermediates remain finite.
behavior.order: TAU is the binary64 literal 6.283185307179586. For each old agent in array order, normalize h0=h-floor(h); emit left then right probe at angle TAU*(h0∓sensorAngleTurns) with fdlibm sin/cos and +x-right/+y-down axes; sample left then right; difference=right-left; turn=turnGain*difference; unwrapped=h0+dt*turn; h1=unwrapped-floor(unwrapped); velocity x then y from speed*cos/sin(TAU*h1); position x then y from old position+dt*velocity. Every primitive is finite-checked. Large finite headings or turns may lose phase through binary64 rounding; no silent repair.
behavior.work: Static grid scan is validation. Charge 3N after static validation and before output allocation: two bilinear samples and one advance per agent. Time is O(columns*rows+N), retained output O(N).
behavior.environment: No callback, host image/pixel access, RNG, clock, renderer, agent wrapping, collision, neighbor graph or hidden y inversion.
behavior.numerics: Ordered separate binary64 primitives; finite-check every computed primitive. fdlibm sin/cos/hypot existing audited implementations. Exact shared fixture outputs; independent trigonometric analytical oracles abs1e-12 relative0, indices/errors/counters exact. No epsilon in classification.
behavior.native_surface: sensorMotorStep2D(input); p5-only initial target, named package export; errors carry stable code.

guide.title: Steer marks with paired sensors
guide.summary: Turn moving marks toward or away from differences in a supplied scalar field.
guide.useWhen: Provide old agent positions, headings and speeds; each step samples two probes before updating all agents.

inputs.agents: Records {position,headingTurns,speed}; heading zero points right, positive turns point toward increasing y.
inputs.field: Values, columns, rows, origin at the first cell center, spacing, and explicit clamp/wrap/zero boundary policy.
inputs.sensorDistance: Probe distance from the old position, in position units.
inputs.sensorAngleTurns: Lateral probe angle, in turns, around the old heading.
inputs.turnGain: Signed heading response to right-minus-left sampled field difference.
inputs.dt: Explicit logical time step; no frame clock is read.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit computation budget. See the operation contract for its event formula; this is not a millisecond limit.

guide.output: {agents,probes,samples}: moved agents and the two old-state probe positions/values used for each response.
guide.code:
const result = sensorMotorStep2D({"agents":[{"position":[1.5,0],"headingTurns":0,"speed":0}],"field":{"values":[1,2],"columns":2,"rows":1,"origin":[0,0],"spacing":[1,1],"boundary":"zero"},"sensorDistance":0,"sensorAngleTurns":0,"turnGain":1,"dt":1,"maxWork":3});
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Replace the field while retaining agents, or invert turnGain to reverse the response.
pitfalls: Field wrapping changes sampling, not automatic agent position wrapping.
There is no deposition or field diffusion in this step.

operations.description: Normalize two caller-supplied one-dimensional kernels and filter a straight ARGB8 raster horizontally then vertically in premultiplied encoded RGB.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong keys, shapes, carriers, dimensions/product, count/value/kernel/maxSamples representation; all configuration validation failures.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Validated declared work P*(kernelX.length+kernelY.length) exceeds maxSamples.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: pixelAt index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: A representable pixelAt index is outside the retained output raster.

errorOrder: Validate source then kernelX then kernelY then maxSamples; INVALID_INPUT precedes WORK_LIMIT.

behavior.input: Exactly source,kernelX,kernelY,maxSamples. Source dimensions are positive signed32 and their product is at most 2147483647; pixels is exactly that many unsigned32 values. Each kernel is odd, nonempty, length at most 2147483647, finite binary64 nonnegative weights with a positive maximum. maxSamples is a required safe integer [1,9007199254740991]. No defaults.
behavior.preflight: Object form first validates exact top-level and source keys. Typed form first validates dimensions/product and non-null exact pixel count. Validate source dimensions/product/count/values, then kernelX length/values, kernelY length/values, then maxSamples representation. Compute P*(lenX+lenY) with wide integer arithmetic; if it exceeds maxSamples, fail WORK_LIMIT before allocating normalized kernels, output, or intermediates. Zero taps and length-one axes count. All invalid input precedes WORK_LIMIT.
behavior.normalization: For each axis independently, m=max(weights); in index order q[i]=weights[i]/m; S begins positive zero and adds q[i] in index order; normalized[i]=q[i]/S. Binary64 underflow follows the host format. No epsilon, compensation, fast math, or sum-before-scale normalization.
behavior.filtering: If both axes have length one, return detached original packed bits exactly after validation and preflight. Otherwise horizontally visit row-major outputs and X taps in array order at x+i-floor(lenX/2), clamped to source bounds. Start A,R,G,B at zero; a=alpha/255.0; A+=a*w; for each encoded RGB byte c, premult=c*a then component+=premult*w as separate operations. Store four P-length binary64 arrays. Vertically visit row-major outputs and Y taps in order at y+i-floor(lenY/2), clamped; accumulate stored A,R,G,B times normalized Y. No intermediate byte quantization or clamp. Calculate coordinate-plus-offset using wide integer arithmetic before clamping, never overflowing signed32.
behavior.quantization: Q(v)=floor(min(255,max(0,v))+0.5). If final A==0 output packed zero. Else alpha=Q(A*255); if alpha==0 output zero; channels are Q(component/A), packed ARGB. Arithmetic uses ordered IEEE binary64, separately rounded ties-to-even; no FMA, reassociation, or gamma conversion. Nonidentity filtering ignores hidden transparent RGB and canonicalizes final alpha-zero output.
behavior.ownership: Result is immutable, owns detached packed pixels, retains neither source nor kernels, and pixels()/toValues() return detached values. Failed calls expose no partial result. Inputs must remain stable for the call.
behavior.access: width() and height() expose dimensions. pixelAt(Object/long) first requires a finite safe nonnegative integer, then requires index < width*height. Negative zero is zero. Java pixelAt returns an int ARGB bit pattern; portable toValues pixels are unsigned32.
behavior.native_forms: Java contract form: org.procedurals.raster.SeparableBlur2D.blur(Object) and blur(int width,int height,int[] pixels,double[] kernelX,double[] kernelY,long maxSamples). Result: width(), height(), pixelAt(Object or long), pixels(), toValues(). Implementation and native acceptance remain pending.
behavior.carriers: Object records are exact-key Map and arrays List. Numeric input and Object indices accept only Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float, Double. Reject Boolean, String, BigInteger, BigDecimal, custom Number, null typed buffers, and non-finite/out-of-range forms. Typed kernel values are doubles and typed pixels are int bit patterns.
behavior.limits: Declared work is O(P*(lenX+lenY)); live storage is four P-length double horizontal arrays plus owned P-length output and kernels, O(P+lenX+lenY). No per-pixel objects or full 2D kernel. Allocation failures are host resource failures, never INVALID_INPUT or partial output.
behavior.environment: No RNG, time, noise, renderer, host image, callback, or mutable global state.

guide.title: Blur with explicit kernels
guide.summary: Apply horizontal and vertical kernels to a raster.
guide.useWhen: Use it when blur parameters must be data rather than renderer state.

inputs.source: A plain `{width, height, pixels}` object. Width and height are positive pixel counts; `pixels` contains exactly width × height unsigned `0xAARRGGBB` integers in row order. Convert p5.Image RGBA channels to this packed format first.
inputs.kernelX: An odd-length list of nonnegative horizontal weights, with at least one positive value. The middle entry aligns with the current pixel. Weights are normalized, so [1, 2, 1] and [2, 4, 2] express the same kernel. [1] leaves this axis unblurred.
inputs.kernelY: Vertical weights with the same rules as kernelX. Use a wider kernel for a broader vertical blur, or [1] for horizontal-only filtering. Samples beyond an edge clamp to that edge.
inputs.maxSamples: Positive integer work budget of at least width × height × (kernelX.length + kernelY.length). Zero-weight taps still count. The operation checks this before filtering.

guide.output: pixelAt(index) and pixels() return packed unsigned ARGB8/AARRGGBB values; toValues().pixels is detached data rather than p5 RGBA channels.
guide.tryThis: Create `const image = p.createImage(raster.width, raster.height)` and call `image.loadPixels()`. Convert each packed ARGB32 pixel to RGBA slots: for pixel i, write red `(pixel >>> 16) & 255`, green `(pixel >>> 8) & 255`, blue `pixel & 255`, alpha `pixel >>> 24` at `image.pixels[4*i…4*i+3]`, then call `image.updatePixels()` and draw it with `p.image(image, 0, 0)`.

operations.description: Sequentially move supplied points outward toward the boundaries of ordered supplied discs.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Shape/carrier/nonfinite/radius/strength/budget representation error.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Validated N*M exceeds maxTests.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: A completed projected coordinate is nonfinite.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: pointInto index is not a permitted long index.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index is outside result.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: target/offset cannot receive two values atomically.

behavior.input: Exactly points,discs,strength,maxTests. Empty arrays are valid. Object records use exact-key Map and List rows traversed sequentially; values and Object numeric carriers are only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double. All coordinates/strength are finite binary64; radius>0; strength in [0,1]; maxTests safe integer [0,9007199254740991]. No defaults.
behavior.typed: project(double[] packedXY,double[] packedDiscs,double strength,long maxTests); packedXY length even and packedDiscs length divisible by3. Validate point count/values, discs/count/values, strength, then budget. Both typed arrays must be non-null; size() is point count and points() returns detached packedXY.
behavior.preflight: Validate points then discs then strength then maxTests. Declared signed64 work N*M counts every disc including strength-zero. INVALID_INPUT precedes WORK_LIMIT; work-limit failure precedes output allocation/geometric traversal. Conversion buffers may be allocated before preflight. Object validates exact top-level keys before fields. Array maxima imply N<=1073741823 and M<=715827882; their product fits signed64. No new work-overflow error exists.
behavior.algorithm: At strength==0, after full validation and work preflight, copy points with positive-zero normalization without disc arithmetic. For each point in input order, visit discs in supplied order and update current coordinates. dx=x-cx and dy=y-cy; if either is infinite, skip that disc. hi=max(abs(dx),abs(dy)), lo=min(...); d=0 if hi=0 else hi*sqrt(1+(lo/hi)*(lo/hi)). Infinite d is outside. If d>=radius skip. Otherwise direction=(dx/d,dy/d), except d=0 uses (1,0); gap=radius-d; movement=strength*gap; newX=x+(ux*movement), newY=y+(uy*movement), each ordered binary64 operation. Nonfinite new coordinate fails NUMERIC_OVERFLOW atomically.
behavior.numeric: Separate IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-even; correctly rounded sqrt; no FMA, reassociation, epsilon, trigonometry, RNG/time/host/renderer state. Normalize completed output zeros to positive zero. Axis vectors compare exactly; nonaxis vector coordinates use abs 1e-12 plus relative 1e-12 fixture tolerance.
behavior.ownership: Immutable owned result; result size equals N and preserves order. points() and toValues() detach. Inputs are stable for call and never retained; failure publishes no result.
behavior.access: size(); pointInto(long index,double[] target,int offset). Validate index in [0,MAX_SAFE] first (INVALID_INDEX), then index<size (INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE), then non-null target and overflow-safe offset>=0 and offset+2<=length (INVALID_OUTPUT), with no partial target write.
behavior.limits: O(N*M+N+M) work and primitive-array storage; no typed-loop per-point objects. This is one-pass deformation, not containment, collision resolution, clipping, Voronoi or a non-overlap guarantee.
behavior.native_forms: org.procedurals.geometry.DiscProjection2D.project(Object) and project(double[] packedXY,double[] packedDiscs,double strength,long maxTests); result size(),points(),toValues(),pointInto(long index,double[] target,int offset). No Object index overload.

guide.title: Project points out of discs
guide.summary: Move points through ordered disc influences.
guide.useWhen: Use it for a simple geometry adjustment before drawing.

inputs.points: Finite `[x, y]` positions to adjust. The result keeps the same count and order; the input list remains unchanged.
inputs.discs: Ordered `[centerX, centerY, radius]` circles, with positive radii. A point inside a disc moves toward its edge before the next disc is tested. Order therefore matters; a later move can enter an earlier disc again.
inputs.strength: A value from 0 to 1. Zero leaves points unchanged; one moves an interior point to the current disc’s edge; intermediate values move it partway. An exact-center point moves along positive X.
inputs.maxTests: Nonnegative integer budget of at least points.length × discs.length, including when strength is zero. This is one pass through the discs, not an iterative collision solver.

guide.output: pointInto(index,out,offset) writes each final local [x,y], while points() returns a packed coordinate array and toValues().points returns [x,y] pairs. Loop size to draw those points.
guide.tryThis: Draw the projected points with your own symbols.

operations.description: Deterministically simplify an open polyline.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed input.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Preflight exceeds budget.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite computed value.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. Complete static shape/value validation precedes work preflight. Geometric/topology tests run after preflight. Failure throws Error with stable code, no partial result. Outputs are detached. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0. Array lengths must fit 4294967295; unsafe requested growth/work arithmetic gives WORK_LIMIT before allocation. Host resource exhaustion is a host error, not an allocation guarantee.
behavior.environment: No ambient RNG, noise, clock, renderer, assets or retained state. All geometry uses caller coordinates; p5 examples use their own canvas convention. Randomness, where present, is explicit input/output rngState.
behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. Check computed numeric intermediates for finiteness and throw NUMERIC_OVERFLOW on nonfinite results. No epsilon in classification or topology, no adaptive exact predicates or near-degeneracy guarantee. General scalar/coordinate comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; topology, indices, order, booleans and RNG states compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exact JSON output.
behavior.algorithm:
Input: points (at least one xy point), tolerance (nonnegative), maxWork.
Output: {points,sourceIndices}. This operation is explicitly open; callers choose
a seam before simplifying a loop. Retain endpoints. For each endpoint interval,
measure each interior point's Euclidean distance to the finite segment, using
clamped projection; coincident segment endpoints use distance to the endpoint.
Choose the earliest source index among equal maximum distances. Split only when
maximum distance > tolerance. Process left interval before right, avoiding host
recursion limits. Return retained indices in ascending order. A one-point input
returns that point/index. Preflight N*N <= maxWork, safe integer arithmetic.
This conservative quadratic bound removes input-dependent budget surprises.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export simplifyPolyline2D(input) from packages/javascript/src/simplify-polyline-2d.js. Other targets deferred.
behavior.projection: For A,B, d=B-A and length=hypot(d). If length==0, distance=hypot(P-A). Otherwise projection=(P-A) dot (d/length), clamp projection to [0,length], closest=A+(projection/length)*d, then distance=hypot(P-closest). Each multiply/add/divide is checked separately.

guide.title: Keep decisive polyline turns
guide.summary: Retains an open path's endpoints and the points beyond its tolerance.
guide.useWhen: Use it to turn sampled gestures into editable skeletons.
guide.output: {points,sourceIndices}, detached retained vertices and their original indices.
guide.code:
const result = simplifyPolyline2D({ points: [[0,0],[1,1],[2,0]], tolerance: .5, maxWork: 9 });
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Raise tolerance to remove smaller bends.
pitfalls: This is explicitly open; choose a loop seam before calling it.

operations.description: Pack supplied rectangles in input order by deterministic lowest skyline placement.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed input.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Preflight exceeds work budget.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Computed value nonfinite.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. Complete static shape/value validation precedes work preflight. Geometric/topology tests run after preflight. Failure throws Error with stable code, no partial result. Outputs are detached. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0. Array lengths must fit 4294967295; unsafe requested growth/work arithmetic gives WORK_LIMIT before allocation. Host resource exhaustion is a host error, not an allocation guarantee.
behavior.environment: No ambient RNG, noise, clock, renderer, assets or retained state. All geometry uses caller coordinates; p5 examples use their own canvas convention. Randomness, where present, is explicit input/output rngState.
behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. Check computed numeric intermediates for finiteness and throw NUMERIC_OVERFLOW on nonfinite results. No epsilon in classification or topology, no adaptive exact predicates or near-degeneracy guarantee. General scalar/coordinate comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; topology, indices, order, booleans and RNG states compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exact JSON output.
behavior.algorithm:
Input: width,height (>0), rectangles (array {width,height} both >0), maxWork.
Output: {placements,unplaced}; placement {index,x,y,width,height}, unplaced is
ascending original indices. Process rectangles in supplied order, no rotation,
padding or implicit sorting. Skyline initially one horizontal span [0,width] at
y=0. Candidate x positions are each current span's start. Candidate y is maximum
height of skyline spans with left < x+rect.width and right > x (positive-width overlap only). Reject right/bottom
overflow. Select smallest y+rect.height, then smallest x. Insert the new top
height across its width, retaining left/right fragments, and merge adjacent
equal-height spans. Failure places nothing and preserves skyline; continue.
Coordinates at touching boundaries count as fitting. Returned placement order
is input processing order with failures omitted. Preflight 8*N*N*N+N <= maxWork, covering the naive candidate/span scan.
This is a deterministic heuristic, not globally optimal bin packing.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export skylinePack2D(input) from packages/javascript/src/skyline-pack-2d.js. Other targets deferred.
behavior.placement_order: No rotation, sorting or implicit padding. Return placed records in original processing order and unplaced IDs ascending. Reject nonfinite fit arithmetic even for a candidate that would not fit. Do not count zero-width span-boundary touching as overlap.

guide.title: Pack rectangles
guide.summary: Place ordered rectangles with a skyline heuristic.
guide.useWhen: Place ordered rectangles with a skyline heuristic.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static keys/carriers/count, nonfinite/out-of-range position, duplicate/descending position or nonintegral/out-of-range RGB24 color; no partial ramp.

behavior.creation: Validate exact object with stops only, then stops List length in[1,2147483647]. In input order validate each exact {position,color} record; position is finite binary64 in[0,1], strictly greater than previous position after conversion; color is finite integral RGB24. Reject duplicates/unsorted positions; do not sort. Canonicalize position zero to +0. Typed create(double[] positions,int[] colors) checks nonnull, positive equal lengths then position/color in the same order. int colors must be nonnegative RGB24, not signed ARGB. All validation precedes exposing a result. No defaults.
behavior.carriers: Java Map records, List containers, and only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double numeric carriers. Reject boolean, null, string, arrays in object route, BigInteger/BigDecimal and arbitrary Number subclasses before coercion. Convert allowed coordinates/query to binary64; validate RGB24 integers before narrowing. Passive stable inputs assumed; concurrent caller mutation during call is outside contract.
behavior.query_validation: sample(Object) accepts the same six numeric carriers and sample(double) accepts a finite binary64 value. Reject invalid query with INVALID_QUERY even for one stop. All finite queries including extreme values are valid.
behavior.sampling: If query<=first position return first color; if query>=last position return last color. Otherwise locate neighboring positions L<=query<R by ordered binary search. If query==L return its color. Compute numerator=query-L, denominator=R-L, t=numerator/denominator, each operation separately rounded binary64. For each encoded channel a,b: d=b-a; p=d*t; value=a+p; rounded=floor(value+0.5), every primitive separately rounded binary64. Pack R*65536+G*256+B exactly. No FMA/reassociation, gamma conversion, alpha, easing or cyclic wrapping. Primitive arithmetic uses IEEE round-to-nearest ties-to-even.
behavior.ownership: Immutable owned snapshot; retain no caller arrays, Maps or Lists. serialize returns newly owned object/list/stop records. Later caller mutation of input or exports cannot change sampling or serialization. No mutable insertion operation.

At a noncollinear turn, classify inside and outside by the exact sign of the centerline cross product: a left turn has left inner/right outer; a right turn has right inner/left outer. The inner side intersects supporting tapered-side lines in exact dyadic/rational arithmetic. Its intersection must lie within both adjoining finite tapered-side sections, including endpoints; a parallel noncoincident pair or out-of-range intersection rejects INVALID_STRIP_TOPOLOGY. A coincident parallel pair shares its common vertex sample if one exists, otherwise rejects. Round the exact intersection once to nearest-even binary64, emit one trim sample and record INNER. If rounding is nonfinite, coincides with a required distinct neighboring sample, or makes topology invalid, reject INVALID_STRIP_TOPOLOGY. The outer side BEVEL emits incoming and outgoing samples. Outer MITER uses the exact rational supporting-line intersection only when the rounded point is distinct and exact squared distance from center vertex <= exact (halfWidth*miterLimit)^2; otherwise it falls back to BEVEL, including nonfinite or representation failure of the optional miter. Collinear same-direction edges share one side sample and mark CONTINUOUS; exact reversal or adjacent coincident centerline points is INVALID_INPUT. A nonfinite base tangent/normal/sample is NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. Validate each assembled ring with exact dyadic topology; only equal consecutive join samples are deduplicated. Invalid open outer ring, or closed output other than exactly one disjoint enclosing outer plus one hole, returns REJECTED INVALID_STRIP_TOPOLOGY. Output ring outer is CCW, hole CW; each normalized ring rotates to its lexicographically least [x,y] vertex (ties impossible in a valid ring). Left/rightBoundary keep traversal order, not ring winding. Accepted witness is NONE/all -1. Rejected witness is first invalid ring/edge/vertex in ring order; unavailable fields -1. LeftBoundary and rightBoundary both follow original centerline forward traversal, with incoming then outgoing samples at each outer bevel; neither boundary is reversed. Only visible rings are winding-normalized and lex-rotated. Exact left turn means positive cross under x/y coordinates, independent of canvas handedness.

operations.description: Advance an ordered independent target-spring state by one explicit logical step: target force, position using updated velocity, then velocity retention. State carries each body's position, velocity and coefficients. Native execution owns a mutable fixed-size batch with atomic steps and detached observations; no pointer, clock, RNG, renderer, topology or convergence guarantee.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-model static state or targets; includes length mismatch.
errors.SPRING_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: First nonfinite step intermediate; bodyIndex,axis,stage; state unchanged.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index not representable as finite nonnegative safe integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Safe index outside retained bodies.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: Into destination cannot hold a pair at offset; atomic failure.

behavior.validation: Passive JSON-compatible data only. Validate exact outer keys state/targets, then complete state, then complete targets. State is exactly bodies; bodies list length N0..357913941. Each body has exactly position,velocity,strength,retention; validate body order, position x/y,velocity x/y,strength,retention. Pairs exactly two finite binary64 numeric values; booleans/strings are not numbers. Strength finite>=0,retention finite0..1. Targets must be list lengthN of finite pairs, validated in body/x/y order. All static validation precedes recurrence and output-sized owned allocation for the portable transition. Canonicalize input zeros positive. No omitted fields/defaults.
behavior.step: For body i=0..N-1, compute full x axis then full y axis. Each primitive rounds separately to binary64 round-to-nearest-even: delta=target-position; force=delta*strength; advanced=velocity+force; nextPosition=position+advanced; nextVelocity=advanced*retention. Check finiteness immediately after EACH primitive in this order. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 truncation or implicit dt. Preserve intermediate signed zeros and gradual underflow; canonicalize completed position/velocity zeros positive before storing/reuse.
behavior.errors: Complete invalid static input always fails INVALID_INPUT before arithmetic, including a late invalid target preceding an earlier would-be overflow. First nonfinite intermediate fails SPRING_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with exactly bodyIndex,axis (x/y),stage (delta/force/advanced/position/velocity). No output on failure. Native current values and coefficients remain unchanged, even if earlier items computed prospective scratch values.
behavior.zero: N0 requires an empty target list and performs no recurrence. Strength0 still computes delta and force and transports existing velocity. Retention0 still computes and stores the current position advance before discarding next velocity. Do not optimize away possible overflow for either zero coefficient. Coincident bodies are independent and keep separate indices. No epsilon, merging, clipping, bounds enforcement or sleep threshold.
behavior.ownership: Portable transition leaves input data unchanged and returns detached state. Native factory creates owned mutable current state; step mutates only after full success. Read access never advances. No caller input array/map/list remains aliased; each export/At returns detached data. No retained initial-state copy, reset method, history, or automatic clock. A detached state export can be edited/imported as another independent batch for replay or coefficient changes. Concurrent reads/mutation of batch or mutation of input during a call are not supported.
behavior.storage: N<=floor(2147483647/6)=357913941 keeps packed six-scalar state signed32-indexable. This representational ceiling is not an allocation guarantee or artistic range. Factory validates all static inputs before output-sized buffers. Explicit step authorizes O(N) work. Own O(N) current/scratch/captured-target storage, reusable between steps; no per-body allocation/parsing/reflection in numeric loop. Host resource exceptions remain host failures, never INVALID_INPUT or a partial result. Atomicity concerns failed calls, not concurrent publication.

Accept passive Map with exact string keys and Lists; supported numeric carriers Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double, converted to finite double. Reject other Number types, arrays as canonical records, bool/string/null. Return fixed-size owned batch. Public construction does not run a tick.
behavior.java_step: void step(Object targets) accepts canonical List of pairs OR double[] packed XY targets; void step(double[] targets) is the typed fast overload with identical packed semantics, including when array arrives through Object. Packed length exactly2N. Reject float[],other primitive arrays,wrong lengths/null/nonfinite values. Validate/capture the complete target input into owned reusable storage before recurrence, then compute next values into separate reusable scratch; commit only after full success. Targets are not retained between calls. Coefficients fixed per batch; zero allocation in a warmed successful packed-target numeric loop is a later performance obligation.

operations.description: Interpret explicit token commands into retained planar segments with stack-restored pose and branch depth.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed shape, supplied scalar/carrier/domain, impossible array representation, or operation-specific static constraint.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: The exact required or next charged work exceeds maxWork or safe work representation.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: A computed floating primitive is nonfinite; no partial state or geometry escapes.
errors.UNKNOWN_TOKEN: A token has no command under ERROR policy; tokenIndex identifies it.
errors.OUTPUT_LIMIT: The next DRAW exceeds maxSegments; tokenIndex identifies it.
errors.STACK_LIMIT: The next PUSH exceeds maxStackDepth; tokenIndex identifies it.
errors.STACK_UNDERFLOW: POP has no stored pose; tokenIndex identifies it.

Numeric carriers are finite binary64 and never booleans; integral fields are exact integers in schema domain. Reject accessors, host instances and coercion. Complete static validation of every field/element precedes work preflight, RNG draws or output allocation. Products defining array lengths must be exact and <=4294967295 or INVALID_INPUT, even if all individual dimensions are valid. Canonicalize input zeros to +0.

Budgets are abstract work, not memory or latency guarantees; host allocation failure remains a host error.
behavior.numerics: Separate binary64 primitive rounding, no reassociation/FMA. Every computed primitive must be finite or NUMERIC_OVERFLOW, including division by an underflowed zero denominator. No numerical repair, implicit epsilon or state clipping. Exposed zeros are +0. General finite output fields use absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; integer/topology/order/state/token values compare exactly. The bound fixture file contains only exact analytical outputs; approximate RK4 linear-field and nonzero-angle turtle geometry tests remain separate future property tests.
behavior.ownership: Read only caller inputs; output records and arrays are detached. No input record, array, RNG object, renderer, host state or callback is retained. All generated state remains private until success. No partial result on error; a successful RK4 boundary termination is its explicit retained-prefix result, not an error. Scalars and immutable strings are values.
behavior.tokens: A token is a nonempty string treated as one atomic symbol. Compare exact UTF-16 code-unit sequences with no Unicode normalization or character splitting. Rule/command token keys are unique; unknown tokens follow the operation-specific passthrough or unknown-token policy.
behavior.algorithm:
Table-driven planar turtle

Proposed ID: `geometry.token-turtle-2d`; generator.

Artist output: retained segments with source token and branch-depth identity. Studies:
bracketed botanical fans; geometric space-filling paths. It consumes explicit tokens,
including candidate17 output, without hiding rewriting or assuming an L-system alphabet.

Input:

```text
{tokens:[token,...], commands:[command,...],
 start:{position:[number,number],heading:number}, unknown:"IGNORE"|"ERROR",
 maxSegments:integer in [0,4294967295],
 maxStackDepth:integer in [0,4294967295], maxWork:integer}
```

Command union (exact keys per variant): `{token,kind:"DRAW"|"MOVE",distance:number}`;
`{token,kind:"TURN",angle:number}`; `{token,kind:"PUSH"|"POP"}`. Tokens follow candidate17's
string domain, with unique command tokens. Signed distance is allowed; angles/headings
are radians without implicit wrapping. No implicit F, +, [, ] or style commands.

Output:
`{segments:[[x1,y1,x2,y2],...],sourceIndices:[integer,...],depths:[integer,...],
position:[x,y],heading:number}`.

Reserve W=commands.length+3*tokens.length. Visit tokens in order. Unknown tokens either
do nothing or raise UNKNOWN_TOKEN with tokenIndex. DRAW/MOVE computes
`dx=distance*cos(heading)`, `dy=distance*sin(heading)`, then x+dx and y+dy, checked in that
order. DRAW checks maxSegments before calculation, appends a segment even if zero length,
and records token index and current stack depth. MOVE only updates pose. TURN adds angle.
PUSH checks depth limit then copies the current pose; POP requires a nonempty stack and
restores its final pose. Unbalanced final nonempty stack raises UNBALANCED_STACK, without
partial output. Exceeding capacity raises OUTPUT_LIMIT or STACK_LIMIT, with tokenIndex;
empty pop raises STACK_UNDERFLOW with tokenIndex. Work O(tokens+commands), retained output
O(draws), temporary stack O(maximum actual depth), never preallocated to maxStackDepth.

inputs.start: Initial position and heading in radians.
inputs.unknown: IGNORE or ERROR handling for absent commands.

guide.output: {segments,sourceIndices,depths,position,heading}.
guide.code:
const result = tokenTurtle2D({ tokens:["F","+","F"], commands:[{token:"F",kind:"DRAW",distance:10},{token:"+",kind:"TURN",angle:1.57}], start:{position:[0,0],heading:0}, unknown:"ERROR", maxSegments:2, maxStackDepth:0, maxWork:20 });

guide.tryThis: Use PUSH and POP around a branch to return to its parent endpoint.
