operations.description: retained planar mapping of caller-provided unit-coordinate pairs through one explicitly supplied ordered triangle. It owns no random stream or distribution claim.

items.description: Ordered closed-unit [u,v] pairs; the operation does not assert their distribution.
Retained planar [x,y] positions in generation order.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, invalid triangle coordinate or u/v outside closed unit interval.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside 0..size()-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination/offset lacks two writable binary64 slots.

behavior.input: Static validation order: outer passive record and exact keys; triangle container; vertex0 x/y; vertex1 x/y; vertex2 x/y; unitCoordinates container/length; then each row i in ascending order with pair shape, u then v. All numbers are finite binary64 and never bool; u/v are closed [0,1]. Normalize accepted zeros to +0. Validate every later pair before output-sized allocation. No defaults and no RNG initialization.
behavior.mapping: for each [u,v], calculate s=correctlyRoundedBinary64Sqrt(u), then independently for x and y calculate L(A,L(B,C,v),s). For L(a,b,t), t=0 returns canonical +0-normalized a and t=1 returns canonical +0-normalized b. Otherwise, when a and b have strictly opposite signs (one <0 and one >0), evaluate raw=round64(round64(a*round64(1-t))+round64(b*t)); otherwise evaluate raw=round64(a+round64(round64(b-a)*t)). Clamp raw to the closed finite [min(a,b),max(a,b)] endpoint interval and canonicalize zero to +0. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion or implicit clamp omission.
behavior.distribution: No RNG is read, consumed or returned. No uniformity claim is implicit: independent uniform unit pairs are a caller-side condition for uniform area sampling; biased expressions are caller composition, not source-named public modes.
behavior.degeneracy: Accept every finite ordered vertex triple, including repeated or collinear triples, as the same collapsed mapping. Compute no area/determinant and use no epsilon or minimum-size gate. Ideal uniform-area interpretation applies only to nondegenerate geometry; a collapsed segment is not promised uniform arclength density. A positive seeded count consumes exactly two units per point even for repeated vertices. Empty outputs still validate every required field.
behavior.layout: N=unitCoordinates length. The result retains 2*N binary64 slots; N<=1073741823 is representational only. Host allocation failure returns no result, is not INVALID_INPUT and never supplies partial output.
behavior.ownership: Match CP4 passive-carrier rules. Do not retain caller triangle/pair lists; successful output owns detached packed points. Complete static validation before output-sized allocation. Only bounded-size triangle metadata may be copied earlier. pointAt and toValues return detached materializations; failure of a fresh materialization leaves the existing result unchanged. No serialize/toJSON/config replay, callback/iterator input, IDs or count aliases.
behavior.access: size() in Java and size property/getter in JavaScript/Python returns retained point count. pointAt/point_at returns a fresh two-component binary64 point: Java double[], JavaScript ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list. Index must be finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991, never bool; integral floating indices accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (index>=size), then INVALID_OUTPUT for pointInto/point_into. Require a finite nonnegative integral offset and two writable binary64 slots; reject Float32 buffers and leave all destination slots unchanged on failure. Java pointInto has required typed int offset and returns void; wrong-type/unrepresentable typed host calls are host-call errors. JavaScript pointInto(index,out,offset=0) returns out; Python point_into(index,out,offset=0) returns None. Validate offset/index before narrowing.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.sampling.TrianglePoints2D.map(Object config), shared result size(), pointAt(Object or long), pointInto(index,double[],int), toValues(). JavaScript mapTriangleCoordinates2D(config), shared result size property, pointAt, pointInto(offset default0), toValues. Python map_triangle_coordinates_2d(config), shared result size property, point_at, point_into(offset default0), to_values.
behavior.native_types: Follow established portable carrier rules: Java accepts Map records and List vertex/pair containers of the specified lengths; only Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double numeric values are accepted, rejecting BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript accepts passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Array pairs; Python accepts exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs with int/float but never bool. PVector, typed-array pair input, class instances, active accessors/proxies and custom mapping/list containers are not interchange inputs. Java pointInto uses double[]; future JavaScript accepts Float64Array or writable ordinary Array and Python exact builtin list or array(d). Python huge-integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT or INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception; validate integral domains before conversion where applicable.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar [x,y] coordinates in an unchanged coordinate system; dimensionless unit coordinates. No axis flip, winding normalization, canvas conversion, topology, area/count allocation, palette/style, clipping or drawing.
behavior.numerics: Every stated primitive uses IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even. sqrt(u) is the correctly rounded binary64 square root; a target whose host sqrt cannot meet this must implement the required result. Normalize accepted input zeros and completed coordinate zeros to +0. Preserve nested interpolation, exact endpoint branches, strictly opposite-sign selection and final endpoint-interval clamp. No FMA, reassociation or binary32 narrowing. Compare all output coordinates, counts and seeded vector state by exact binary64 bits; no output tolerance. Output quantization and finite PRNG units are not an exact continuous probability law. Private/source Java Random and direct-weighted-sum images are not bit-reproduction targets.
environment: IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic and correctly rounded sqrt
behavior.complexity: O(N) eager mapping and 2*N retained binary64 slots; O(1) indexed access and O(N) detached export. Avoid per-point objects. The ceiling is not a performance guarantee.
behavior.native_errors: Validation and access failures expose code with no dynamic detail. Java exceptions may subclass IllegalArgumentException, JavaScript Error, Python ValueError, with equivalent code fields. There is no dynamic triangle arithmetic error: validated finite input uses the endpoint-aware clamped map. Host allocation failure remains a host resource exception; it is never converted into INVALID_INPUT or partial success. Wrong-type/unrepresentable Java typed host calls are host-call errors.

guide.title: Map chosen triangle coordinates
guide.summary: Turn supplied unit pairs into retained points in a triangle.
guide.useWhen: Use it when you want a custom distribution instead of seeded uniform samples.

inputs.triangle: Three finite `[x, y]` vertices with nonzero area, in your drawing units. Either winding works. The mapping preserves your coordinate-pair order.
inputs.unitCoordinates: Your chosen `[u, v]` pairs, each value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The map uses sqrt(u) to convert the unit square to triangle area coordinates. Uniform independent pairs give area-uniform points; patterned pairs create your own distribution. The operation itself draws no random numbers.

guide.output: pointAt(index) returns each mapped local [x,y] in unitCoordinates order; loop size to draw those points. toValues() copies them.
guide.tryThis: Generate unit coordinates with your own rule, then map them once.

operations.description: Ear-clip a strict simple polygon into original-index triangles.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed input.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Preflight exceeds budget.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite computed value.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the required schema keys in plain passive JSON-compatible objects and dense ordinary arrays, with finite binary64 values and safe integer descriptors; no coercion, defaults, accessors, booleans-as-numbers or retained aliases. Complete static shape/value validation precedes work preflight. Geometric/topology tests run after preflight. Failure throws Error with stable code, no partial result. Outputs are detached. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0. Array lengths must fit 4294967295; unsafe requested growth/work arithmetic gives WORK_LIMIT before allocation. Host resource exhaustion is a host error, not an allocation guarantee.
behavior.environment: No ambient RNG, noise, clock, renderer, assets or retained state. All geometry uses caller coordinates; p5 examples use their own canvas convention. Randomness, where present, is explicit input/output rngState.
behavior.numerics: Separate IEEE754 binary64 arithmetic, Math.hypot and host sin/cos/sqrt for the named formulas. Check computed numeric intermediates for finiteness and throw NUMERIC_OVERFLOW on nonfinite results. No epsilon in classification or topology, no adaptive exact predicates or near-degeneracy guarantee. General scalar/coordinate comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; topology, indices, order, booleans and RNG states compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exact JSON output.
behavior.algorithm:
Input: points (at least three xy vertices, no repeated seam), maxWork.
Output: {points,triangles}. points is a detached unchanged vertex list; triangles
contains triples of original vertex indices. Require distinct vertices, nonzero
signed shoelace area, no intersecting/touching nonadjacent edges, and no collinear
consecutive triple. These intentionally strict simple polygons exclude holes and
degenerate boundary runs. INVALID_TOPOLOGY for these violations. Normalize only
the working index ring to positive winding (positive input [0..N-1], negative
input [N-1..0]); never reorder output points. Ear candidates are scanned from
ring position zero each pass. A candidate is a strict positive turn and its
closed triangle contains no other remaining vertex (edges included). Emit
[previous,current,next], remove current, restart scan. Final ring emits its
three indices in ring order. No ear -> INVALID_TOPOLOGY. Preflight N*N*N + N*N
<= maxWork; reject unsafe count before geometric allocations. General binary64
orientation, not adaptive predicates; near-degenerate classifications may fail.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export triangulateSimplePolygon2D(input) from packages/javascript/src/triangulate-simple-polygon-2d.js. Other targets deferred.

guide.title: Split a strict polygon into ears
guide.summary: Produces deterministic triangle indices for a simple nondegenerate boundary.
guide.useWhen: Use it to color facets inside a supplied silhouette.

inputs.points: At least three distinct [x,y] boundary vertices.

guide.output: {points,triangles}; triangles are original point indices with positive working winding.
guide.code:
const result = triangulateSimplePolygon2D({ points: [[0,0],[4,0],[4,4],[2,2],[0,4]], maxWork: 150 });
console.log(result);
guide.tryThis: Fill each returned index triple with a palette color.
pitfalls: Touching, self-intersecting, repeated, and collinear-boundary polygons are rejected.

operations.description: Return nearest-site cells clipped to an explicit axis-aligned rectangle.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed input, nonfinite supplied number or violated shape/domain constraint.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Required work exceeds explicit maxWork, or work-count arithmetic is not a safe integer.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: A computed geometry or scalar intermediate is nonfinite.

behavior.validation: Accept exactly the input keys and plain JSON-compatible objects/arrays, finite numeric values (not booleans), and safe integer count/budget fields. Validate complete input before computation. maxWork is required nonnegative safe integer. No coercion, defaults or hidden allocation retries. Failure throws an Error with stable code. No partial result. Canonicalize exposed signed zero to +0.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, renderer, assets or host state. Coordinates use caller units, x right and y down in p5 examples; algorithm works in either coordinate orientation. Inputs are copied or read only, output detached; no retained aliases.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 separate arithmetic operations, no epsilon in classification or topology. Reject every nonfinite computed intermediate with NUMERIC_OVERFLOW. General coordinate and length comparisons allow absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-12; integer indices, output order and topology compare exactly. Analytical shared fixtures use exactly representable cases and exact comparison. No exact-predicate robustness promise for nearly degenerate inputs.
behavior.algorithm: bounds=[minX,minY,maxX,maxY] with minX<maxX and minY<maxY. Sites may lie outside bounds; empty sites yields cells=[]. Produce one cell per site in original order. Exact duplicate sites (signed zero equal) belong only to first site; later cells=[]. Start each cell [(minX,minY),(maxX,minY),(maxX,maxY),(minX,maxY)]. For each other site in input order, skip equal duplicate, clip by a*(x-midX)+b*(y-midY)<=0 where a=other.x-site.x,b=other.y-site.y,midX=site.x+a/2,midY=site.y+b/2. Visit polygon edges previous->current with previous initialized last vertex; inside-inside append current, outside-inside append intersection then current, inside-outside append intersection, outside-outside append nothing. Intersection t=dPrevious/(dPrevious-dCurrent), point=previous+t*(current-previous). Boundary is inside. No coordinate snapping.
behavior.canonicalization: After each clip remove consecutive exactly equal points including duplicate closing point. Retain collinear vertices. At completion remove cells with fewer than three vertices or exactly zero signed double area (sum cross-products in polygon order). Preserve rectangle winding; rotate each nonempty polygon to lexicographically smallest [x,y] vertex, first occurrence wins. Empty/point/line cells are []. Numeric rounding can collapse cells; no repair or exact geometric guarantee.
behavior.budget: Before processing, charge N*N work for duplicate/comparison preflight (safe arithmetic required). Then charge one work unit for each polygon edge visited during clipping. If total would exceed maxWork, throw WORK_LIMIT before that visit. Empty input costs 0. Worst-case O(N^3) clipping work, O(N^2) retained output, bounded by supplied maxWork; no universal latency guarantee.
behavior.native_surface: p5.js named export voronoiCells2D(input) from packages/javascript/src/voronoi-cells-2d.js; plain output matching output_schema. Other targets deferred.

guide.title: Divide a rectangle into nearest-site cells
guide.summary: Create polygon regions around supplied sites.
guide.useWhen: Use it for mosaics, nested cell outlines or independently styled regions.

inputs.sites: Ordered finite [x, y] points, in your drawing units. Moving one changes its nearest-site region. Sites may lie outside the bounds; exact duplicates belong to their first occurrence.
inputs.bounds: [minX, minY, maxX, maxY] with strictly positive width and height. Every returned cell is clipped to this rectangle.
inputs.maxWork: Nonnegative safe integer work allowance. The operation charges sites.length squared, then one unit per polygon edge visited while clipping. An insufficient budget throws WORK_LIMIT without returning partial cells.

guide.output: The plain result {cells} contains one polygon per input site, in the same order. Each polygon is an array of [x,y] vertices with implicit closure; [] represents an empty or later-duplicate cell. Outputs are detached from your inputs.
guide.tryThis: For each nonempty cell call p.beginShape(), emit its vertices, then p.endShape(p.CLOSE). Change the sites to edit boundaries; reuse the same polygons for different drawing treatments.
pitfalls: Nearly degenerate geometry uses binary64 arithmetic without an exact-predicate guarantee.
Shrinking a cell toward its site is a drawing choice, not an equal-distance polygon inset.

operations.description: Move sites synchronously to exact pixel-mass centroids of their nearest-site assignments.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed carrier, dimensions, weights, sites or scalar domain.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Specified deterministic event count exceeds maxWork or safe-integer work.

behavior.validation: Exact required own string keys on passive ordinary/null-prototype records; dense ordinary arrays with own data slots only, no extras, symbols, accessors or coercion. Proxies outside interchange. Validate all fields in schema order, every weight/site, and dimensions before budget; width*height<=2147483647 and equals weights.length. Arrays/count<=2147483647. All scalars finite. No partial result or input mutation/retention. Canonicalize exposed -0. Host allocation failures remain host errors.
behavior.environment: Raster row-major: flat index=row*width+column, pixel area [column,column+1]x[row,row+1], center (column+0.5,row+0.5), x right/y down. Weight is dimensionless relative mass, zero has none. No asset, renderer, luminance conversion, clock or host RNG; caller supplies weights.
behavior.native_surface: weightedRasterCentroids2D(input), WeightedRasterCentroids2DError with stable code. First target p5.js package; other targets deferred.
behavior.order: Validate each site coordinate within closed [0,width]x[0,height]. Let M count positive-weight pixels and S sites. Empty sites with positive total mass are INVALID_INPUT even before budget; empty sites with zero mass return empty arrays after budget. For each positive pixel center row-major, choose nearest original site by exact squared Euclidean distance on binary64 dyadic values; exact ties choose lowest index. Accumulate mass and weighted integer column/row sums exactly. Output site coordinate is exact rational (2*sum(weight*column)+mass)/(2*mass), and analogously row, rounded once nearest-even binary64. Zero-mass site returns detached original point, canonical +0. All assignments use original sites; this is one synchronous step.
behavior.work: Reserve exact P+M*S after full static validation, including empty-site rule; WORK_LIMIT if above maxWork or safe integer. Before output allocation and distance work. P counts weights; M*S counts nearest-site comparisons. Time O(P+M*S), storage O(P+S) at most; no implicit iteration, acceleration or stochastic reseeding.
behavior.numerics: Exact dyadic squared distances and integer accumulators. Final rational coordinates round once to nearest-even binary64. Masses are exact safe integers. No epsilon, approximate winner, tolerance in fixtures or centroid damping.

guide.title: Relax marks toward weighted centers
guide.summary: Move sites once toward the image mass assigned to each nearest site.
guide.useWhen: You already have site positions and want one synchronous, mass-weighted layout update.

inputs.width: Raster width in pixel cells; each pixel center is at column + 0.5.
inputs.height: Raster height in pixel cells; each pixel center is at row + 0.5.
inputs.weights: Row-major nonnegative integer masses; zero-weight cells do not participate.
inputs.sites: Original [x,y] sites inside the closed raster bounds. Exact distance ties choose the first site.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit cap for P pixel inspections plus M positive pixels times S sites.

guide.output: {sites,masses}: one detached centroid per original site and its assigned integer mass. Empty sites retain their original positions.
guide.code:
const result = weightedRasterCentroids2D({width:3,height:2,weights:[0,2,5,1,0,3],sites:[[0.5,0.5],[2.5,1.5]],maxWork:100});
console.log(result.sites, result.masses);
guide.tryThis: Use sampled marks as the sites, then call this operation once per deliberate relaxation step while retaining the same weights.
pitfalls: Every pixel is assigned using the original sites, so one call is not an implicit convergence loop.
The output preserves one entry per input site even when a site receives no mass.

operations.description: Draw positions from caller-supplied integer raster density with explicit deterministic random state.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed carrier, dimensions, weights, sites or scalar domain.
errors.WORK_LIMIT: Specified deterministic event count exceeds maxWork or safe-integer work.

behavior.validation: Exact required own string keys on passive ordinary/null-prototype records; dense ordinary arrays with own data slots only, no extras, symbols, accessors or coercion. Proxies outside interchange. Validate all fields in schema order, every weight/site, and dimensions before budget; width*height<=2147483647 and equals weights.length. Arrays/count<=2147483647. All scalars finite. No partial result or input mutation/retention. Canonicalize exposed -0. Host allocation failures remain host errors.
behavior.environment: Raster row-major: flat index=row*width+column, pixel area [column,column+1]x[row,row+1], center (column+0.5,row+0.5), x right/y down. Weight is dimensionless relative mass, zero has none. No asset, renderer, luminance conversion, clock or host RNG; caller supplies weights.
behavior.native_surface: weightedRasterPoints2D(input), WeightedRasterPoints2DError with stable code. First target p5.js package; other targets deferred.
behavior.order: After all validation, sum integer mass exactly (at most 140735340806145); zero total or count=0 returns empty arrays and unchanged rngState after paying P work. Otherwise build cumulative integer weights in row-major order. For each output: advance LCG32 twice high word then low word, U=high*2^32+low; q=floor(U*totalMass/2^64) using exact integer product. Find first prefix>q using lo=0,hi=P, while lo<hi: mid=floor((lo+hi)/2); prefix[mid]>q sets hi=mid, else lo=mid+1. Select index lo. Advance LCG twice ux then uy; x=column+(ux+0.5)/2^32, y=row+(uy+0.5)/2^32. Append point and index in draw order; sampling with replacement. There is no rejection loop.
behavior.rng: LCG32 version1: advanced state=(1664525*state+1013904223) modulo2^32, each draw returns new unsigned word. Exactly4 draws per output, no ambient state; return final state. Consecutive words are correlated; no claim of statistical unbiasedness, independence or blue-noise quality.
behavior.work: P=width*height. After validation require P+4*count<=maxWork when mass>0, else P<=maxWork, with exact integer arithmetic. Total charge P+4 per produced point+one per actual binary-search comparison. Charge each comparison before performing it; WORK_LIMIT if budget exceeded. All output is local and discarded on failure, so input rngState is unchanged. Time O(P+count*log P), storage O(P+count).
behavior.numerics: All mass/prefix/product/ticket arithmetic exact integer; U is uint64, product up to111 bits. Jitter expression as specified binary64 is exact under dimension cap, strictly inside pixel. No tolerance for points, indices, RNG or error codes.

guide.title: Place marks from image mass
guide.summary: Turn a caller-prepared weight raster into replayable, jittered mark positions.
guide.useWhen: You have one nonnegative integer mass per pixel and want denser marks where that mass is larger.

inputs.width: Raster width in pixels; x increases right and the flat array is row-major.
inputs.height: Raster height in pixels; y increases down.
inputs.weights: One nonnegative integer mass per pixel. Zero mass excludes that pixel from selection.
inputs.count: Number of positions to draw with replacement; several may land in one pixel.
inputs.rngState: Explicit unsigned 32-bit LCG state. Pass the returned state into the next call to continue the stream.
inputs.maxWork: Explicit work cap: pixel scan, four draws per emitted mark and charged search comparisons.

guide.output: {points,pixelIndices,rngState}: detached jittered positions, source pixel indices in draw order and the advanced RNG state.
guide.code:
const result = weightedRasterPoints2D({width:3,height:2,weights:[0,2,5,1,0,3],count:4,rngState:42,maxWork:100});
console.log(result.pixelIndices, result.points, result.rngState);
guide.tryThis: Swap in a second image-derived mass raster while keeping count and rngState fixed; then switch dots to stitches without resampling.
pitfalls: Prepare the mass raster yourself; this operation does not choose luminance, handle alpha or render marks.
The supplied LCG stream is deterministic, but sampled marks have no minimum spacing.
